## Pre-registration: PAPER1, forward paper tracking of three candidates (written 2026-10-20 before any paper entry exists)

**What it is.** A keyless scheduled function (`kalshiPaperTick`) reads public open markets and records what L1's rule WOULD have bought, one contract, no money, and later the public result. It places nothing, signs nothing, holds no key, makes no `/portfolio` call and no POST. Its records are never shown next to the live record.

**Why paper, and why these three.** The owner wants more short-term strategies and markets. The 2026-10-20 census of Kalshi's short-term series found the liquid, repeating markets already covered; what is left is thin or only now trading. Forward paper entries are the only way to add days for a candidate that cannot be tested on history (AUDUSD and USDCAD have 12 days of it) and to read a near miss on days it was not selected on (natural gas). Three candidates, fixed now, no others:
1. **KXAUDUSD15M**, never tested (12 days of history, median volume about 1,600 contracts a market).
2. **KXUSDCAD15M**, never tested (the same).
3. **KXNATGAS15M**, tested in E5 on discovery and holdout and not shown (closest of the commodities, +1.4c, z 1.9); this is a forward read of a near miss, so it counts as a try.

**Rule (identical to L1).** Every minute inside the L1 window (330 to 400 s before the close) for each candidate's open markets: buy the favourite when its ask (YES) or one minus its bid (NO) is 0.88 to 0.97, one contract, taker at that price, fee 7% x p x (1 - p) per contract (the research's `scalps.fee`, NOT `kalshiSignalLib.takerFee`: that rounds up to a cent per order, which at one contract would charge about 1c where the research charges about 0.5c, and would bias every paper result down; corrected on 2026-10-20 while building, before any entry existed), hold to settlement. One entry per market (a deterministic document id, so two processes cannot record it twice). Nothing reads a result to decide an entry.

**Counterparty.** The same as L1's and no new one is claimed: retail buying the cheap side of a near-certain short-dated market. For the FX pairs there is no earlier evidence that this holds.

**Pass bar for promotion to a real-money slot, fixed now.** One read per candidate, on or after **2026-11-30** (about 40 days of entries), at least **300** paper entries and at least **10** days; mean net above zero; day clustered z at least **2.1**; both halves of the days positive; positive with fees x1.2; and then still only a candidate for a small capped slot with its own loss stop that cannot hold a position at the same time as L1's (see CLAUDE.md, "L1 is the only strategy"). A candidate that does not reach 300 entries by 2026-12-31 reads `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`, never a pass or a fail. The read is run **once**; if the data are not enough it is repeated only after the minimum is met, never to chase a pass.

**Numeric prediction, before the first entry.** AUDUSD and USDCAD: net about +0.3c per entry, z under 1.5 at 40 days, **FALSIFIED or NOT_ENOUGH_DATA** (FX 15 minute markets are thin and the three FX pairs already tested were negative: -0.6c to -4.3c in the earlier FX check). Natural gas: about +0.5c, z under 1.5, FALSIFIED. Minimum detectable edge at 300 entries is about +1.0c, so a true +0.5c edge cannot be seen.

**Kill criterion.** Any bar condition failing is FALSIFIED. The paper record has nothing to say about slippage on a real order at size; a pass is only permission to consider a small live slot.

**Count.** Three tries: the running total in this file was about 4,625 after TP1, so it is about 4,628.

## Information: the research data is archived (2026-10-20, not a try)

The databases under `kalshi-scalper/data/` are gitignored and lived only in the cloud research container, and Kalshi's history reaches back about 69 days, so the early August days (the L1 holdout `l1b`, the E3B and E5 holdouts) would have been unrecoverable once the container ended or mid-September passed. They are now on the branch **`research-data`** of `shwoopnet/shwoopnet`: 14 databases and one price-file archive, 44 MB compressed, with `MANIFEST.md` (size, coverage, checksum per file) and `restore.sh` (decompresses into `kalshi-scalper/data/`; tested: `l1b` restores with its 7,213 markets and passes SQLite's integrity check; `book` and `e3b` were integrity-checked too). Public Kalshi market data and public price files only; no keys, balances or account data. The branch is not published by Pages (it is not the default branch) but it is readable by anyone who can read the repository, and a full clone now downloads about 44 MB more. The archive is a snapshot of 2026-10-20: forward days after it (for example the 2026-11-16 reads) come from fresh downloads, and a second snapshot should be taken before about 2026-12-01 so the early days are never the only copy.

## Information: a census of Kalshi's 340 daily series (2026-10-20, counts and volumes only, not a try)

The follow-up to the short-term census above: every daily series was asked for its settled markets in the last 69 days. Nothing was priced or tested.

**What trades.** 143 of the 340 daily series had a settled market in the window; 197 are listed and idle. Total contracts traded by category: weather 165 million (51 series), economics 61 million (56), commodities 22 million (6), politics 15 million (5), sports 9 million (1), financials 5 million (19), crypto 1 million (2), entertainment and science almost nothing.

**Weather is where the volume is, and it is already crossed off.** The seven daily-high cities tested in WX1 (Los Angeles, Miami, New York, Chicago, Austin, Denver, Philadelphia) are the seven most liquid (median 5,600 to 73,800 contracts a market). The untested ones are the same mechanism in other cities: San Francisco, Phoenix, Seattle, Dallas, Atlanta, Houston, Las Vegas, Oklahoma City, Boston, Minneapolis, Washington DC and New Orleans highs (median 2,100 to 8,200), plus daily lows. By this file's own rule a new city is a rewording of a crossed-off mechanism, not a new one: WX1 found the market beats the public forecast (-3.3c, z -2.5), FLB1 found long-dated favourites lose (-0.6c to -1.8c), and the one new angle, late-day certainty, is closed by availability (WX2: by 6 hours before the close no quoted bucket is left inside 80c to 98c).

The approval, gas price and generic ballot markets are driven by a published number (a poll average, AAA's daily price), so any edge would have to come from reading that number before the market does, which is a different test from L1's and has to be registered with its own source and timing before any price is downloaded. Nothing here is a candidate for money. The only candidates worth a registered paper track are the ones with a public daily source and enough strikes a day to reach 300 entries in a month or two: the gas price series first.

## Pre-registration: GAS1, APP1 and CMD1, daily ladders on a published number or a spot price (written 2026-10-21 before any of the three rules was computed)

**Why now.** The owner asked (2026-10-21) for three strategies on markets other than L1's, tested on history in one sitting instead of weeks of paper, and said any that look good go to a small live slot. The speed comes from the settled markets themselves: each daily ladder's `expiration_value` is the published number, so the AAA gas price, the RCP approval average and the commodity settlement prices can be rebuilt for every past day and a walk-forward model scored against the quote the market actually showed. **The bar is not lowered for the speed**: it is the single-try bar of WX1 with a Bonferroni step for three tries.

**Disclosed before registering.** I downloaded the settled markets and read their structure and a handful of values (gas 2026-10-20 4.2786 and 2026-08-14 4.0776; approval 38.8 and 39.6; Brent 105.39 and 91.08), the same for the open gas ladder on 2026-10-20 (17 strikes, the market already inside one strike of 4.26 to 4.265). No model was fitted and no rule was run. The data are in `data/pub1.sqlite` (`scalper/pub1.py fetch`).

**Counts as three tries, two mechanisms.** GAS1 and APP1 are one mechanism (a slow published number, forecast from its own recent path, against a ladder priced by people reading headlines) on two series. CMD1 is H7's mechanism (distance to the strike, scaled by volatility and time left) on a new universe: thin commodity daily ladders instead of Bitcoin. Under this file's own rule CMD1 is closer to a reword than to something new; it is registered because H7 was falsified where the market is most efficient (Bitcoin) and these ladders trade at 1,000 to 8,000 contracts a market.

**Machinery common to all three (copied from WX1: `wx1.pick_trade`, `calibration.cluster_mean_z`, `scalps.fee`, `scalps.STRESS`).**
- Unit: a market-day (one close). Walk-forward: a day's model uses only values published strictly before its DECISION time.
- The decision is made DECISION_LEFT seconds before the close; the entry is the quote at the END of the NEXT hourly candle (ENTRY_LEFT seconds before the close), strictly later than every input. Entry price is that candle's ask (YES) or one minus its bid (NO), taker, one contract, hold to settlement, fee 7% x p x (1 - p) (the research's `scalps.fee`). A quote is usable if bid is at least 0.01, ask at most 0.99 and ask at least bid.
- Trade: per market, the side with the larger (model probability minus price minus fee), taken if that is at least EDGE = 0.03 and the price is inside 0.05 to 0.95. At most one entry per market. Nothing reads a result to decide an entry.
- **Pass bar, per strategy, one run each:** at least 100 entries on at least 25 days; mean net per contract above zero; day-clustered z at least **2.4** (2.1 with a step for three tries); positive in both halves of the days; positive with fees x1.2; and above the 95th percentile of 200 fair-market placebo draws (outcomes drawn as Bernoulli at each entry's mid price). Fewer than 100 entries or 25 days reads `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`; anything else short of the bar is `FALSIFIED`; a pass is `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` and means "permission to consider a small capped live slot with its own stop", never evidence of an edge. The minimum detectable edge (2.4 standard errors) is printed with every result; where it is above 3c a FALSIFIED reads "not shown at this sample size".
- Information only, not tries: Brier score of the model against the market's mid on every scored bucket; entries and net by side; threshold sensitivity (EDGE 0, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05); per series for CMD1.

**GAS1: the AAA national average gas price ladder (`KXAAAGASD`).**
- Markets: the "greater than strike" markets; they close 23:59 US Eastern the evening before the price they settle on, so the price is not yet published when the market is trading. DECISION_LEFT 8 hours, ENTRY_LEFT 7 hours.
- Known at the decision: the AAA values of earlier days (the `expiration_value` of earlier events). A day is scored only if the previous event closed 24 hours earlier (plus or minus 1 hour) and at least 21 earlier consecutive daily values exist.
- Model: V_prev is the previous day's value; the forecast change is the mean of the last 3 daily changes; sigma is the population standard deviation of the forecast errors (each day's change minus the mean of the 3 changes before it) over the last 20 days, never below 0.0010 (a tenth of a cent). P(price > strike) = 1 - Phi((strike - (V_prev + forecast change)) / sigma). Nothing else is fitted.
- **Counterparty.** The people holding the cheap side of a strike near the boundary. AAA's published average moves by a few tenths of a cent a day and by momentum, so on a clear-trend day the market's tail strikes are too expensive; the model sells those tails (buys the favourite side). The model is blind to a turning point and to the futures market, which is the realistic way it loses.
- **Prediction, before the run.** Net per contract between -1.5c and +0.8c, z below 1.5, **FALSIFIED** (my probability about 65%). The market already shows the price inside one strike on the day I looked, so a persistence model starts no better than the market.
- **Kill criterion.** Any bar condition failing. Also: model Brier above the market's Brier with fewer than 100 entries counts as no evidence either way.

**APP1: Trump's RCP approval average ladder (`KXTRUMPAPPROVE`).**
- Markets: all three types (below, exactly, above), the value taken to one decimal as the market's own wording says (`E39.2` is 39.2). Continuous ranges on the 0.1 grid: "below c" is under c - 0.05; "exactly x" is x - 0.05 up to x + 0.05; "above f" is over f + 0.05. They close at 1:00 PM US Eastern on the day. DECISION_LEFT 20 hours, ENTRY_LEFT 19 hours (the evening before). A day is scored only if the previous event closed 24 hours earlier (plus or minus 1 hour) and 21 earlier consecutive values exist.
- Model: mu = V_prev (no drift); sigma = the population standard deviation of the last 20 daily changes, never below 0.15. Normal. Nothing else is fitted.
- **Counterparty.** Retail reacting to the day's political news; the RCP average is a slow smoother of many polls and moves by 0.0 to 0.3 on most days, so strikes more than a step away are priced too wide. The model is blind to a poll entering or leaving the average overnight and to the live RCP number the market can see, which is the realistic way it loses: the market has the number at 5 PM and the model only has yesterday's.
- **Prediction.** Net between -2.5c and 0c, z below 1, **FALSIFIED** (about 75%): the market can see the live average and the model cannot.
- **Kill criterion.** As the common bar.

**CMD1: commodity daily ladders priced from the spot price (`KXBRENTD`, `KXWTI`, `KXGOLDD`, `KXSILVERD`, `KXNATGASD`, `KXCOPPERD`; Yahoo front-month futures `BZ=F`, `CL=F`, `GC=F`, `SI=F`, `NG=F`, `HG=F` as the spot proxy).**
- Markets: "greater" and "less" strikes (a "between" market is not scored). DECISION_LEFT 3 hours, ENTRY_LEFT 2 hours. Pooled across the six series (one verdict); per series is information.
- Spot at the decision: the last 5 minute bar that ended at or before the decision time. Vol: the standard deviation of the 5 minute log returns of the prior 2,000 bars (about 7 trading days) with no return spanning a gap over 15 minutes. n = the number of 5 minute steps from that bar's end to the close.
- Basis: the proxy is not the settlement source. basis = median over the last 10 settled days of (the settled value minus the proxy's close at that day's close time), needing at least 5; the centre of the distribution is spot + basis. A series with fewer than 5 such days is not scored that day.
- Model: P(price > K) = 1 - Phi( ln(K / (spot + basis)) / (vol x sqrt(n)) ). Nothing else is fitted.
- **Counterparty.** Retail pricing a strike by the last price it saw and a round-number feel, not by volatility or the time left. H7's story, with the same blind spot: informed traders in the final hours, which is why the decision is 3 hours out and not 30 minutes.
- **Prediction.** Net between -1.5c and +1.0c, z below 1.5, **FALSIFIED** (about 60%; this is the one of the three with the most entries, so it is the one most likely to tell the truth either way).
- **Kill criterion.** As the common bar, pooled.

**If one passes.** The owner's instruction of 2026-10-21 is that a strategy that passes goes to a small live slot. That slot is a separate, reviewed change and must show how it cannot hold a position at the same time as L1 (its own series, its own cash limit and its own loss stop; CLAUDE.md, "L1 is the only strategy"). A paper tracker for it is built first or alongside, so its forward days accumulate from the first day.

**Single read.** Each of GAS1, APP1 and CMD1 is run once, on the data downloaded above; a fix to the code that is not a change to a rule or a number above (a parse error, a crash) is made and logged, and the run repeated only for that reason. **Running count of tries on Kalshi: about 4,631 with these three.**

## Results: GAS1, APP1 and CMD1, one run each (2026-10-21; the rules, bars and predictions are those registered above; nothing was changed after seeing them)

Code: `scalper/pub1.py`, committed before any run. Result files: `data/pub1_result_GAS1.txt`, `..._APP1.txt`, `..._CMD1.txt` (a second run is refused unless the file is deleted).

| | Entries | Days | Net per contract | Day clustered z | Halves | Fees x1.2 | Placebo 95th pct | Brier model vs market | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GAS1, AAA gas price ladder | 184 | 47 | **-7.50c** | -2.27 | -4.59c / -11.63c | -7.70c | +2.28c | 0.2351 vs **0.0826** | **FALSIFIED** |
| APP1, RCP approval ladder | 97 | 27 | not computed (below the 100 entry and 25 day minimum) | | | | | 0.0926 vs **0.0746** | **NOT_ENOUGH_DATA** |
| CMD1, six commodity daily ladders, pooled | 1,054 | 42 | **-7.28c** | **-4.31** | -7.60c / -7.00c | -7.48c | -0.93c | 0.2115 vs **0.0789** | **FALSIFIED** |

**Predictions against results.** GAS1 predicted -1.5c to +0.8c and FALSIFIED: the verdict was right and the loss is five times larger than the range I gave. APP1 predicted FALSIFIED and got NOT_ENOUGH_DATA (97 entries against a minimum of 100): the verdict word was wrong by three entries, and its model is still sharper than nothing but worse than the market on Brier. CMD1 predicted -1.5c to +1.0c and FALSIFIED: right on the word, wrong on the size (-7.3c, z -4.3). In every case the market's own probability scored far better than the model's (Brier about a third to a half), which is the plain reading: **the market in each of these ladders is better informed than a persistence or a spot-distance model, and trading against it costs about 7c a contract.** Recorded as it was.

**Information, not a try: is CMD1's miss a coding error or a result?** The standard deviation of the standardised error (settled value against the model's centre, divided by its own predicted spread; 1.00 means the volatility rule is right): gold 1.02, silver 0.95, WTI 1.43, copper 1.50, Brent 2.03, natural gas 3.79. Gold and silver are calibrated and still lost (-7.1c and -0.2c), so the market is simply sharper there. Brent and natural gas are not calibrated: the Yahoo front-month contract is not the contract Kalshi settles on, and a 10-day median basis does not absorb that, so those two series are mis-measured by the proxy and are not a fair read of the idea. They are **not** re-run (a changed rule is a new try, and the pooled verdict is far outside the bar either way, z -4.3 with gold and silver alone negative).

**What the three results do and do not say.** They say a persistence or a distance-from-spot rule does not beat these ladders on this history, and that the cost of being wrong is large (7c a contract against about a 3c edge threshold). They do not say a published-number edge cannot exist: the one lead left is APP1 at 97 entries (Brier worse than the market's, so I do not expect it), and a model with a better input than yesterday's value (the futures curve for gas) was not tested.

**Decision.** Nothing built, nothing changed live. **Count: about 4,631 tries on Kalshi.** APP1 reads NOT_ENOUGH_DATA, so by its own registration it is repeated only after the minimum is met, on days it has not seen.

## Pre-registration: PERP1, a daily trend breakout on four liquid perpetual markets (written 2026-10-21 before any return was computed)

**Why.** The owner likes leverage in Kalshi's perpetual futures (bigger gains on small moves, less capital tied up) and asked whether a perps strategy is worth pursuing (`docs/PERPS_THEORY.md`, `docs/PERPS_STRATEGY_GUIDE.md`). Kalshi's perps API has no historical data, but a slow daily-bar idea can be tested on years of public daily prices of the same underlyings with Kalshi's fees applied. This is the first and simplest idea in the guide. My odds that it passes are about 10 to 15%.

**Disclosed before registering.** I downloaded the daily bars (Yahoo chart, `interval=1d`) and read only their counts and date ranges: gold `GC=F` 2010-01-04 on (4,226 bars), the S&P 500 `^GSPC` 2010-01-04 on (4,225), Bitcoin `BTC-USD` 2014-09-17 on (4,418), Ethereum `ETH-USD` 2017-11-09 on (3,269). No signal, trade or return has been computed.

**Proxies, and why they can only mislead one way or the other.** `GC=F` is the continuous front-month gold future (roll gaps; Kalshi's `KXGOLDPERP` tracks spot gold); `^GSPC` is the index, which does not trade overnight or at weekends (Kalshi's `KXUS500PERP` tracks the MerQube US Large Cap Index around the clock); Bitcoin and Ethereum are 24/7 daily bars closing at 00:00 UTC. These are proxies, not the instruments.

**Rule (fixed now; one run).** Daily bars per market; all signals use only data through the signal day's close; every fill is on a LATER bar.
- **Entry.** Long when the day's close is above the highest close of the previous 20 days; short when it is below the lowest close of the previous 20 days. Filled at the NEXT day's open. One position per market, no adding, no re-entry until a fresh signal.
- **Stop.** Fixed at entry open minus (long) or plus (short) 1.5 times ATR(14), where ATR is the simple mean of the last 14 true ranges ending on the signal day. Checked every day from the entry day: a long is stopped when the day's low is at or below the stop and exits at the stop, or at the open if the day opens beyond it; shorts mirror with the high.
- **Exit.** At the close of any day after entry, a long whose close is below the lowest close of the previous 10 days (a short: above the highest of the previous 10) exits at the NEXT day's open. If the same close also gives a 20-day breakout the other way, that opposite position opens at the same next open.
- **Costs.** Taker fee 0.12% a side (0.24% a round trip, from CFTC filing summaries, unconfirmed against Kalshi's fee page), slippage 0.01% a side, and a funding charge assumed AGAINST the position at 0.02% of notional per calendar day held (the real funding rate is unmeasured; this is a deliberately harsh placeholder). Net return per trade on notional r = side x (exit / entry - 1) - 0.0026 - 0.0002 x days held.
- **Unit and statistic.** One trade. The statistic is mean net r per trade on notional, pooled over the four markets, with the standard error clustered by calendar month of entry (`calibration.cluster_mean_z`), because Bitcoin and Ethereum trend together.
- **Leverage, for information only:** equity return = min(3, 0.02 / stop distance as a fraction of entry) x r, i.e. 2% risked per trade and leverage capped at 3x.

**Pass bar, fixed (one try, so the single-try bar).** At least **100 trades** across at least **4 calendar years**; mean net r above zero; day-clustered (month-clustered) z of at least **2.1**; positive in both halves (trades split at the median entry date); positive with fees, slippage and funding all x1.2; and above the 95th percentile of **200 placebo draws** (the same trades' sides and holding lengths with each entry date moved uniformly at random within its market's history, no stops, same costs). Otherwise `FALSIFIED`; fewer than 100 trades or 4 years reads `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`; a pass is `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` and means permission to consider a one-contract-scale live probe on a small separate balance, never evidence of an edge. The minimum detectable edge is printed with the result.

**Information only, not tries:** trades, mean r, win rate and stop-hit share per market; mean r per calendar year; buy-and-hold return of each market over its sample; equity-return mean at the stated leverage rule.

**Counterparty story.** Slow money that acts late on a persistent move, and holders who sell into a trend too early. The blind spot: markets with no persistence, where the rule is stopped out repeatedly and pays 0.26% plus funding each time.

**Numeric prediction, before the run.** Pooled mean net r per trade between **-0.4% and +0.5%**, z below 1.5, **`FALSIFIED`** (my probability about 85%). The cost placeholder of 0.26% plus 0.02% a day is large against a typical trade, and our own record on trend strategies (the withdrawn Alpaca figures) says the edge was thin before costs.

**Kill criterion.** Any condition of the bar failing. A pass on the pooled set that holds in only one market is reported as exactly that.

**Count.** One try: about **4,632** on Kalshi-related ideas. Single run: `python -m scalper.perp1 fetch` then `python -m scalper.perp1 run`; a second run is refused unless the result file is deleted on purpose (a crash fix only).

## Result: PERP1, one run, read once (2026-10-21; the rule, bar and prediction are those registered above; nothing was changed after seeing them)

Code `scalper/perp1.py` and `tests/test_perp1.py`, committed before the run. Result file `data/perp1_result.txt`.

**Registered verdict: `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED`.** 745 trades on four markets over 17 years: mean net **+1.40% per trade on notional**, month-clustered z **+2.76**, halves +1.94% and +0.86%, positive with costs x1.2 (+1.28%), above the placebo 95th percentile (+0.46%). Minimum detectable edge +1.06%.

**My prediction was wrong.** I said -0.4% to +0.5% a trade, z under 1.5, `FALSIFIED` (about 85%). The pooled result is nearly three times the top of that range. Recorded as it was.

**What is under the pooled number (information; each of these cuts was made after seeing the result, so none is a try and none is evidence):**

| Cut | Trades | Mean net | z |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bitcoin and Ethereum, all years | 323 | **+4.09%** | +3.44 |
| Gold and S&P 500, all years | 422 | **-0.66%** | **-4.87** |
| Entries from 2022 on, all markets | 287 | **0.00%** | -0.01 |
| Entries from 2022 on, Bitcoin and Ethereum | 168 | +0.46% | +0.40 |
| Entries from 2022 on, gold and S&P 500 | 119 | -0.66% | -2.70 |
| Longs | 389 | +3.26% | +3.83 |
| Shorts | 356 | -0.63% | -1.20 |
| All trades except the 10 best | 735 | +0.35% | +0.99 |

By market: gold -0.65% (206 trades), S&P 500 -0.66% (216), Bitcoin +3.55% (186), Ethereum +4.82% (137). By year of entry: 2017 +7.6%, 2018 +3.1%, 2019 +2.9%, **2020 +7.7%**, 2021 +1.4%, then 2022 -0.4%, 2023 +0.4%, 2024 +0.2%, 2025 -0.3%, 2026 +0.1%. The ten best trades (+46% to +129% on notional each) are all Bitcoin or Ethereum, eight of them from 2017 to 2021.

**Honest reading.**
- The pass is real as registered, and it is a pass of "long Bitcoin and Ethereum through their enormous early run" (buy and hold on those two returned +18,149% and +669% over their samples), carried by a handful of very large winners. Without the 10 best trades the z is 1.0.
- **Gold and the S&P 500 lose at every cut** (z -4.9 pooled), so a daily trend rule on the two markets without crypto's drift is worse than nothing after costs.
- **The edge is not visible in the last five years:** 287 trades from 2022 on average 0.00% (z -0.01). This is the same shape as the "window series" finding for the earlier strategies (an edge that lives in the early, flattering window).
- The pass therefore says "a simple rule rode a historic bull market", not "there is a perps trend edge today". Permission to consider a probe is not a reason to build one.
- The funding charge (0.02% a day) is a placeholder; the real rate is unmeasured. Long positions in a strong uptrend usually PAY funding, so the pass is not flattered by it, but the sign and size are unknown.

**Decision.** Nothing built, nothing changed live. A follow-up (crypto only, or from 2022 on) would be a new try, registered first and run once; because it would be chosen after seeing these cuts, it would need a stricter bar and ideally days that do not exist yet (a forward record). **Count: about 4,632 tries.**

## Pre-registration: PERP2 (buy the dip in an uptrend) and PERP3 (gold against silver), written 2026-10-21 before either was computed

**Why.** PERP1 passed as registered but only because of Bitcoin's and Ethereum's early years (flat since 2022; gold and the S&P lost at every cut). The owner chose to try a different perps idea first. These are the guide's ideas B and C (`docs/PERPS_STRATEGY_GUIDE.md`). Each is run once on the same daily prices as PERP1 plus daily silver (`SI=F`, from 2010-01-04); the bars, costs and placebo method are PERP1's (`scalper/perp1.py`), so nothing about the market data or the fee model is new. **Two more tries; the z bar is raised from 2.1 to 2.4 for each** (a step for the tries made together).

**Disclosed before registering.** PERP1's full result and its cuts (gold and the S&P lose, crypto carried it, flat since 2022) were seen first. Both ideas were written in the guide before PERP1 ran and are not shaped by its cuts, except that PERP2 is registered on all four markets and PERP3 on gold and silver only. No silver bar has been downloaded or read; no PERP2 or PERP3 signal, trade or return has been computed.

**PERP2: buy the dip in an uptrend (long only; gold, S&P 500, Bitcoin and Ethereum, as PERP1).**
- **Signal at a day's close:** the close is above its 100-day simple average (including that day), AND the last three closes each fell (close < previous close, three days running).
- **Entry:** at the NEXT day's open, long. One position per market; a fresh signal is needed after any exit.
- **Stop:** entry open minus 2.0 x ATR(14) (ATR from the signal day, as PERP1), fills intrabar or at the open if the day gaps through it.
- **Exit:** at the close of any day from the entry day on, if the close is above the highest close of the previous 5 days, exit at the NEXT open; also exit at the NEXT open once 20 daily bars have been held.
- **Costs:** PERP1's: 0.12% a side fee, 0.01% a side slippage, funding 0.02% of notional per calendar day held, charged against the position.
- **Counterparty.** Panic sellers after a short drop within a rising market. The blind spot: a trend that is actually breaking, where the dip is the first leg of a larger fall.
- **Prediction.** Pooled mean net per trade between **-0.3% and +0.4%**, **`FALSIFIED`** (about 80%). Crypto's drift will flatter it, which is what the placebo is for.

**PERP3: gold against silver (a pairs trade; two legs of equal dollars; gold `GC=F` and silver `SI=F` daily bars, dates present in both).**
- **Ratio** R = gold close / silver close. At day i (59 days of history needed), z = (R_i minus the mean of R over days i-59 to i) / the population standard deviation of R over the same days.
- **Signal at the close:** z above +2.0 -> short gold / long silver; z below -2.0 -> long gold / short silver. Filled at the NEXT day's open on both legs. One position at a time.
- **Exit at the NEXT open** after the first close where z has crossed back through zero (a short-gold position exits when z is at or below 0; long-gold when at or above 0), or where |z| is at least 4.0 (the stop: the spread kept running), or after 30 daily bars held.
- **Return per trade** r = side x (gold exit/entry - 1 - (silver exit/entry - 1)) - 2 x cost(days), with side +1 = long gold / short silver, per $1 of EACH leg, where cost(days) is PERP1's single-leg cost; so both legs pay fees, slippage and the funding assumption.
- **Counterparty.** Whoever must rebalance between the two metals (index and fund flows, industrial buyers). The blind spot: the ratio shifting for months, which the |z| = 4 stop is for.
- **Prediction.** Mean net **-0.3% to +0.3%**, **`NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` or `FALSIFIED`** (about 90%).

**Pass bar, per idea, one run each (PERP1's, with the z step).** PERP2: at least **100 trades** and **4 calendar years**; PERP3: at least **40 trades** and **4 calendar years** (a pairs trade is rare; fewer reads `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`, never a pass or a fail). Mean net r above zero; month-clustered z at least **2.4**; positive in both halves (trades split at the median entry date); positive with all costs x1.2; and above the 95th percentile of **200 placebo draws** (same side and holding length, entry date moved uniformly at random within the market's history; no stops; PERP3 moves both legs together). Otherwise `FALSIFIED`. A pass means "permission to consider a small probe" and nothing more.

**Information only, not tries:** per market, per calendar year, win rate and stop share; for PERP2 the buy-and-hold of each market; for PERP3 long-gold and short-gold sides separately.

**Single read.** `python -m scalper.perp2 fetch` then `python -m scalper.perp2 run`, once each; a second run is refused unless the result file is deleted on purpose (a crash fix only). **Running count: about 4,634 tries.**

## Results: PERP2 and PERP3, one run each (2026-10-21; the rules, bars and predictions are those registered above; nothing was changed after seeing them)

Code `scalper/perp2.py`, `tests/test_perp2.py`, committed before the runs; result files `data/perp2_result_PERP2.txt` and `..._PERP3.txt`. **One crash fix, logged:** the first PERP3 run crashed in the placebo (a tuple unpacked as 2 values when the rows carry 3: `(g0, s0, date)`) before it wrote a result file, so no PERP3 number had been seen; the one line was fixed and the run repeated. No rule, number or threshold changed.

| | Trades | Mean net per trade | Month-clustered z | Halves | Costs x1.2 | Placebo 95th pct | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PERP2, buy the dip in an uptrend | 393 over 17 years | +0.32% | +1.31 | +0.13% / +0.51% | +0.25% | +0.56% | **FALSIFIED** |
| PERP3, gold against silver | 84 over 17 years | **-1.67%** | **-2.07** | -0.87% / -2.47% | -2.05% | -0.46% | **FALSIFIED** |

**Predictions against results.** PERP2 predicted -0.3% to +0.4%, `FALSIFIED` (about 80%): right on the word, and the mean (+0.32%) landed inside the range. PERP3 predicted -0.3% to +0.3%, `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` or `FALSIFIED`: right on the word, but the loss (-1.67%) is about five times the range's edge.

**PERP2, information.** Every market is slightly positive (Bitcoin +0.84%, gold +0.19%, Ethereum +0.15%, S&P 500 +0.11%) with a 62% to 69% win rate and about a 5 to 7 day hold, but the pooled edge (+0.32%) does not clear the placebo (+0.56%): random long entries held the same lengths did as well, which means the result is the markets' upward drift, not the dip signal. By year it swings from -2.9% (2022) to +2.6% (2020).

**PERP3, information.** Average hold about 35 days (most trades ran into the 30 bar time stop, so the ratio did not come back quickly); only 4% hit the |z| 4 stop; long gold -2.12%, short gold -1.33%. Costs were about 1.9% a trade, of which the funding placeholder (0.02% a day on EACH leg, charged against both) is about 1.4%, so the gross edge was about +0.2% before costs. **The funding assumption is the harshest part of the registration for a pair**: the two legs are opposite sides, so in reality part of the funding offsets. That is a fact about the registered cost model, not a reason to overturn the verdict; a corrected cost model would be a new try.

**What this adds to PERP1.** Three simple daily ideas on the public histories of the four underlyings: one passed only through crypto's early years (PERP1), one is the markets' drift (PERP2), and one is eaten by funding (PERP3). The common finding is again that cost and drift, not signal, decide these. **Decision.** Nothing built, nothing changed live. **Count: about 4,634 tries.**

## Information: PERP3's arithmetic under other cost models (2026-10-21, no hypothesis, no verdict, no variant counted)

The owner asked to try gold against silver again with a fairer funding model. Before registering a new try, the arithmetic on the SAME 84 PERP3 trades (already seen, so this is not evidence of anything):
- Mean gross return per trade (before any cost): **+0.237%**; average hold 34.6 days; 60% of trades positive before costs.
- Fixed round-trip cost of two legs: **0.52%** at the 0.12% taker fee plus 1bp slippage a side; **0.24%** at a 5bp maker fee.
- Mean net for funding per leg per day of 0.00% / 0.01% / 0.02%: taker **-0.28% / -0.98% / -1.67%**; maker **-0.00% / -0.70% / -1.39%**.

**So no funding model, however generous, makes the taker version positive** (it is -0.28% with zero funding), and only a zero-funding, all-maker version reaches break-even. A new registered try would be decided by the arithmetic above before it ran; it was therefore **not registered** (running it would spend a try, and raise the deflation floor for everything after it, on a result already known). Real funding rates and real maker fills would change this only if a recorder measured them; that is the recorder's job, not a backtest's.

## Pre-registration: TREE1 (a small decision tree that skips L1 entries) and PAT1 (nearest-pattern matching that skips L1 entries), written 2026-10-21 before any feature, tree or neighbour was computed

**Why.** The owner asked for "pattern recognition and decision trees". Both are filters on L1's own entries, not new lanes: they only ever say "skip this one", so they cannot hold a position at the same time as L1 and need no new live code path beyond a skip rule. L1's record on this data is thin and lumpy (about 6.5% of entries lose, and a loss costs about 15 times a win), so the only way a learner can help is by finding the losers in advance. **Two more tries; the z bar is raised from 2.4 to 2.5 for each.** Running count after this registration: about **4,636**.

**Disclosed before registering.** The earlier filters (Q1 to Q3, VOL1, PM2, PM3 and the distance rules) were read and mostly failed; the base L1 numbers on `book.sqlite` (n = 3,038 entries, 196 losses, +0.41c mean net) were printed once to size this test and nothing else was computed. No feature value, split or neighbour has been looked at.

**Population.** `scalper.lstrats.hold_rule` with `L1` on `data/book.sqlite` (Bitcoin, Ethereum, gold; 41 UTC days from 2026-09-02): one row per market, entry at the candle that ends 360 s before the close, ask 0.88 to 0.97, as already coded. Costs and the x1.2 stress are those of the other L1 tests.

**Features (TREE1; every one uses only candles that END at or before the decision candle, so nothing later than the entry can reach a feature).** Computed on the bought side (NO values are 1 minus the YES values):
1. `price`: the entry price. 2. `spread`: ask minus bid of the bought side at the decision candle. 3. `d1`, 4. `d3`, 5. `d5`: the bought side's mid now minus its mid 1, 3 and 5 candles earlier (missing candles: the row is excluded from the tree and counted, never filled). 6. `rng5`: highest minus lowest mid over the last 6 candles. 7. `dip`: the lowest mid of the bought side over all earlier candles of the market (how far it was ever doubted). 8. `hi_gap`: the decision candle's bid high minus its bid close. 9. `hour`: UTC hour. 10. `dow`: day of week. 11 to 13: three flags for the series (Bitcoin, Ethereum, gold).

**TREE1 rule (all numbers fixed here).**
- A greedy regression tree on net profit per contract, **maximum depth 2** (at most 4 leaves), **minimum 250 training rows per leaf**, split by the lowest sum of squared error, candidate thresholds the 9 decile cut points of each feature taken from the whole sample's feature values (labels never enter the thresholds). A split that leaves a leaf under 250 rows is not allowed; if no split is allowed the tree is one leaf and skips nothing.
- **Skip rule:** an entry is skipped if its leaf's TRAINING mean net is below zero. Otherwise it is kept.
- **Walk-forward:** the first 14 UTC days are training only. For each later day, the tree is refit on all earlier days only and applied to that day's entries. Every kept/skipped decision is therefore out of sample. The kept set is the arm; the skipped set is the complement.
- **PAT1 (pattern recognition).** For each entry the pattern is the bought side's mid at the last 10 candles up to the decision candle, each minus the entry mid (a shape, not a level), the 10 numbers compared by Euclidean distance. The 200 nearest entries from EARLIER days (same walk-forward, 14 days of burn-in) vote: **skip if 24 or more of the 200 lost** (the base loss rate gives about 13 of 200, so 24 is about three standard deviations of noise above it). Entries with a missing candle in the pattern are excluded and counted.

**Counterparty.** Whoever sells us the favourite at 88c to 97c in a market that is about to flip against it. The blind spot being tested is that such flips leave a visible mark (a recent fall, a wide spread, a deep dip earlier, a time of day) that a simple rule can read. The plain reason it should fail is that the market already prices that mark, and every earlier filter on these entries was priced in the same way.

**Prediction, recorded first.** TREE1 and PAT1 each skip **5% to 25%** of entries; the kept set's mean net lands within **-0.5c to +1.0c** of the base +0.41c; both read `FALSIFIED` (about **85%** each). The most likely way either looks good is a lucky leaf in the walk-forward, which is what the placebo is for.

**Pass bar, per idea, one run each (the filters' bar, with the z step, plus a placebo and a backward holdout).** Out-of-sample kept set at least **300 entries on 5 days**; mean net above zero with a day-clustered z of at least **2.5**; positive in both halves (split at the median close time); positive with fees x1.2; kept minus skipped above zero with a day-clustered difference z of at least **2.0**; and the **gain** (the kept set's mean net minus the mean net of all out-of-sample entries) above the 95th percentile of **100 placebo draws**: the same walk-forward run again with every entry's net shuffled among the entries of the SAME DAY (features untouched), so the placebo pays for the search the learner did over 13 features. **Backward holdout, read once, only if the above all pass:** the rule fitted on ALL of `book.sqlite` and frozen, applied to `data/l1b.sqlite` (the 28 days before it, same three series); there the kept set must beat the skipped set and beat the all-entries mean. Failing the holdout is `FALSIFIED`.

**Information only, not tries:** the same two rules on `e3b.sqlite` (XRP, Dogecoin) as a different-series read; the leaves and thresholds of the final tree; the share of skipped entries that were losers.

**What a pass would and would not mean.** `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` is permission to run the skip rule on paper beside the live bot's real entries, which the owner has said he does not want, so a pass would be put to him as a choice; it is never a switch. A skip rule in live code would also change which entries the bot takes, so it would need the same promotion-and-demotion rule as a market and its own gate tests.

**Single read.** `python -m scalper.tree1 run`, once; a second run is refused unless the result file is deleted on purpose (a crash fix only, logged here). **Running count: about 4,636 tries.**

**Amendment to the TREE1 and PAT1 registration (2026-10-21, before any tree, neighbour or result was computed).** The pattern was registered as the last 10 candles up to the decision candle. A 15 minute market has only **9** candles up to the 6 minute mark (the 10th would predate the open), so the first load found no row with a 10 candle pattern. The pattern is therefore the 9 candles that exist (the decision candle and the 8 before it, each minus the decision candle's mid). Nothing else changes: the distance, k = 200, the skip at 24 losses of 200, the bar and the placebo are as registered. The load printed counts of rows only (3,038 entries, 3,036 with features); no profit, loss or tree was looked at.

## Results: TREE1 and PAT1, one run each (2026-10-21; the rules, bars and predictions are those registered above; nothing was changed after seeing them)

`python -m scalper.tree1 run`, once. 3,038 L1 entries over 41 days; 2,067 decided out of sample by TREE1 (27 days after the 14 day burn-in) and 2,062 by PAT1.

- **TREE1: `FALSIFIED`.** Skipped 718 of 2,067 (**34.7%**, above the 5% to 25% predicted). Kept 1,349: net **-0.21c**, z -0.25, halves +0.57c / -1.00c, fees x1.2 -0.30c. Kept minus skipped **-0.21c** (z -0.15): the entries the tree skipped did as well as the ones it kept. **Gain over all decided -0.50c** against a placebo 95th percentile of **+0.48c**. The final tree on all days splits on UTC hour (up to 02:00) and the 5 minute range of the mid; its leaves (-2.2c, -2.4c, +1.2c) are what a 6.5% loss rate looks like when each leaf holds about 250 entries and about 16 losses. Every earlier fit disagreed with the next one enough to cost money out of sample.
- **PAT1: `FALSIFIED`, and almost untested.** It skipped **1** of 2,062 entries. The registered threshold (24 or more losses among 200 neighbours) was set from a base loss rate of 6.5% and turned out far too high: with nearest-neighbour votes this smooth, a neighbourhood almost never holds twice the usual losses. The prediction of 5% to 25% skipped was wrong. The verdict is correct as registered (a rule that skips nothing gains nothing) but it says **nothing about whether pattern shape carries information**. A looser threshold would be a **new try** and is not run here.
- **Backward holdout (28 days before, `l1b.sqlite`): not read**, as registered (the main bar did not pass).

**What this adds.** A 13 feature tree and a 9 candle shape match on the same market's own prices, tested out of sample with a placebo, find nothing the 88c to 97c price has not already priced. This matches the earlier filters (Q1 to Q3, VOL1, PM2, PM3, the distance rules). With about 20 losses per 300 trades there is not enough loss data for a learner to separate a real pattern from noise at this depth. **Decision.** Nothing built, nothing changed live. **Count: about 4,636 tries.**

## Pre-registration: TREE2, a decision tree that chooses which markets and hours L1 trades (the owner's choice after TREE1 and PAT1; written 2026-10-21 before any pooled feature, tree or result was computed)

**Why.** TREE1 failed on three series with 196 losses, which is too few for a learner. The owner chose "trees on a different question": instead of filtering a market's entries by its own price path, let a tree pick **which series and which hours** L1 should trade at all, learned only from earlier days. The same L1 rule on every 15 minute series in the repo's data gives about **21,000 entries and about 1,500 losses**, seven times TREE1's loss data. **One more try; the z bar is raised from 2.5 to 2.6.** Running count after this registration: about **4,637**.

**Disclosed before registering (this shapes the design, so the bar is raised for it).** A per-series printout of L1's raw mean net was seen while sizing this test: Dogecoin about +1.5c, XRP about +1.4c to +1.5c, gold +1.0c (book) and +2.2c (earlier 28 days), silver +0.4c, natural gas +0.5c, WTI +0.1c, Bitcoin +0.4c to +0.6c, Ethereum +0.0c to +1.3c; negative: ZEC -1.6c, USDJPY -4.3c, GBPUSD -2.7c, BNB -0.6c to -0.8c, NEAR -0.5c, palladium -0.9c, HYPE -0.2c to -0.4c, EURUSD -0.6c, copper -0.1c, platinum -0.3c. A tree that learns "Dogecoin good, USDJPY bad" would be rediscovering that printout, which is why the test is **walk-forward**: the choice for a day is made only from earlier days, so a series that was good in September and bad in October costs the tree money, exactly as it would cost the live bot. Nothing about hours, days or price was looked at.

**Population.** `lstrats.hold_rule` with `L1` on every series ending in `15M` in `alts2`, `alts3`, `alts4`, `book`, `l1b` and `e3b` (`.sqlite` under `data/`), de-duplicated by ticker. Ladder series (`KXBTCD`, `KXETHD`, `KXINXU`) and non-candle databases are not in it. Costs and the x1.2 stress are as in every L1 test.

**Features (all from candles that END at or before the decision candle):** TREE1's `price`, `spread`, `d1`, `d3`, `d5`, `rng5`, `dip`, `hi_gap`, `hour` (UTC) and `dow`, plus **one 0/1 flag per series** present in the data. Rows with a missing candle are excluded and counted.

**Rule.** TREE1's learner (greedy regression tree on net profit per contract, decile cut points from the whole sample's feature values) with **maximum depth 3** and **minimum 400 training rows per leaf**. **Skip an entry if its leaf's training mean net is below zero.** Walk-forward by UTC day: the first **14 days** of the pooled calendar are training only; the tree is **refit every 7 days** on all earlier days and used for the next 7 days (a day's decisions never use that day or later). The kept set is the arm, the skipped set the complement.

**Counterparty.** Whoever sells the favourite in a series where the 88c to 97c price understates how often it flips (thin books, a wide spread, a time of day with less informed flow). Calendar and venue effects like these are persistent in principle, which is the best argument for this version; the argument against is the owner's own record, where more markets meant more loss, not more gain.

**Prediction, recorded first.** TREE2 skips **20% to 60%** of out-of-sample entries; the kept mean lands between the all-entries mean and that mean plus **1.5c**; verdict **`FALSIFIED`** (about **65%**). If it passes, the likeliest reason is that it learned a few durable series (Dogecoin, XRP), which the live bot's per-market table can already read without a tree.

**Pass bar (one run).** Kept set at least **1,000 entries on 10 days**; mean net above zero with a day-clustered z of at least **2.6**; positive in both halves (median close time); positive with fees x1.2; kept minus skipped above zero with a day-clustered difference z of at least **2.0**; the **gain** (kept mean minus the all-decided mean) above the 95th percentile of **100 placebo draws** (the same walk-forward with every entry's net shuffled among the entries of the SAME DAY; features untouched). **Also read, as part of the same bar:** the gain in **each calendar month** present (the kept set must beat the all-decided mean in every month with at least 300 decided entries). There is no backward holdout (the earlier days are inside the pool); the forward test is the live probe markets, which is stated here so a pass is not mistaken for one.

**Information only, not tries:** the final tree on all days; per series, the share kept and the kept and skipped means; the share of skipped entries that were losers.

**Single read.** `python -m scalper.tree2 run`, once; a second run is refused unless the result file is deleted on purpose (a crash fix only, logged here). A tree on this data can only suggest what to look at in the live per-market table; **it is never a switch**. **Running count: about 4,637 tries.**

## Results: TREE2, one run, read once (2026-10-21; the rule, bar and prediction are those registered above; nothing was changed after seeing them)

`python -m scalper.tree2 run`, once (the only earlier call was a timing of one walk-forward that printed a row count, not a result). The pool was **24,793** L1 entries (the registration said about 21,000) over 18 series and 69 days; 24,342 had features; 20,002 were decided out of sample.

- **TREE2: `FALSIFIED`, by the z bar alone.** Skipped 4,954 of 20,002 (**24.8%**, inside the predicted 20% to 60%). Kept 15,048 on 55 days: net **+0.44c**, z **+1.97** (bar 2.6), halves +0.72c / +0.15c, fees x1.2 +0.34c. All decided entries: **+0.08c**.
- **What passed:** kept minus skipped **+1.45c** (day clustered z **+3.14**, bar 2.0); gain over all decided **+0.36c** against a placebo 95th percentile of **+0.22c**; positive in both halves and with fees x1.2; and the kept set beat the all-decided mean in **every month** (Aug +0.81c vs +0.62c, Sep +0.43c vs +0.05c, Oct +0.17c vs -0.28c). Everything but the absolute z cleared. The skipped set averaged about **-1.0c**.
- **What it means, in plain terms.** This is the first filter on L1 in this log whose skipped entries are reliably worse than its kept ones (every earlier Q, VOL, PM and distance filter failed that test). It is a **ranking** result, not a profit result: the kept set is still only +0.44c a contract, one third of it in a September that is not a promise, and it falls every month (+0.81c, +0.43c, +0.17c) as the tree and the market move on. The z of 1.97 is below the bar set for this try because the sample cannot distinguish +0.44c from zero.
- **What the tree used.** Not series. The final tree (information) splits on **spread** (at or under 3c), the 3 minute change in the side's mid (`d3`), the lowest the side's mid had been (`dip`) and day of week; the leaves with a wide spread or a large rise in the last 3 minutes are the negative ones (-0.6c to -7.0c), the narrow spread, flat leaves the positive ones (+0.5c to +1.9c). Series differences did not need the tree: kept versus skipped within a series differs in most of them (Bitcoin +0.6c vs -2.0c; copper +0.6c vs -2.7c; natural gas +1.0c vs -0.9c; NEAR +0.4c vs -1.5c; HYPE +0.2c vs -2.4c), so **the spread and shape of the entry carries information across series**.
- **Not run, and why:** a rule that keeps only a spread under 3c, or only the best leaves, would be a **new try** on the same rows and is not run here. It needs fresh days (nothing after 2026-10-12 is in these databases), and the live bot's own per-order log does not record the quote's spread at entry.

**Decision.** Nothing built, nothing changed live. If a forward test is ever wanted, the cheapest honest one is to have the live bot **log the spread (and `d3`, `dip`) at each entry** and read the live record against a rule registered first; that needs a code change to the live bot and so the owner's go. **Count: about 4,637 tries.**

## Pre-registration: FWD2, a forward read of "skip a wide spread" on the live bot's own orders (the owner's choice after TREE2; written 2026-10-21 before any live order's spread was looked at)

**Why.** TREE2's strongest and plainest finding was that L1 entries with a quote spread over 3c did worse than the rest (the tree's first split; kept minus skipped +1.45c, z +3.14 across 18 series), while its absolute bar failed. The live bot already saves the quote it saw on every order (`seen.bid`, `seen.ask`), so the spread of every live L1 order is on record without any change to the bot. The all-orders CSV on the page now exports `seenBid` and `seenAsk` (PR from `claude/log-entry-quote`; no live code touched). **One more try; the bar is stated below, not raised, because this is a one-sided forward read of a single pre-named cut with no search.** Running count: about **4,638**.

**Disclosed.** TREE2's cut (3c) was read off its final tree and its per-series table. No live order's spread has been computed or compared with its result; the 477 orders exported earlier did not include the quote.

**Rule (fixed here).** For L1 orders the bot sent **on or after 2026-10-22 00:00 UTC** that filled and settled with a win or loss (`result` is not `hand`, not `exit`; an `exit` is read separately below): **spread = seen.ask minus seen.bid**, per contract net = saved P/L divided by contracts filled. **Wide** is spread **over 0.03**; **narrow** is 0.03 or less. Orders with no saved quote are excluded and counted.

**Counterparty / mechanism.** A wide spread means few resting orders on one side; the favourite there is priced by a thin book that a single order can move, and the same state is where a flip is least visible to the price.

**Prediction, recorded first.** Wide orders are **10% to 30%** of fills; the wide group's mean net per contract is **at least 1.0c below** the narrow group's; verdict `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` (about **40%**; a spread cut measured on 1 minute candles may not equal the spread at the decision second).

**Read (once).** At the first of **250 filled settled orders or 2026-12-01**. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` needs: wide group at least **40** orders; narrow group mean net **above zero**; narrow minus wide **above zero** with a day-clustered z of at least **2.0**; and the narrow group above zero in **both halves** (by time). Anything else is `FALSIFIED`; fewer than 40 wide orders is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`, never a pass. Information only, not part of the verdict: the same split by series; orders that were exited at 50c, read separately (the exit watch makes their net not comparable).

**What a pass would and would not mean.** It would be a reason to put a "skip when the spread is over 3c" rule to the owner as a choice, with its own gate tests; it is never a switch, and a rule added to live code would cost the entries it skips (about the share above). **Running count: about 4,638 tries.**

## Information: slippage and fees from the owner's own order diagnostics (2026-10-21; no hypothesis, no verdict, no variant counted)

The owner asked whether slippage on the bot's immediate-or-cancel limit orders is what makes fees "kill" it. `studies/order_diagnostics_2026-10-21.csv` is the page's "Copy order diagnostics" export (150 bot orders, 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-21; 103 filled, 101 with a public settled result in `..._results.json`). A NO order's `avgFill` is the YES-book price, so the price paid is 1 minus it. Settlement result per market from Kalshi's public market endpoint. Hold-to-settlement P/L at the ACTUAL fill price and actual fee; exit-watch sells are not modelled (an exited order is scored as the held loss).

| | |
|---|---|
| Filled orders / contracts | 103 / 384 |
| Slippage against the decision price | mean **-0.99c** (negative = filled BETTER), median -0.10c; worse than decided by over 0.5c on only **5** of 103 orders, better by over 0.5c on **38** |
| Actual fee per contract | **0.50c**, equal to Kalshi's 7% x p x (1 - p) at the fill price (mean difference -0.001c), so the order-level round-up is already inside it |
| All 101 settled | **-$10.61** (-2.83c a contract), 9 losses (8.9%); before fees at the actual fills **-$8.71**, fees **$1.90** |
| Filled better than decided by over 0.5c | 37 orders, 6 lost, **-$11.91 (-8.8c a contract)** |
| Filled within 0.5c of decided | 59 orders, 2 lost, **+$5.09 (+2.31c a contract)** |
| Filled worse than decided by over 0.5c | 5 orders, 1 lost, -$3.79 |

**Reading (one look, not pre-registered, so a lead and not a result).** Slippage is not what costs the bot: fills are on average better than the decision price, and fees are exactly the formula. What the table shows is **adverse selection in the price improvement**: when the order fills 1c to 25c BETTER than the quote, the book had moved against the position between the read and the order landing, and those fills lose far more often (16% against 3%). An IOC at the touch is therefore filling a mix of stable quotes (good) and collapsing ones (bad), as the 2026-10-08 live fills study also suggested. Two cheap, testable consequences, neither run here: (1) refuse a fill that is more than about 1c better than the decision price (it needs a limit on the other side, which Kalshi does not offer on an IOC, so the check would be after the fact, by selling or by sending a smaller order first), and (2) the maker/resting idea is unchanged by this table. Any rule built from this table is a new try and needs a pre-registration and fresh orders; the forward set is the bot's own new orders (FWD2 already reads their spread).

## Information: Kalshi's maker and taker fee schedule (looked up 2026-10-21; not a try)

Primary source: `kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf`. Fetching the PDF itself was refused (HTTP 429, twice), so the figures below come from a search summary quoting it and from third-party write-ups that agree with it. **Re-read the PDF before any decision rests on these numbers.**

- **Taker:** fee = round up to the next cent of `0.07 x contracts x p x (1 - p)`. This matches the bot's measured 0.50c a contract exactly (see the slippage section).
- **Maker (a resting order that fills later):** `0.0175 x contracts x p x (1 - p)`, one quarter of the taker rate. Cancelling costs nothing. Maker fees are not charged on every market; the schedule page lists which have them. Some series carry their own multiplier. Whether the 15 minute series carry a maker fee, or a multiplier, is **not confirmed**.
- **At L1's prices:** at 94c a taker fee is about **0.40c** a contract before round-up and a maker fee about **0.10c**, so resting saves about **0.3c** a contract. L1's mean net is only about +0.1c to +0.4c, so 0.3c is the same size as the whole edge.
- **Why that does not settle the owner's question.** The fee is not the obstacle; the fill is. Resting-limit entries were tried and fills concentrate on the losers (the market only trades down to a resting bid when it is falling), so the 0.3c fee saving was more than paid back in selection. A manual scalper pays less in fees per trade but still has to be filled by someone who knows more. **Not a try, no verdict.**

## Pre-registration: FWD3, "a fill much better than decided is a warning" on the bot's own new orders (written 2026-10-21 before any order from 2026-10-22 was looked at)

**Why.** The slippage section found that the 37 of 103 orders filled more than 0.5c better than decided lost 6 times (-8.8c a contract), against 2 losses in 59 orders filled within 0.5c (+2.31c). That was one look at orders already seen, so it is a lead. This reads it forward on orders that do not exist yet. **One more try. Running count: about 4,639.** No search, one cut (0.5c) taken from that table, so the bar is stated, not raised.

**Rule (fixed here).** Population is FWD2's: L1 orders sent on or after **2026-10-22 00:00 UTC** that filled and settled as a win or loss (not `hand`, not `exit`). Paid price = `avgFill` for YES, `1 - avgFill` for NO. **Improvement = decisionPrice minus paid price.** **Improved** is improvement over **0.005**; **steady** is 0.005 or less (including worse fills). Per contract net = saved P/L divided by contracts filled. Read from the "Copy order diagnostics" export or the all-orders CSV.

**Mechanism.** A big price improvement means the quote the bot read was stale when the order landed, and a stale quote on the favourite's side is stale because sellers rushed in.

**Prediction, recorded first.** Improved orders are **25% to 45%** of fills; improved loses at least **3 percentage points more often** than steady and has a mean net at least **2.0c lower**; verdict `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` (about **35%**; a gap of 8.8c on 37 orders is mostly 6 losses, and regression to the mean is the likeliest outcome).

**Read (once).** At **250 filled settled orders or 2026-12-01**, together with FWD2. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` needs: improved group at least **40** orders; steady minus improved mean net **above zero** with a day-clustered z of at least **2.0**; steady group above zero overall; and the sign of steady minus improved the same in both halves (by time). Fewer than 40 improved orders is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. Anything else is `FALSIFIED`. Information only: the same split by series; improvement size buckets (0.5c to 2c, over 2c).

**What a pass would and would not mean.** It cannot be applied as a pre-trade filter, because the improvement is only known after the fill. The only after-the-fact moves are a **probe order first** (a 1 contract IOC, then the full size only if the probe filled steady) or **selling back at once**. Both cost the entries they skip and the spread; each would be its own registered test using the book at the time, which the order log does not hold. A pass is a reason to log the book after each fill, nothing more. Never a switch.

**Amendment to FWD3 (2026-10-21, at the owner's decision relayed by the main session; before any order from 2026-10-22 was looked at).**
1. **Two rules the bot could apply, each read as its own arm.** (A) *post-fill*: the improved-fill split above (needs a sell-back or probe, and the book after the fill, which is not logged). (B) *pre-trade*, which needs no new data because the order log already saves `bidSize` and `askSize`: **skip when the size resting at the ask of the bought side is 10 contracts or fewer** (a thin touch is the quote most likely to be gone when the order lands). The 10 is fixed here, not read from any data; no size has been compared with any result. Arm B is read exactly like arm A: group at least 40 orders, steady minus thin mean net above zero, day-clustered z, same sign in both halves.
2. **Two arms, so two tries. Running count: about 4,640.** The z bar is raised from 2.0 to **2.2** for each arm.
3. **Population widened:** the bot's own filled, settled L1 orders from 2026-10-22 on, plus any days a longer export covers that the 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-21 file does not (those days are read as a separate, older block and are never pooled with the forward block for the verdict).
4. **Prediction for arm B:** thin-touch orders are **15% to 40%** of fills and lose at least 3 points more often; `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` about **25%**. A pre-trade skip costs the entries it skips, so arm B must also show the skipped group's mean net below zero, not merely below the kept group.
Nothing else changes. Live code is untouched; a pass of either arm is put to the owner as a choice with gate tests, never a switch.

## Pre-registration: SLOW1, time-series trend on nine liquid ETFs, one family of three cells (written 2026-10-21 before any return was computed; the owner's "cross-asset screen of documented slow return sources")

**What the request asked for and what is already done (so nothing is retried under a new name).**
- *Overnight vs intraday on SPY/QQQ*: **already run as IDX1 (2026-10-14), FALSIFIED** (SPY holdout alpha -2.05% a year, QQQ +0.57%, both negative at 4 bp). A rerun on the SIP open and close would test the same effect; I have no Alpaca key (and never ask for one), so it is **not run here**. If the owner wants it, the main session can run it with the account's key as a separate, registered try.
- *Turn of the month*: **already run as IDX1, FALSIFIED (not shown)**, +1.09% a year, z 0.72. Not rerun as a "control".
- *Post-earnings drift*: **`NOT_RUNNABLE` here.** It needs point-in-time earnings dates and surprise figures; no free source I can fetch gives them, and I will not fabricate. `shwoop-server/research/MECHANISMS.md` is said in this README to hold it as FALSIFIED; that file is not in this checkout, so I cannot confirm it.
- *Trend*: PERP1 (20 day breakout, gold/S&P/Bitcoin/Ethereum, 2010 on) passed as registered, but only through crypto's early run; **entries from 2022 on averaged 0.00%**. SLOW1 below is a different rule (monthly, long or cash, nine ETFs, no crypto), so crypto's bull market cannot carry it.
- `src/scalper/deflate.py` named in the request **does not exist in this checkout**. I price the tries with a Sidak correction instead (below) and say so.

**Disclosed.** I downloaded Yahoo daily bars (adjusted close, total return) and printed only counts and date ranges: SPY from 1993, QQQ 1999, EFA 2001, EEM 2003, TLT and IEF 2002, GLD 2004, DBC 2006, UUP 2007-03-01, all to 2026-10-21. No signal or return has been computed.

**Universe and sample.** SPY, QQQ, EFA, EEM, TLT, IEF, GLD, DBC, UUP (US large and tech, developed and emerging stocks, long and mid Treasuries, gold, broad commodities, the dollar). Common sample starts 2007-03-01 (UUP's first bar) to 2026-10-21, about 19.5 years of months. Source: Yahoo chart API, `interval=1d`, adjusted close.

**Rule (fixed; one run, three cells).** At each month's last trading day close, for each ETF: if its trailing total return over the last **L trading days** (L = 252, 126, 63 for cells S1, S2, S3) is above zero, hold it next month; otherwise hold cash (return zero; cash earning nothing is deliberately harsh). Weight 1/9 per ETF, so the portfolio is a share in cash when few ETFs trend. Entry and exit are at the **next trading day's close** after the signal (a one day lag, no signal-day fills). Rebalanced monthly; the benchmark `b` is the same nine ETFs, equal weight, rebalanced monthly, always invested.
- **Costs.** 5 basis points per side on each ETF's traded weight (spread plus slippage; Alpaca charges no commission on ETFs), 6 in the stress case (x1.2). No shorting, no leverage, no funding.
- **Statistic.** Monthly return `s` of the timed portfolio net of costs; alpha = intercept of `s` on `b`, annualised x12; z from Newey-West errors with 3 lags (monthly returns overlap in volatility). It asks whether timing earns more than its own market exposure explains.

**Tries and the bar (priced for the family).** Cells: S1, S2, S3 = **3 tries**. The same family of calendar and trend ideas has already used IDX1 (4) and PERP1 (1), so the family count is **8**; a Sidak one-sided p of 0.05/8 = 0.0064 is **z = 2.5**. That is the bar for each cell. Kalshi running count unchanged (this is not a Kalshi idea; its own count is 8 family tries).

**Pass bar, per cell.** At least **120 months**; alpha net of costs above zero; Newey-West z at least **2.5**; alpha above zero in **both halves** (months split at the median) **and in 2022 on**; alpha still above zero at the stress cost; alpha above the 95th percentile of **200 placebo draws** (for each ETF, the same number of invested months placed at random months, same costs). Anything else `FALSIFIED`; under 120 months `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`; a pass is `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED`, which is permission to consider a forward probe, never evidence of an edge.

**Counterparty.** Slow money that reacts late and unevenly to a persistent move (investors who rebalance quarterly, pensions, anyone anchored to last year's level), and the documented time-series momentum premium in futures and ETFs. The blind spot: since 2009 the cost of cash drag in a long bull market, and trend reversals that arrive faster than a monthly review.

**Prediction, recorded first.** Net alpha between **-1% and +2% a year** per cell, z below 1.5, all three `FALSIFIED` (about **80%**). The likeliest "good" outcome is lower drawdown for the same average return, which this bar does not count as alpha; I report drawdown and Sharpe as information.

**Dollar size (information).** For any cell with positive alpha: alpha in percent a year times a $200 account. At 2% a year that is $4; the report states it so a statistically real edge is not mistaken for a useful one.

**Information only, not tries:** timed versus buy-and-hold return, volatility, Sharpe and worst drawdown; alpha by calendar year; months invested; per-ETF contribution.

**Single read.** `python -m scalper.slow1 fetch` then `python -m scalper.slow1 run`, once; the result file blocks a rerun unless deleted on purpose (a crash fix only). Nothing here goes live. **Family tries: 8.**

| Cell | Months | Net alpha a year | NW z (bar 2.5) | Halves | 2022 on | At x1.2 cost | Placebo p95 | Verdict |

| S1, 252 day lookback | 223 | **+2.32%** | **2.30** | +1.98% / +2.06% | +4.31% | +2.31% | +1.10% | **FALSIFIED** |
| S2, 126 day lookback | 229 | **+2.75%** | **2.27** | +3.20% / +1.35% | +2.44% | +2.73% | +0.92% | **FALSIFIED** |
| S3, 63 day lookback | 232 | **+2.70%** | **2.10** | +2.09% / +3.02% | +3.67% | +2.67% | +0.85% | **FALSIFIED** |

But its return is **lower**: 5.2% a year against 6.9% for buying and holding the same nine ETFs. The "alpha" is mostly that it holds less market (beta 0.33 to 0.41) at a similar Sharpe edge. This is a risk-reduction result, not a way to earn more.
- **The three cells are one idea at three lookbacks**, so they are not three independent confirmations; agreement among them says little beyond "trend over 3 to 12 months looks the same".
- **Dollar size.** +2.3% to +2.75% a year on a $200 account is **about $4.60 to $5.50 a year** before any account fees or tax. Real, if it is real, and not worth the attention at this size.
- **Window check.** The edge is not a recent-window artefact (positive 2007 to 2014 and 2015 on, and larger from 2022), which is the main difference from PERP1 and the overnight work.
- **Not run, and why:** a looser z or a shorter sample would be a new try chosen after seeing this; so would other lookbacks or shorting. A reading of "NOT_YET_FALSIFIED in spirit" is not allowed: the verdict is `FALSIFIED`. If it is ever wanted forward, it needs a registered paper record from today (nothing here goes live), and the owner has said he prefers live over paper, so this one is put to him as a choice, not recommended.

## Pre-registration: SECT1, sector momentum on the nine original SPDR sector ETFs (written 2026-10-21 before any sector return was computed; the owner's instruction: find a strategy or an edge to deploy)

**Why this and not another.** The mechanisms index above (about 180 registered ideas) shows Kalshi 15 minute, ladder, weather, sports, perpetual and single-stock ideas all crossed off. The one family with a published reason to work, a long clean history, near-zero cost and no overlap with anything tried is **cross-sectional momentum**: winners among industries keep beating losers for months because industry news diffuses slowly across investors (Moskowitz and Grinblatt, 1999; Hong, Torous and Valkanov, 2007). SLOW1 asked "should I be in the market"; this asks "which parts of it". **Prior that it passes: about 15%.** The published effect weakened after 2000, which is the reason to expect `FALSIFIED`, and the sample below is mostly after 2000.

**Disclosed.** I know the ETF tickers and approximate start dates from memory (the nine Select Sector SPDRs launched in December 1998). I have not downloaded them. No return, rank or signal has been computed. SLOW1 (same universe type, different question) is the only related result, and it used different ETFs.

**Universe and sample.** XLB (materials), XLE (energy), XLF (financials), XLI (industrials), XLK (technology), XLP (staples), XLU (utilities), XLV (health care), XLY (discretionary). Yahoo daily adjusted close (total return), common sample from the first full month after all nine exist (expected 1999) to 2026-10-21. XLRE and XLC are excluded (they start in 2015 and 2018 and would change the universe mid-sample).

**Rule (fixed; one run, two cells).** At each month's last trading day close, rank the nine by their return from **L days ago to 21 trading days ago** (skipping the latest month, the standard 12-1 or 6-1 construction; L = 252 for cell C1, L = 126 for cell C2). **Hold the top 3 at equal weight for the next month**; the other six are not held (cash share is zero, the account is always fully invested). Entry and exit at the **next trading day's close** after the signal (a one day lag). The benchmark `b` is all nine at equal weight, rebalanced monthly.
- **Costs.** 5 basis points per side on traded weight (6 in the x1.2 stress). No shorting, no leverage, no borrow.
- **Statistic.** Monthly net return `s` of the held portfolio; alpha = intercept of `s` on `b`, annualised x12; z from Newey-West errors with 3 lags (the SLOW1 code, reused unchanged).

**Tries and the bar.** Two cells. The family count was 8 (IDX1 4, PERP1 1, SLOW1 3); it is **10** after this registration. Sidak one-sided p = 0.05/10 = 0.005, **z bar = 2.6** for each cell.

**Pass bar, per cell.** At least **120 months**; alpha net of costs above zero; Newey-West z at least **2.6**; alpha above zero in **both halves** (months split at the median) **and in the last 8 years (2019 on)**; alpha above zero at the x1.2 stress cost; alpha above the 95th percentile of **200 placebo draws** (3 sectors picked uniformly at random each month, same costs and one day lag). Anything else `FALSIFIED`; under 120 months `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`; a pass is `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED`, permission to propose a probe and nothing more. **A near miss is a miss.**

**Counterparty.** Investors who adjust industry exposure slowly (committees, quarterly rebalancers, benchmarked managers). The blind spot: when leadership rotates fast, the rule buys last year's winners just as they turn.

**Prediction, recorded first.** Net alpha between **-1.5% and +2.5% a year**, z below 1.5 in both cells, both `FALSIFIED` (about **85%**). Turnover costs are small (5 bp on about half the portfolio a month, around 0.6% a year), so a miss would be about the signal, not the cost.

**Dollar size (information).** Alpha in percent a year times $200 and $500.

**Information only, not tries:** return, volatility, Sharpe and worst drawdown against the equal-weight benchmark; alpha by calendar year; how often each sector is held.

**Single read.** `python -m scalper.sect1 fetch` then `python -m scalper.sect1 run`, once; a second run is refused unless the result file is deleted on purpose (a crash fix only). Nothing here goes live. **Family tries: 10.**
