## LIVE3: fills against no-fills in the full live export (2026-10-22, information only)

The owner's full "Copy all orders" export (607 orders, Oct 7 to 22) arrived in three parts. I saved the 219 L1 orders that did not fill (`studies/live_nofills_2026-10-22.csv`; count matches 607 minus the 387 fills) and scored them next to the fills (`src/scalper/live_fill.py`), both held to settlement at the order's limit price with the fee, using public results. This removes the exit rule and the actual fill price from the comparison. No registered claim, no verdict; adds no tries.

- Fills: 366 settled, loss rate **5.7%**, **+0.92c** a contract. No-fills: 209 settled, loss rate **8.1%**, **-0.82c** (30 orders on XRP, Dogecoin and natural gas cannot be settled from the candles I hold).
- The no-fills are not hidden winners. The orders that did not fill would have done worse than the ones that did, so the live record is not adverse-selected by the IOC fill rule. Per-day paired difference is -0.87c with z -0.19 over only 13 days with both, so treat the sign as unresolved, not as an edge.
- Held to settlement, the 366 fills lose 5.7%, under the roughly 6.8% break-even. The live net P/L (-$11.74) is therefore not the entry rule; it comes from size (the two large Bitcoin losses), the exits and the crowded windows (LIVE2).

## Pre-registration: FLAT1 (2026-10-22), a firm and flat favourite in the 5 minutes before entry

Owner's pick (Option 2). Idea: an L1 favourite whose price has barely moved in the last 5 minutes has no pending reversal, while one that is still moving may overshoot. This is a single simple rule on two features the model studies (FEAT1 to FEAT4) only used inside a fitted blend. It overlaps TIB1 and DIP1 (firm favourites) in spirit; those are forward claims on fresh days and this is a different, simpler cut tested on the history. I count it as a separate try.

- **Data:** `feat1.build(markets, 360)` rows (L1 entries at 360 s, band 0.88 to 0.97, all 18 series in the history). Features per row: `rise3` (3 minute change of the bought side's mid) and `rng5` (5 minute range of that mid).
- **Groups (known at the entry minute):** FLAT = `rng5 <= 0.02` and `abs(rise3) <= 0.01`. MOVING = every other entry. Each group from its own entries, compared per day (day-clustered).
- **Primary claim:** FLAT minus MOVING mean net per contract is at least +1.0c.
- **Prediction (now):** +0.8c; I expect a smaller gap than the clean +1.0c because FEAT showed these features carry only part of the signal.
- **Supported (NOT_YET_FALSIFIED) needs all of:** FLAT n >= 1,500 and >= 10 days; diff >= +1.0c with day-clustered z >= 2.0; same sign in both halves by time; same sign under the x1.2 fee stress; same sign in at least 2 of the months present (months with at least 200 FLAT entries); placebo (100 random relabels of the same group sizes) 95th percentile of diff z below the observed.
- **FALSIFIED:** diff < +0.3c or z < 1.0. Anything else NOT_ENOUGH_DATA.
- **Information only:** FLAT share of entries, loss rates of both groups, results on the live five series alone.
- Tries: +1 (running count about 4,691). Run once: `python -m scalper.flat1 run`.

### FLAT1 result (2026-10-22, run once): NOT_ENOUGH_DATA

My thresholds were set without counting the group first (the same mistake as XLEAD1). Only **31 of 24,792** entries met `rng5 <= 0.02` and `abs(rise3) <= 0.01` (0.13%), over 21 days; the claim needed 1,500. The figures are not evidence: flat +2.25c against moving +0.12c, difference +2.71c, z 1.15, first half +5.61c and second half -1.10c, no month with 200 flat entries. The live-five-series information cut has 8 flat entries. Nothing was concluded.

Feature distribution (no outcomes looked at): the median 5 minute range at the 6 minute mark is **0.24**, and the 5th, 25th percentiles are 0.067 and 0.15; |rise3| 25th percentile is 0.049, median 0.11. Favourites at 6 minutes have mostly just arrived, so a "flat for 5 minutes" favourite is very rare. A fair test needs a looser cut, chosen from these quantiles and not from outcomes, and registered as a new try (FLAT2). Tries: +1 (running count about 4,691).

## Pre-registration: SIZE1 (2026-10-22), put the contracts on FLAT entries at the same total contracts

Idea: FLAT's value may be where the size goes, not which trades are skipped. Policy B puts 6 contracts on every FLAT entry and none on the rest (FLAT is about 14% to 15% of entries, so B holds about 85% of policy A's contracts a day). Policy A is today's 1 contract on every entry. History only, in dollars per day, no live code.

- **Data and rule:** `feat1.build(markets, 360)` rows (L1, 6 minutes, band 0.88 to 0.97) for the five live series (Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Dogecoin, gold), FLAT = `rng5 <= 0.15` and `abs(rise3) <= 0.05` (FLAT2's cut). Per day: A = sum of `net` over all entries (1 contract each); B = 6 x sum of `net` over FLAT entries. `net` already includes the fee. No fill assumption beyond the posted ask (live fills were within about a cent in LIVE3).
- **Claims, both needed:** (1) B's mean daily P/L minus A's is positive with a day-clustered paired z >= 2.0, same sign in both halves of the days; (2) B is not riskier: B's 5th percentile day is no more than 25% worse than A's (B_p5 >= 1.25 x A_p5 when A_p5 is negative), and B's worst single trade is the 6 contract loss (reported, not a pass condition).
- **Prediction (now):** (1) yes, B about 2x A per day; (2) borderline, because 6 contract losses on a 3.5% loss rate make worse bad days.
- **FALSIFIED** if claim (1) fails (z < 1.0 or the difference <= 0); NOT_YET_FALSIFIED only if both hold; otherwise NOT_ENOUGH_DATA. Days >= 30.
- **Information only:** the same without gold; B with 3 contracts; days where B lost more than A.
- Tries: +1 (running count about 4,701). Run once: `python -m scalper.size_flat run`.

### SIZE1 result (2026-10-22, run once): NOT_ENOUGH_DATA (claim 1 passes, the risk claim fails)

Five live series, 69 days, dollars per day (history, fees in, posted asks). A (1 contract on every entry): **+$1.63 a day**, sd $2.80, 5th percentile day -$2.81, worst day -$5.01. B (6 contracts on FLAT only): **+$3.42 a day**, sd $5.39, 5th percentile day **-$6.89**, worst day **-$15.73**. B minus A +$1.80 a day, paired day-clustered z 3.40; halves +$2.38 and +$1.23; B lost more than A on 21 of 69 days. Claim 1 holds; claim 2 (5th percentile day no more than 25% worse than A) fails, B is about 2.5x worse. Without gold the picture is the same (A +$1.32, B +$3.37, B 5th percentile -$7.39).

The reading that matters: B roughly doubles both the mean and the spread (mean to sd about 0.64 for B against 0.58 for A). It is close to leverage, not a free improvement. At 3 contracts on FLAT, the mean equals A ($1.71 against $1.63, difference +$0.08, z 0.28) with about the same spread, so concentrating size on FLAT at equal risk adds little. FLAT's edge per trade is real in this history, but at constant risk it does not pay much more than trading everything. Tries: +1 (running count about 4,701).

## Pre-registration: ENTRY1 (2026-10-22), does choosing each series' entry minute from past data beat a fixed 6 minutes

The 10 minute entry (PR #453) helped Bitcoin, XRP and natural gas. ENTRY1 asks whether picking each series' best entry minute from earlier days is something that holds afterwards. Walk-forward only, because picking the best of eight minutes on the same days is the overfit.

- **Data:** `feat1.build(markets, left)` L1 entries (band 0.88 to 0.97) for left = 720, 660, 600, 540, 480, 420, 360 and 300 seconds, all 18 series, 69 days. Each market can appear at several minutes; a market is only ever entered once, at its series' chosen minute.
- **Split by days (fixed now):** TRAIN = the first 46 days, TEST = the last 23.
- **Choice:** for each series, among minutes with at least 150 TRAIN entries, the minute with the highest TRAIN mean net per contract. A series with no eligible minute stays at 360.
- **Claim:** on TEST days, the chosen-minute entries minus the fixed-360 entries (each group from its own entries, mean net per contract per day, pooled over series with a chosen minute other than 360, day-clustered) is at least +0.5c with z >= 2.0; same sign in both halves of the TEST days and under the x1.2 fee stress; at least 5 series change minute; and the placebo (100 random choices of one minute per series from the eligible ones) 95th percentile of the same statistic is below the observed.
- **Prediction (now):** +0.3c, a miss. Selecting among eight minutes per series from 46 days will mostly overfit; I expect most series to keep a minute near 360 or to drift.
- **FALSIFIED** if the difference is below +0.2c or z < 1.0. NOT_YET_FALSIFIED only if every condition holds; otherwise NOT_ENOUGH_DATA.
- **Information only:** which minute each series picked, and the full table of mean net by series and minute on TRAIN and TEST.
- Tries: +1 (running count about 4,703; the choice step itself is searched over 144 cells, which is why it is walk-forward). Run once: `python -m scalper.entry1 run`.

## Pre-registration: WX1 (2026-10-22), weather daily-high markets against the official blended forecast

Owner: "get more aggressive with our edges" (hunt bigger edges). A different market class from the 15 minute book. Kalshi lists a daily high temperature ladder per city (six markets a day: two tails and four 2 degree brackets, resolved on the NWS climate report maximum), with volumes in the tens of thousands of contracts. Checked first (information): a market that is already decided by the observed temperature trades at 100c (LAX, 37 decided cases at 5 times of day, all priced 1.00), so a nowcast has no edge. The only open question is whether the official forecast beats the market price BEFORE the day. Source: the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive of the National Blend of Models (NBS) text forecast, which gives the forecast daily maximum (`txn`) and its standard deviation (`xnd`) directly.

- **Cities and markets:** KXHIGHAUS, KXHIGHCHI, KXHIGHDEN, KXHIGHLAX, KXHIGHMIA, KXHIGHNY, KXHIGHPHIL (stations KAUS, KMDW, KDEN, KLAX, KMIA, KNYC, KPHL), every settled market over the 69 days Kalshi serves.
- **Forecast (no lookahead):** for target local day D, the NBS run at 12:00 UTC of day D-1 (published before the market's first useful hour); `txn` at the forecast time that is 00:00 UTC of D+1 is the forecast maximum for D, `xnd` its standard deviation. P(max >= k) uses a normal with those two numbers and the integer correction (max is a whole degree): P(max >= k) = 1 - Phi((k - 0.5 - txn) / xnd). Tail and bracket probabilities follow. A run with `txn` or `xnd` missing is skipped.
- **Price:** the market's YES bid and ask in the 60 minute candle that ends nearest 20:00 UTC on D-1 (ask for buying YES; 1 minus the bid for buying NO). No candle, no trade.
- **Rule:** buy YES if `p - ask - fee >= 0.07`; buy NO if `(1 - p) - (1 - bid) - fee >= 0.07`; fee is 7% p(1-p) at the price paid; one contract per market, held to settlement. At most one trade per market.
- **Claim:** mean net per contract >= +2.0c with day-clustered z >= 3.0 (market date as the cluster), n >= 300 trades over >= 20 days, same sign in both halves by date and under the x1.2 fee stress, and positive in at least 5 of the 7 cities. FALSIFIED if mean < +0.5c or z < 1.0; otherwise NOT_ENOUGH_DATA.
- **Prediction (now):** FALSIFIED (about 70%). The market already uses the same models; I expect the model probabilities to be well calibrated and the trades that clear 7c to be mostly edges in the thin tails. If it passes, the first suspect is the 12Z run's availability time.
- **Information only:** calibration of p against outcomes by decile; the same rule at a 3 cent threshold; by city.
- Tries: +1 (running count about 4,704). The fetch step and the run are separate: `python -m scalper.wx1 fetch`, then `python -m scalper.wx1 run` once.

### WX1 result (2026-10-22, run once): FALSIFIED, and the loss is significant

Seven cities, 2,772 settled markets with a forecast and a price, 69 days. The rule (buy where the NBS-normal probability beats the ask or bid price by at least 7c after the fee) fired on **1,197 trades over 67 days**: mean net **-4.70c a contract, day-clustered z -4.17**, both halves negative (-2.80c, -6.60c), fee stress -4.91c, only 1 of 7 cities positive (Austin +0.54c; New York -11.8c, Los Angeles -6.5c). The 3c threshold version is the same (-4.26c, z -4.74, 1,659 trades, 0 of 7 cities positive).

The model itself is not badly calibrated (observed YES rate by decile of model probability: 6% at the 0 to 10% decile, 17%, 23%, 36%, then thin), yet every trade it picks loses: where the forecast disagrees with the market, **the market is right**. The market uses at least as much information as the NBS point forecast and its stated spread (other models, the newest runs, and real-time observations). The prediction (FALSIFIED, about 70%) held. No claim is made on the reverse (taking the market's side of every disagreement), because that pays the spread and fee on both legs and was not registered. Tries: +1 (running count about 4,704).

## Pre-registration: LOSSCL1 (2026-10-22), do favourite flips cluster in the same series

Owner: "keep going". Idea: volatility clusters, so after a recent favourite flip in a series the next hour may be riskier. A rule that skips L1 entries right after a loss in the same series would be cheap to run live, because the bot already records every outcome.

- **Data:** `feat1.build(markets, 360)` rows (L1, 6 minutes, band 0.88 to 0.97), all 18 series, 69 days, 24,792 entries. For each entry, RL = at least one earlier entry of the SAME series that closed between 3,600 and 1,800 seconds before this entry's close and settled as a loss (`gross < 0`). The nearest window (900 s before) is deliberately left out so the result is certainly known at the entry minute. The entry needs at least one earlier entry in that stretch to be classified; otherwise it is not used.
- **Groups (both known at the entry minute):** RL and NOT_RL. Each group from its own entries, compared per day (day-clustered). Count before registering (features only): with the 4-window stretch there were 2,014 RL and 17,173 NOT_RL; the 3-window stretch used here has fewer, the run will print the exact number and it must be at least 1,000 for the claim to count.
- **Claim:** NOT_RL minus RL mean net per contract >= +1.0c with day-clustered z >= 2.0; RL n >= 1,000 over >= 10 days; same sign in both halves and under the x1.2 fee stress; same sign in at least 2 of the months present with 200 or more RL entries; placebo (100 random relabels of the same group sizes) 95th percentile of diff z below the observed.
- **Prediction (now):** +0.8c; honestly uncertain, because flips of different 15 minute windows are mostly independent given the same price band.
- **FALSIFIED** if diff < +0.3c or z < 1.0; otherwise NOT_ENOUGH_DATA unless every condition holds.
- **Information only:** the same with the market-wide version (any series, any loss in the stretch); loss rates of both groups.
- Tries: +1 (running count about 4,705). Run once: `python -m scalper.losscl1 run`.

### LOSSCL1 result (2026-10-22, run once): FALSIFIED, no clustering of flips within a series

Same series: RL 1,527 entries (loss rate 6.29%, +0.42c) against NOT_RL 15,157 (6.54%, +0.14c); NOT_RL minus RL **-0.26c, z -0.37** (needed +1.0c and z 2.0). Halves -0.55c and -0.01c; the loss rates are the same, so a flip in the last hour tells nothing about the next one. The prediction (+0.8c) was wrong in size and sign, so the rule is dead. The market-wide version (information only, not a claim): RL 11,532, NOT_RL 13,175, difference -0.93c, z -2.40, wrong sign for the idea and almost half of all entries are "RL" (any of 18 series lost in the stretch), so it mostly marks busy hours, not volatility. Not pursued. Tries: +1 (running count about 4,705).

The main session built the recorder as PR #465 (not merged when this was written; the owner merges). Honest limits from the sandbox run: about 13% of polls refused with 429 on a shared IP; scheduled jobs start late, so some windows are missed (the coverage file counts them). Nothing changes any trade.

### Pre-registration: RECORD1 (written 2026-10-22 before any real recorder file has been read)

Question: do Kalshi quotes lag the spot index in the last minute, so that the spot-implied settlement probability beats the quote by more than fee plus a margin?

- **Index proxy:** each second, the median of the latest price of Coinbase, Kraken and Bitstamp for the asset (an exchange whose last update is older than 5 s is dropped; at least two exchanges are needed or the second is skipped).
- **Model (fixed now):** the market settles on the average of the index over the last 60 seconds before the close (the strike is in `quotes.csv`). With `s` seconds left and the index `S_t` at the decision second: the known part is the sum of the index values for the seconds of the final 60 s window already elapsed (none if `s > 60`); the rest is `S_t` plus a driftless random walk with per-sqrt-second volatility `sigma` taken from the standard deviation of one second index changes over the previous 300 s. For `m` seconds still to run inside the final window the average of the future part has variance `sigma^2 * m / 3`, scaled by `(m/60)^2`; if `s > 60` the whole average has variance `sigma^2 * ((s - 60) + 20)`. P(YES) is the normal probability that the 60 s average is above the strike.
- **Decision times:** the first poll at or after `s` = 60, 45, 30 and 15 seconds before the close; one trade per market, the earliest `s` that qualifies. Buy YES if `p - ask - fee >= 0.03`; buy NO if `(1 - p) - (1 - bid) - fee >= 0.03`; fee 7% x price x (1 - price). Only polls with `ask_size` (or the matching side's size) of at least 5 contracts count, so the trade is fillable at a small size. Held to settlement, 1 contract.
- **Claim:** mean net per contract >= +2.0c; day-clustered z >= 3.0; at least 300 trades over at least 10 days; same sign in both halves by date and under the x1.2 fee stress; positive in at least 3 of the 5 assets; and the recorder's clock offset within 100 ms where `clock.csv` has a value.
- **FALSIFIED** if there are at least 300 trades and the mean is below +0.5c or z below 1.0; **NOT_ENOUGH_DATA** if fewer than 300 trades or 10 days; **NOT_YET_FALSIFIED** only if every condition holds. A pass is a lead, never a switch: it still needs a separate order latency and fill test.
- **Prediction (now):** FALSIFIED (about 75%). Market makers are fast; I expect the quotes to track the index within a cent, as in the kill criterion of the recorder spec.
- **Information only:** the lag (seconds after a 3 bp index move until `yes_bid` or `yes_ask` moves by 1c); coverage (windows caught); share of polls with 429.
- Tries: +1 (running count about 4,707). Reader and runner: `python -m scalper.record1` (written after the first real files exist, with a test, before any run).

## Pre-registration: SCAN1 (2026-10-23), mine the recorded history for rules, then test them on days the mining never saw

Owner: "scan our recorded data and search for patterns or themes, certain rules that may populate more often than others". "Recorded data" is two things: the 69 days of one-minute Kalshi candles (24,792 L1 entries at 6 minutes across 18 series, all in the repo's databases) and the new live recorder (only 25 windows so far, far too thin to mine; the recorder is read by RECORD1 and will be scanned the same way once it has weeks). SCAN1 mines the candle history, and because mining thousands of rules always finds good-looking ones, the rules are chosen on the first 46 days and tested once on the last 23.

- **Conditions (fixed now, all known at the entry minute):** price (<0.92, 0.92 to 0.95, >=0.95); spread (<=1c, >1c); `rise3` (below -0.02, -0.02 to 0.02, 0.02 to 0.10, above 0.10); `rng5` (<0.10, 0.10 to 0.25, 0.25 to 0.45, >0.45); minutes already in band `tib` (0 to 1, 2 to 4, 5 or more); lowest earlier mid `dip` (<0.50, 0.50 to 0.75, >=0.75); series class (Bitcoin/Ethereum; other crypto: SOL, XRP, DOGE, BNB, HYPE, NEAR, ZEC; metals: gold, silver, platinum, palladium, copper; energy: WTI, natural gas; FX: EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY); side (yes, no); close hour block in UTC (six blocks of four hours); weekend or weekday.
- **Rules:** every conjunction of 1, 2 or 3 conditions from different features (about 4,500). Enumerated count is printed by the run.
- **Mining (first 46 days only):** a rule needs at least 400 entries; score = mean net per contract minus one standard error; keep the **top 10**.
- **Test (last 23 days, once):** the union of entries matched by any of the 10 rules against all other test entries, each group from its own entries, compared per day (day-clustered). **Claim:** difference >= +1.0c, z >= 2.0, union >= 600 test entries, the same sign in both halves of the test days and at the x1.2 fee, and at least 6 of the 10 rules individually above the rest of the test. FALSIFIED if difference < +0.3c or z < 1.0; NOT_ENOUGH_DATA otherwise unless every condition holds.
- **Prediction (now):** FALSIFIED (about 80%): mined rules usually shrink to nothing. If any survive I expect the firm and flat style conditions (low `rng5`, low `rise3`) and high price, the lead that is already known.
- **Themes (information, not a claim):** among the top 100 train rules, how often each condition appears; the rules with the largest support whose train net is at least +1c ("populate more often"); each of those on the test days.
- Tries: +10 (the 10 rules scored on the test days); the mining over about 4,500 rules is the search itself and is why only 10 reach the test (running count about 4,717). Run once: `python -m scalper.scan1 run`.

### SCAN1 result (2026-10-23, run once): NOT_ENOUGH_DATA, a near miss with themes

24,792 entries; train = first 46 days (to 2026-09-20), test = last 23 days. 4,504 rule instances seen, 1,911 with at least 400 train entries. Top 10 by train score; their union on the test days: 2,126 entries against 7,168 for the rest: **+1.07c, z 1.86**, halves +1.39c and +0.79c, fee stress +1.07c, **8 of 10 rules above the rest**. The claim needed z 2.0, so the word is NOT_ENOUGH_DATA, not falsified. Full table in `studies/scan1_result_2026-10-23.txt`. Note the test days are weaker than the train days: the rest of the test earns about -0.25c.

Themes (information only):
- **Hour of day dominates the top 100 train rules** (16 to 19Z in 29 of them, 20 to 23Z, 04 to 07Z) but is **not stable**: the 16 to 19Z rules, best on train (+3.0c to +3.7c), were -1.66c, -1.54c, -0.12c and +0.54c on the test days, while the 20 to 23Z rules held (+1.43c, +2.12c) and 04 to 07Z held (+1.09c). Time-of-day is mostly mined noise.
- Other conditions recurring in the top 100: `dip` 0.50 to 0.75, side yes, weekday, `spread <= 1c`, `rng5` 0.10 to 0.25, price 0.92 to 0.95, `rise3` 0.02 to 0.10.
- **Rules that populate most (largest support, train net >= +1c)** mostly faded to about zero on the test days (`rng5` 0.10 to 0.25: -0.14c; `rise3` 0.02 to 0.10: -0.11c), **except `spread <= 1c AND tib 2 to 4`: train 3,931 entries at +1.14c, test 2,365 at +1.03c**, against about -0.25c for the rest of the test. Tight spread (a liquid market) and 2 to 4 minutes already in the band is the only broad rule that carried over. It was picked after seeing the test days, so the test days no longer count for it.

## FILLIMP1 (2026-10-23), INFORMATION ONLY, no claim, no verdict, no try: do favourites that got cheaper before the order lose more often

Hypothesis from the live record (see "Slippage request" above): a fill cheaper than the seen quote means the favourite's price fell before the order, and those fills lose more often. The history only has one-minute candles, so this is a rough version: decision at the candle ending 360 s before the close (the L1 entry, `feat1`), a one-minute gap, fill at the ask of the candle ending 300 s before the close, under the live immediate-or-cancel rule (limit = the decision ask: the order fills only if the next ask is no higher; fill price = the next ask). Improvement = decision ask minus next ask, in buckets: no fill (ask rose), 0, 0 to 1c, 1c to 3c, above 3c. Per bucket: entries, loss rate, mean net per contract at the fill price (no-fills: net had it filled at the decision ask), and the exact tail against the pooled loss rate of the filled entries. Nothing is concluded from it; a pattern would only be written up as a forward claim on the live export (the main session was asked for that table).

### FILLIMP1 result (2026-10-23, information only): the price move after the decision predicts the outcome

24,791 L1 entries at 6 minutes, fill one minute later under the immediate-or-cancel rule (limit = the decision ask). Fixed a tail calculation overflow in `fillimp.py` (tool bug, no change to the analysis). Table:

| Next-minute ask against the decision ask | Entries | Loss rate | Net per contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rose (no fill at the limit) | 16,734 | **3.66%** | +3.00c had it filled at the decision ask |
| Equal | 1,269 | 5.75% | +0.59c |
| 0 to 1c cheaper | 1,071 | 5.88% | -0.04c |
| 1c to 3c cheaper | 1,966 | 8.44% | -0.40c |
| More than 3c cheaper | 3,751 | **19.19%** | **-1.56c** |

The filled entries (8,057) lose 12.68%. A favourite whose price keeps falling after the decision loses much more often than one whose price rises; the gradient is monotone and the last bucket is far from the pooled rate (tail p 0.000). **Caveats that matter:** (1) this uses the next minute's price, so it is a diagnostic of what a stale decision costs, not a rule one could apply in advance; (2) the live gap between the quote used for the decision and the order is not a minute (the main session said the latest candle can be up to 150 s old, and the order itself takes under a second), so the live fills are a milder version: the live fills lost 5.7% held to settlement, not 12.7%, and the live unfilled orders did worse than the fills (LIVE3), the opposite of this table, because the history's gap is longer; (3) one period, no holdout. The implementable question is: **if the bot re-reads the live ask just before sending and the ask is already lower than the candle quote it decided on by more than about 2c, does that order lose more often?** That is exactly what the table requested from the main session answers on the live export (fills by improvement bucket). If it shows the same gradient, it becomes a pre-registered forward claim on the next export (a "fresh quote check"), a protective rule with no new risk, not a source of income. Tries: none counted (information only).

Improvement = how much cheaper the fill was than that book (YES: seenAsk - avgFill; NO: avgFill - seenBid).

| Improvement | Fills | Losses | P/L | Exited | Tail p (vs 7.0% pooled) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 or worse | 171 | 9 (5.3%) | +$15.72 | 7 | 0.85 |
| 0 to 1c | 119 | 7 (5.9%) | -$10.93 | 6 | 0.73 |
| 1c to 3c | 58 | 5 (8.6%) | -$7.84 | 5 | 0.38 |
| **over 3c** | **25** | **5 (20.0%)** | **-$9.06** | 3 | **0.027** |

Orders of 6 contracts or fewer: 4.3%, 4.9%, 7.9%, **26.7%** (4 of 15, tail p 0.015). Same direction as FILLIMP1 on the history (loss rate 19.2% in the more than 3c bucket against 5.8% at equal). If every over-3c fill had been sold into the bid seen about 0.8 s later, after both fees: +4.54c a contract, positive in all 25, +$5.80 against the -$9.06 actually realised; the 1c to 3c bucket would net +0.4c (77% positive), the smaller buckets lose to fees. One 12-contract Bitcoin loss (-$11.11) is a large part of the difference. Not a claim; the sample is 25 fills and the selection is over four buckets and three splits.

### Calibration across every price (2026-10-23, information only, no claim, no try)

All 18 series, 69 days, buy either side at its ask 360 s (or 600 s) before the close, held to settlement, fee included, net per contract by ask bucket (day-clustered z). The market is **calibrated at every price**: the win rate equals the ask within about 1c in every bucket, so every bucket below 0.90 loses the fee and spread (-0.7c to -4.4c at 600 s, z -2 to -12), the 0.90 to 0.95 bucket is about break-even (**+0.13c at 360 s, +0.69c at 600 s**), and 0.95 to 1.00 is +0.17c (360 s) and -0.87c (600 s). There is no mispriced price zone in these markets; the +0.1c to +0.7c at the top of the book is the whole unconditional favourite effect, and every larger edge found here came from conditioning (FLAT, the 10-minute entry), which has so far been fragile out of sample. The 10-minute entry beats 6 minutes in the 0.90 to 0.95 bucket (+0.69c against +0.13c).

### Trade tape (2026-10-23): a new data source, fetch running
Kalshi's public `/markets/trades` returns every trade with a microsecond timestamp, size (`count_fp`), price and the taker's side (`taker_outcome_side`). A Bitcoin 15 minute market prints thousands of trades per window (about 13,000 in the 5 minutes before the 6 minute decision; the whole market is millions of contracts). To keep it feasible: only the 2,684 L1-qualifying entries (Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, gold, SOL; markets closing in the last 21 days) and only the 2 minutes before the decision (`c-480` to `c-360`); per-market summaries are saved to `data/tape_flow.json` (taker contracts on YES and NO, the same for the last 60 s, trade count, largest trade), no outcome is looked at. Next step, after the fetch: count the groups by features only, then register TAPE1 (does the favourite-side share of taker flow predict the outcome beyond the price) before any outcome is read. Check scheduled; the fetch takes about 2 hours.

Main session reply on `rng5` (2026-10-23): from git, #460 merged at 14:59Z and #461 (`rng5`) at 15:07Z, so any deploy from main after 15:07Z carries it; the first observed row is 2026-10-22T15:24Z, so **the live FLAT sample starts at 2026-10-22T15:24Z** (the earlier 17:00Z figure was wrong). Blank `rng5` is by design: `riseFromCandles` sets it only if all six one-minute marks are finite, so an order whose six public-candle marks are not all present gets `rise3` without `rng5`. Count from 15:24Z (orders with `rise3`): 5 blank of 51: Bitcoin 4 of 10, XRP 1 of 6, none on Ethereum, gold, Dogecoin or natural gas; 0 of 31 at the 6 minute entry and 5 of 20 at the 10 minute entry. Blanks cluster in the 10 minute entries (the candles at that minute are thinner), so a FLAT rate over Bitcoin and XRP at 10 minutes is measured on about 70% of orders.

## Pre-registration: BTC1 (2026-10-23, before any outcome was split by the prior window), a new mindset for Bitcoin: the window is not independent of the one before it

Owner: Bitcoin's live record is poor; find an entirely new mindset and a strategy with a high profit factor. Every Bitcoin rule so far looked inside one window (price, rise, time in band, distance to strike). This asks the other question: **does the result of the window that just closed tell us anything about the next one?** Markets reset to a fresh strike each 15 minutes, so a market that prices each window as a fresh 50/50 would be missing any momentum or reversal between adjacent windows. KXBTC15M only, `load()` history (6,427 markets, 69 days), prior window = the market closing 900 s earlier, its settled result is known at the next window's open.

Four fixed groups, each tested against zero (not against each other):
- **AGREE:** the L1 entry (favourite 0.88 to 0.97, 360 s left, held) whose side equals the prior window's result (n 957).
- **DISAGREE:** the L1 entry whose side is opposite (n 1,001).
- **CONT:** at the open arm (the candle ending 780 s before close, about 2 minutes in), buy the side equal to the prior window's result at its ask, hold to settlement (n about 6,400).
- **FADE:** same candle, buy the opposite side.
Group sizes counted from features only. Fee 7%·p·(1-p) as live.

Claim per group (any one group can pass; tries +4, z bar 2.6 for four groups): n >= 300, mean net per contract >= +2.0c, day-clustered z >= 2.6 against zero, both halves of the days > 0, fee stress x1.2 > 0, and profit factor (sum of winning nets over sum of losing nets) >= 1.3. FALSIFIED for a group: mean < +0.5c or z < 1.0. Otherwise NOT_ENOUGH_DATA. A pass only registers a forward read on fresh days (the markets after 2026-10-13 are held back from this test: `load()` history only), never a trade.
Prediction (now): all four FALSIFIED. CONT and FADE cross a spread and a 1.75c fee at 50c, so they would need a 55% hit rate; AGREE and DISAGREE are L1 entries the market already prices as calibrated. If any passes, the first suspects are an open-arm quote that is stale and the prior result being leaked into the same day's cluster.
Run once: `python -m scalper.btc1 run`.

- CONT n 6,416: -1.87c, z -3.39, PF 0.92, loss 50.6%. FADE n 6,416: -2.31c, z -4.18, PF 0.90, loss 49.4%. At the open the next window is a coin flip (50.6% vs 49.4%); the loss is the spread plus fee. There is no momentum and no reversal between adjacent Bitcoin windows.

## Pre-registration: LAG2 (2026-10-23, before any of this data was scored), the one Bitcoin edge with a mechanism: Kalshi's trades against the spot price

Owner: "there's got to be some way to be profitable trading [the Bitcoin] market." Honest state: 60 price-path and volume rules have failed on Bitcoin (BTC1, IDEAS20, IDEAS20B), because the book already holds every fact the book itself shows. The only thing a Bitcoin 15 minute market can be slow at is the **outside** fact: the spot price that settles it. The market settles on the average of the final 60 seconds of the CF index; the recorder's first look found Kalshi quotes followed a 3 bp spot move within 20 s in only 10 of 22 jumps (median 4.6 s). If prices lag by seconds, a model that reads the spot can buy a side that is mispriced right now. RECORD1 will test this on quote data when 10 recorded days exist (about 2 weeks). LAG2 tests it **now** on history: Kraken's public trade history (per second last price) and Kalshi's public trades (price, time, taker side) for the last 12 days of Bitcoin markets (`lag2_fetch.py`, `lag2.py`).
**Model (fixed):** at 120, 90 and 60 seconds before the close, S = Kraken last price (carried forward up to 5 s); K = the market's strike; sigma = standard deviation of 10-second log returns over the previous 900 s, per sqrt(second); P(yes) = Phi( ln(S/K) / (sigma * sqrt(left - 40)) ) (the variance of the mean of the last 60 s). **Reference price** = the yes price of the latest Kalshi trade in the previous 15 s (no trade, no decision). **Signal:** buy yes if P - (reference + 1c) >= 0.07, buy no if (1 - P) - ((1 - reference) + 1c) >= 0.07; first qualifying decision per market. **Fill (conservative):** the price of the first trade after 2 s of latency, within 20 s, whose taker bought our side (what someone actually paid); no such trade, no fill. Held to settlement, fee 7% x p x (1-p), x1.2 at stress.
**Claim:** n >= 150 trades on >= 8 days; mean net >= +2.0c with day-clustered z >= 2.5; both halves of the days positive; stress positive; profit factor >= 1.3. FALSIFIED if mean < +0.5c or z < 1.0; otherwise NOT_ENOUGH_DATA (also if fewer than 150 trades result: the window is only 12 days, so a pass-by-size needs a longer window later). Tries +1.
**Prediction (now):** FALSIFIED (about 65%). Market makers react to spot in well under a second and my sigma is crude (Kraken is one of the index's venues, not the index). If it passes, the suspects are the fill model (trade prices that printed after the move, i.e. the trade itself already reflects spot) and the Kraken-to-index basis.
**Not claimed even on a pass:** the book thins fast near the close (size of at least 5 on the favourite side in 56% of windows at 60 s left, 12% at 15 s), so a lag edge would carry one or two contracts per window, not a ladder; and a pass here would still need the RECORD1 quote-level read before anything is proposed.
Run once after the fetches finish: `python -m scalper.lag2 run`.

- 30-day mean profit at k = 1 / 3 / 5 / 8 per series (5th percentile in brackets, single series): Dogecoin $14 / $42 / $71 / $113 ($4 / $12 / $21 / $32); natural gas $6 / $18 / $31 / $48 ($0.6 / $1.5 / $4 / $5); Bitcoin(10 min) $6 / $18 / $29 / $47 (-$1 / -$4 / -$7 / -$12); Ethereum $5 / $14 / $24 / $38 (-$6 / -$18 / -$29 / -$48).

### LAG2 result (2026-10-23, run once): NOT_ENOUGH_DATA, because the volatility input was missing for 93% of decisions
`LAG2: NOT_ENOUGH_DATA; markets with a tape 1,068, trades 15 on 8 days` (needed 150). 21 signals fired and all 21 were filled; 15 markets traded (first signal per market), 5 winners, mean +8.01c, **not a result** (n 15, below the registered minimum; printed after the run as a diagnostic, so it counts as seen).
**Why so few decisions.** Of 3,204 decisions (1,068 markets x 120, 90, 60 s), the spot price was missing in 288, the reference Kalshi trade in 0, and the volatility in **2,979 (93%)**. Kraken's XBT/USD prints a trade in only 40% of seconds, and the registered volatility needed all 91 points of a 10 second grid over 900 s, each carried forward at most 5 s: almost never true. This is a defect in my estimator for a sparse venue, not a finding about the market. The spot model itself was scored on only 225 decisions (median |model minus last trade| 0.2c, 90th percentile 7.5c, 99th percentile 15.2c; informational).
Honest status: LAG2 neither passed nor failed. A repair (LAG2B: volatility from the available grid points scaled by the gap, at least 45 of 91, everything else unchanged) would be registered before scoring the other 2,979 decisions, with the 15 trades above disclosed as seen, tries +1. Not run: the owner paused research on 2026-10-23. Tries for LAG2: +1 counted.

## Pre-registration: LAG2B (2026-10-23, before the other 2,979 decisions were scored), LAG2 with a volatility estimator that works on a sparse feed

Owner picked "2" (run the repair). LAG2 returned NOT_ENOUGH_DATA because Kraken prints a trade in only 40% of seconds and the registered estimator needed all 91 points of the 10 second grid. **One change, nothing else:** the volatility is `sqrt( sum of squared log returns between consecutive grid points that have a price / sum of the time gaps between them )`, using at least 45 of the 91 grid points (a price carried forward at most 5 s, as before). Spot, reference trade, model P(yes), signal threshold (0.07 after a 1c half-spread), fill model (first trade after 2 s whose taker bought our side, within 20 s), fee, claim (n >= 150 on >= 8 days, mean >= +2.0c, z >= 2.5, both halves and stress positive, PF >= 1.3), kill criteria (FALSIFIED if mean < +0.5c or z < 1.0) and the same 1,068 markets are unchanged.
Disclosure: the 15 trades from LAG2 (5 winners, +8.01c) were printed before this repair; the repair uses no outcome. Tries +1 (LAG2B). Prediction (now): FALSIFIED (about 65%, unchanged): with sparse Kraken ticks the volatility is itself noisy, and market makers track spot to within a cent (the median gap between the model and the last trade was 0.2c).
Run once: `python -m scalper.lag2 runb`.

The yearly and daily touch series have no settled history. **The touch markets are the most liquid, but only 3 monthly events (Aug, Sep, Oct) have settled, so any bias there rests on 3 independent months and cannot be tested.** The hourly ladders are too thin per strike to fill.
**Quick look 1, a market-maker style entry (resting bid on the favourite side, filled only when a taker sells to it; the 112 s tape window of 1,068 Bitcoin markets, 12 days; optimistic fill rule: a taker trade at or below our bid; maker fee at the full taker fee or one quarter):** band 0.88-0.97: 127 fills of 237 quotes, **-1.1c to -1.5c a contract (z -0.5 to -0.7), loss rate 8.7%**; band 0.80-0.93: 145 fills, **-8.4c to -8.9c (z -3.4 to -3.7), loss rate 21%**. A resting bid is filled mostly when the price is falling through it, so it buys the losers (adverse selection, as FILLIMP found for live fills). Passive entry on the favourite is worse than taking, not better.
**Quick look 2:** none other run. Not tested because the data does not exist or cannot be filled: monthly touch pricing, hourly-ladder model trades.
**Honest list of strategy types left for Bitcoin and Ethereum** (see the owner message): (1) the 9 minute early entry (EARLY540, forward, 2026-11-12); (2) quote-level spot lag (recorder, about 10 days of recording); (3) taker-flow rules (tape, queued); (4) the hour-close and absorption leads (HOUR3-F, ABSORB-F, forward); (5) drop them and spend their slot on XRP, Dogecoin and gold.

## Slot contention: Bitcoin and Ethereum take the single crypto order from XRP and Dogecoin (2026-10-23; information from the build session plus a history replay, no try, no claim)

Build session (code on main, read-only answers): candidates are tried in `L1_SERIES` order (gold, Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Dogecoin, AUD/USD, USD/CAD, natural gas); Bitcoin, XRP and natural gas decide at about 10 minutes left, Ethereum and Dogecoin at about 6 minutes; `cryptoTaken[window]` and `recentList` give one capped crypto order per window (a filled order holds the window, an unfilled one does not). So a 1-contract Bitcoin order at 10 minutes takes the slot from a 3-contract XRP order at the same tick, and any filled Bitcoin or XRP order at 10 minutes blocks Ethereum and Dogecoin at 6 minutes. Dogecoin is the most exposed (last in the list and last in time).
**History replay (7,393 windows, 79 days, XRP and Dogecoin 3 contracts, Bitcoin and Ethereum 1, every qualifying L1 favourite assumed filled, history edges assumed to persist; sequential: 10 minute tick Bitcoin then XRP, then 6 minute tick Ethereum then Dogecoin):**
- Current order: **$102.34** (Bitcoin 711 orders +$15.1, Ethereum 1,826 +$18.6, XRP 591 +$40.5, Dogecoin 996 +$28.1).
- Same ticks, **XRP before Bitcoin and Dogecoin before Ethereum**: **$162.65** (+$60.31, +59%): XRP 1,005 orders, Dogecoin 1,870, Bitcoin 297, Ethereum 952.
- Drop Bitcoin and Ethereum entirely: **$156.77** (+$54.43): XRP 1,005, Dogecoin 1,973.
So the reorder (a list order change only) recovers about all of what dropping would, and keeps Bitcoin and Ethereum for the windows XRP and Dogecoin leave empty. Caveats: perfect fills, no live-record check (the build session cannot read the order records; the owner's export can), history edges assumed, and Dogecoin's 6 minute entry still loses a window to a filled XRP or Bitcoin order at 10 minutes (so the 6 minute tick is where Dogecoin remains exposed).

This is the list, backtested once, with the multiple-comparison cost paid up front. `src/scalper/ideas100.py`; Bitcoin and Ethereum 15 minute markets pooled (7,393 each, 2026-08-06 to 2026-10-23); candles carry bid, ask, volume, open interest; the market table carries the strike. Each rule is an entry filter applied to the coin's favourite at **two entries: E540** (9 minutes out, favourite 0.80-0.93) and **L1360** (6 minutes out, 0.88-0.97), held to settlement: 100 rules x 2 = **200 tries** (running count about 5,040).
**The 100 rules, in 15 families (not tried before in these forms):** time of day (8 three-hour blocks of the close) and weekday (7); quartiles, cut at the entry's own baseline features (no outcomes), of the favourite's drift since the first candle, drawdown from its peak, realised volatility of its mid, open-interest growth and open-interest level (20); path shape (flip counts 0, 1, 2, 3 or more; share of up-minutes at least 70% or at most 30%; last three minutes all up or all down) (8); results in the previous 8 and 4 windows (6); cross-asset (the other coin's drift since open stronger, weaker or the same, on each side; the other coin's price on our side at least 3c higher or lower) (8); candle microstructure (the ask fell back 2c from its high; the bid bounced 2c from its low; spread at least 2c) (3); the strike's move against the previous window against each side (4) and whether the previous window reversed or stayed clean in its last two minutes (2); stale quotes and spread extremes (4); volume tilt up or down (2); minute of the hour (3); side (2); last-minute move up or down (2); dip below 50c or never below 70c (2); avoid-lists (not 00-06 UTC, not weekend, not the US open) (3); time above 0.80 (2); the four quarters of the entry band (4); side x session (8) and side x weekend (2). Thresholds were fixed after counting entries only; counts were checked before the run: all 200 cells have discovery n of at least 150 and confirmation n of at least 70 except 17 (DD_Q2 and Q3, UPSHARE_LE30, LAST3_DOWN, YES8_LE2_FAVNO, SPREAD_GE2, PRIOR_REVERSED, STALE_GE2 at both entries, FLIPS_0 at the 6 minute entry), which come out NOT_ENOUGH_DATA by construction.
**Split and bars (fixed now):** discovery = the days before 2026-09-27, confirmation = the days from it. A rule is scored against the same coin's own baseline for the same entry in the same period (net and stress minus that coin's all-entries mean), because Bitcoin and Ethereum already earn a little with no rule. NOT_YET_FALSIFIED needs ALL of: discovery adjusted mean >= +1.5c with day-clustered **z >= 3.0** (raised from 2.5 for 200 tries: about 0.27 false discoveries expected, and about 0.014 after the confirmation bar), confirmation adjusted mean >= +1.0c with z >= 1.65, stress positive in both, raw profit factor >= 1.3, both coins above their own baseline. FALSIFIED if the all-days adjusted mean is under +0.5c or z under 1.0; otherwise NOT_ENOUGH_DATA. Run once: `python -m scalper.ideas100 run`.
**What happens to a survivor (fixed now):** it is a candidate only. It gets a forward claim on markets closing from 2026-10-24 on (bars as the confirmation bars, n at least 150), read with the other forward claims (2026-11-12), and meanwhile runs as a paper lane. A live deployment at 1 contract in its own lane, with the kill rules of the EARLY540 proposal, is a proposal to the owner after the forward read, not before.
**Prediction (now):** zero survivors (about 85%); if one appears the likeliest is a side-by-session cell, which would itself be a warning about overfitting.

Why start-50-and-halve looks as good as flat 9 even though it averages only 5.4 contracts: the 85 gold entries that followed a loss averaged +3.72c a contract against +1.6c overall (sampling noise at n 85; the standard error is about 2.4c), and the large orders land on exactly those; the profit parity is luck of 85 trades, not a feature of the schedule. Book depth is unmeasured at this size (the recorder saw at least 5 contracts on the favourite side in 54% of windows 60 s before the close). Nothing here is a try; no change proposed.

## Information: how much size has actually filled at the 6 to 10 minute look (2026-10-24; owner: measure depth before testing a bigger gold ceiling; no try, no claim)
**The recorder cannot answer it:** it polls only the last 150 seconds of each window (its files start about 150 s before the close) and only the top of the book; the 6 and 10 minute looks are not in it, and gold is not among the recorded series. **Live fills can.** From the owner's exports (373 filled orders with the quote seen at decision, to 2026-10-22, plus the 86 new orders to 2026-10-23): price paid minus the ask seen at decision, by order size, filled orders only: **gold** 2-4 contracts n 26 mean -0.90c (worst +0.4c); 5-8 n 40 mean -0.15c (worst +0.8c); **9-12 n 41 mean -0.50c (worst +0.9c)**; other series 9-12 n 100 mean -0.78c (worst +0.7c), 13 or more n 5 mean -1.14c (worst +0.0c). **No filled order of any size paid 1c or more above the ask it saw.** Orders are all or nothing in these records: gold orders of 4 to 7 contracts in the new export were filled fully or not at all (none partly filled; 7 of 11 four-contract orders and 4 of 7 five-contract orders filled, the others lost the price rather than the depth). The fills are slightly better than the ask seen (the price-improvement and adverse-selection pattern of FILLIMP), not worse.
Reading: up to about 12 contracts the book at these looks has shown no depth penalty; above 13 contracts there are only 5 fills, so nothing is known there. The replay's 1c to 2c of extra cost past 10 contracts (S2b) is therefore harsher than anything seen up to 12 and untested beyond. The binding limits on size are the risk rules (the 5.5% window cap, 12% stop, loss per order), not the book, up to about 12 contracts.

It is worth taking only if the edge is as good as measured (gold's live record: 142 trades, +$33, profit factor 2.7); if the loss rate drifts to its upper bound the same ceiling loses faster than it earns (at 20, 11% of 30 day paths end more than $100 down). Depth is not the limit up to about 12 contracts (previous section); above that it is untested. Not a try; no change proposed.

**Proposed ladder gate (for the owner; nothing built):** a series earns one ladder step (one more contract per order, at most one step a week, down at once after a stop) when ALL of: at least 100 live fills at its current size; net above $0 at that size; loss rate at or under 6.0% (break-even is about 6.8%); mean price paid minus the ask seen at or under +0.3c for its size band; and the new size stays at or under 1% of its median two-minute volume (XRP 48, Dogecoin 23, natural gas 18, Ethereum 106, gold 195). Today only gold qualifies. The first other candidate to earn one is XRP, then Dogecoin; natural gas and Dogecoin are capacity-capped at about 20 contracts per order; Bitcoin and Ethereum smooth entries are too few to matter in dollars.

**Did losers reach 98c or 99c?** 23% of losers had a bid high of at least 0.98 before the last minute and 10% at least 0.99 (54% at least 0.95); winners: 94% reached 0.98 and 88% 0.99. By series, losers reaching 0.98: gold 19%, XRP 21%, Dogecoin 25%, Ethereum 26%, Bitcoin 22%. **Take profit** (sell the first time the bid high reaches T, fill 0.5c under T, fees both legs, otherwise hold): hold +1.10c; TP 0.96 -1.01c; **TP 0.97 -0.51c; TP 0.98 +0.02c; TP 0.99 +0.36c** (differences against hold -2.11c, -1.61c, -1.09c, -0.74c). A take profit gives up about 2c on nearly every winner to rescue about a quarter of the losers; it would need about 45% of losers to touch the level to break even. **When do the losers turn** (seconds before the close when the side's mid first fell under 50c): last minute 21%, 1 to 2 minutes left 29%, 2 to 3 minutes 20%, 3 to 4 minutes 18%, 4 to 5 minutes 9%, 5 to 6 minutes 3%: no fixed time, median about 2 minutes left, and 70% of the collapses happen in the last 3 minutes. **Timed stops** (sell if the bid is under X at N minutes left): at 4, 3 and 2 minutes left with X from 0.60 to 0.85 every variant is below hold by 0.10c to 0.35c (4 min X 0.60 +1.01c, 3 min X 0.70 +0.91c, 2 min X 0.80 +0.80c, against +1.10c). Reading: a loser looks like a winner until late, so neither a level nor a clock separates them in time; the lever is entry quality, not exits (the live 25c rule sells only what has nearly lost).

## Pre-registration: QUIRK1, does any series resolve one way more often than its opening price says (written 2026-10-25 before any result; 36 tries, running count about 5,240)

**Idea.** Settlement quirks (ties at the strike, a settlement average that lags spot, coarse price steps on low-priced or FX series) would show up as a series whose outcomes lean one way against the price paid for that side at the start of the market. This is not a price-and-time rule: it asks whether any series is mispriced at its open.

**Rule.** For each of the 18 series, at the first candle (about 14 minutes left), buy YES at its ask on every market (side "yes"), and separately NO at 1 minus its bid (side "no"). Hold to settlement. Fee as everywhere (7%·p·(1-p)). 36 tries.

**Pass bar (all must hold).** On the older half of the days (discovery): net per contract of +1.0c or more and day-clustered z of 3.0 or more. On the newer half (confirmation): same sign, net above 0. The 36-try bar is z 3.0, not 2.1.

**Prediction.** None passes. Expected net per contract is about -2.5c to -3c (fee about 1.75c plus half the spread), and the price at the first candle already equals the probability. **Kill.** Any cell failing the bar is `FALSIFIED`; a cell passing discovery only is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`; a cell passing both is `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` and goes to a forward read on new days. Nothing here means "trade".

## Result: QUIRK1 (run once on 2026-10-25)

79 days, split at 2026-09-14. 28 of the 36 cells had enough days in both halves; **none passed** (the best discovery cells were XRP yes -0.78c z -0.9 and BNB yes -1.09c z -1.4; every other cell was -1.5c to -5.5c, most with z beyond -2, and every confirmation half was negative). The other 8 cells (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY, palladium and platinum, both sides) have no days in the older half and are `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. 28 `FALSIFIED`, as predicted: buying either side at the first candle loses the fee plus the spread on every series, so no series leans one way against its opening price. Count: 36 tries added, about 5,240. Nothing to build.

## Pre-registration: IV1, option-style fair value from implied volatility (written 2026-10-25 before any Deribit data was fetched and before any result; 2 tries, running count about 5,242)

**The question (owner's).** H7, L8, L9, N1 and N2 priced the 15 minute market as a digital option using **realised** volatility (the last 60 minutes of spot) and were `FALSIFIED`. What has never run is the same fair value with **implied** volatility: Deribit's DVOL index (the 30 day implied volatility of Bitcoin and Ethereum options, public, keyless, 1 minute history) was listed as N7 and marked "could not be run" for lack of data. It can be fetched now. The new thing is the sigma: forward-looking, from option prices, not from the last hour of moves.

**Data.** `data/iv1.sqlite`: Deribit `BTC-PERPETUAL` and `ETH-PERPETUAL` 1 minute bars (spot proxy; the perpetual trades within a few hundredths of a percent of the index, so the distance is measured against the perpetual's own price at the market's open, which removes the basis) and DVOL 1 minute values for both, over the same days as the existing Bitcoin and Ethereum 15 minute markets. Disclosed: the strike is not stored in the candle data, so the proxy for it is the perpetual's close at the open minute; this adds noise to the distance, which can only hide an edge, not create one.

**Model, fixed.** At the candle ending 6 minutes before the close, S = the perpetual's close at that minute, K = its close at the open minute, sigma_iv = DVOL/100 divided by the square root of 525,600 (per minute), tau = 5 minutes before the last minute begins, and the settlement average over the last minute gives variance sigma_iv squared times (5 + 1/3). p(YES) = Phi(ln(S/K) / (sigma_iv x sqrt(5.333))). The comparator `p_rv` uses the sample standard deviation of the last 60 one minute log returns instead (information only).
- **Entry (the tried one).** Buy YES at its ask if p - ask - fee exceeds 0.02; buy NO at 1 minus the bid if (1 - p) - price - fee exceeds 0.02. Real two sided book only. One observation per market, held to settlement, 7%·p·(1-p) fee.
- **Judged by the common bar:** at least 300 entries, day clustered z of 2.1 or more, positive in both halves (split by close time at the median), positive with fees x1.2. Verdict words only. Two tries: Bitcoin and Ethereum.
- **Information, decides nothing:** the Brier score of p_iv, of p_rv and of the market's own mid (0.5 x (bid + ask)) over all markets; if p_iv does not beat the market mid, the market already knows more than the option-implied volatility says.

**Prediction.** `FALSIFIED` for both. Brier: market mid best, p_iv worst. Reason, stated now: DVOL is a 30 day average, flat across the day, while intraday volatility swings by a factor of two with the clock; a model that uses it will be most wrong exactly when it disagrees most with the market, so its largest "edges" will be its largest errors. Prior for a pass: under 5%.

## Result: IV1, implied-volatility fair value (run 2026-10-25; first read discarded for a lookahead bug, corrected read stands)

**Disclosure.** The first run showed Bitcoin +2.02c (z 3.46) and, on the realised-sigma comparator, +3.57c (z 7.08). A result that strong for an idea whose siblings (H7, L8, L9) were `FALSIFIED` was treated as a bug until shown otherwise. It was one: Deribit stamps a bar with its start, so the bar stamped at the decision minute closes one minute later, and the model saw one minute of the future. Fixed (the last usable bar starts 60 s before the decision, the strike proxy and DVOL likewise; test T in `tests/test_iv1.py` now fails if a later bar is read), and the corrected run is the read. The first numbers are not evidence of anything. No rule, threshold or data changed between the two runs. Tries unchanged (2).

| Series | Entries | Net per contract | z | Halves | Fee x1.2 | Brier: p_iv / p_rv / market mid | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bitcoin | 5,423 of 7,308 | -0.97c | -1.64 | -0.67 / -1.28 | -1.18c | 0.1550 / 0.1476 / **0.1401** | `FALSIFIED` |
| Ethereum | 5,601 of 7,308 | -2.13c | -4.39 | -1.97 / -2.29 | -2.32c | 0.1477 / 0.1358 / **0.1289** | `FALSIFIED` |

Predicted, and it came out as predicted: the market's own mid is the best probability, the realised-volatility model is second and the implied-volatility model is worst on both series. The information-only realised-sigma entries also lose (Bitcoin -1.00c, Ethereum -1.31c). So an options-style fair value from implied volatility does not beat the price; the 15 minute market already prices distance and time better than a model that has Deribit's volatility. Code: `src/scalper/iv1.py`, data `data/iv1.sqlite` (not committed). Nothing to build.

## Pre-registration: TAPE20, who was trading in the two minutes before the 6 minute L1 decision (written 2026-10-25 before the tape download finished and before any outcome was split; 16 tries, running count about 5,260)

**The new information.** Everything so far read prices and candles. The public trade tape (`/markets/trades`) says who crossed the spread: each trade has a `taker_outcome_side` and a size. Buyers of the favourite pushing into the window, one big print, or a burst of small retail-sized trades are things a candle cannot show. Counterparty for each: whoever is resting on the other side without seeing the flow.

**Data.** For each L1 entry (the favourite at 6 minutes left, band 0.88 to 0.97) on Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, gold and Solana markets of the last 21 days, every trade between 8 and 6 minutes before the close, aggregated into taker contracts per side, trade count, largest print, and the same for the last 60 seconds of the window (`data/tape_flow.json`, resumable download, `python -m scalper.tape20 run` reads it once).

**The 16 rules (each compares its entries with the REST of the same entries; thresholds fixed here, quartile cuts per series from the entries themselves, no outcome used).** Favourite-side taker share of contracts: BUY_PRESSURE at least 0.60; SELL_PRESSURE at most 0.40; LATE_BUY and LATE_SELL the same on the last 60 seconds; ACCEL and DECEL (last-60-second share minus first-minute share at least +0.20 or at most -0.20); ONE_SIDED_BUY at least 0.75; ONE_SIDED_SELL at most 0.25; BALANCED between 0.45 and 0.55. Size and count: BIG_PRINT (largest print at least 8 times the average), SMALL_TRADES (average at most 10 contracts), BUSY and QUIET (top and bottom quartile of trade count), HEAVY and LIGHT (top and bottom quartile of contracts), BURST (at least 60% of the trades in the last minute).

**Judging (the numbers in the code, fixed before the run).** Discovery on the first two thirds of the days, confirmation on the last third. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` needs the group's net per contract above the rest by at least +2.0c with day-clustered z of 2.0 or more on discovery, at least +1.0c with z 1.0 or more on confirmation, and positive with fees x1.2 on both. `FALSIFIED` if the all-day difference is under +0.5c or its z under 1.0. Fewer than 150 discovery or 60 confirmation entries is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. One run; a second is refused.

**Prediction.** At most one of the 16 passes by chance, and none survives a forward read. Prior for a real tape effect: under 10%. The price already reflects the trades; the tape's only chance is flow that arrives in the last minute of the window and has not moved the quote yet.

## Pre-registration: SEARCH5K, 5,000 Bitcoin and Ethereum rules from outside information, with a family-wise null (written 2026-10-25 before any new feature was fetched and before any rule was scored; 5,000 tries, running count about 10,260)

**Why this is different from IDEAS100 and the earlier rule searches.** Those used Kalshi's own candles. This search adds information the Kalshi price does not contain by construction: Deribit perpetual 1 minute bars with volume, funding rates, the DVOL implied-volatility index and its gap to realised volatility, the other asset's move (ETH for Bitcoin and the reverse), the clock, and the model distance of spot from the strike. And it is the first search with an honest family-wise error control: a permutation null for the maximum over all 5,000 rules, so "the best of 5,000" is compared with what the best of 5,000 looks like on shuffled outcomes.

**Universe.** L1 entries on Bitcoin and Ethereum 15 minute markets (the favourite at 6 minutes left, band 0.88 to 0.97, exactly as `feat1.build` makes them), about 78 days. A rule selects a subset of those entries; the question is whether the subset earns more than the other entries.

**Features (35, every one computed only from data stamped before the decision minute; a Deribit bar stamped T is usable only from T + 60 s).** Kalshi: entry price, spread, rise over 1, 3 and 5 minutes, 5 minute range, minutes in band (tib), earlier dip, last-minute volume, volume ratio to the minute before, flip count. Perpetual: signed (toward the favourite) return over 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes, realised volatility over 15 and 60 minutes and their ratio, last-5-minute volume against its trailing 24 hour distribution, 15 minute range, distance of spot from the strike proxy in sigma units, distance from the 60 minute high and low. Implied: DVOL level, 60 minute change in DVOL, DVOL minus realised volatility (annualised). Funding: the last funding rate and its change. Cross-asset: the other asset's signed 15 minute return, and whether it agrees with the favourite's direction. Time: UTC hour bucket (four), weekend flag, which quarter-hour slot, the US cash-open window (13:30 to 15:00 UTC). "Signed" features are measured in the direction of the favourite so they read the same for YES and NO entries.

**Rule grammar.** A condition is one feature in its bottom quartile, top quartile, below the median or above the median (cut points from the discovery days only; calendar features take their natural values). 35 features give about 140 single conditions; a rule is one condition or two conditions on two different features (AND). The 5,000 rules are the 140 singles plus 4,860 pairs drawn without replacement with a fixed seed (25102501) before any outcome is looked at.

**Splits by day.** Discovery: the first 60% of days. Confirmation: the next 20%. Holdout: the last 20%, read once, only for survivors.

**Scoring.** Each rule's group is compared with the rest of the same entries (difference in mean net per contract, fee included, same entries for both). A rule needs at least 150 discovery entries and 60 confirmation entries.

**The family-wise null.** On the discovery days, the outcomes (net per contract) are shuffled among entries of the same series and day, 300 times, and for each shuffle the largest plain Welch z over all 5,000 rules is recorded. That gives the null distribution of "the best of 5,000 by chance". Welch z for the screen (day-clustered z for the survivors).

**Pass bar (all must hold).** (1) Discovery difference at least +2.0c and discovery z above the 95th percentile of the null maximum. (2) Confirmation difference at least +1.0c with z at least 1.64. (3) Positive with fees x1.2 in discovery and confirmation. (4) Holdout difference above 0 with z at least 1.0. A rule that clears (1) to (3) and not (4) is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`; a rule that fails (1) is `FALSIFIED`. Verdict words only. Nothing here means "trade"; a survivor goes to a forward read on days after 2026-10-25.

**Prediction.** No rule clears (1). The maximum discovery z over the 5,000 rules lands inside the null distribution (it will look impressive in isolation, about 4 to 5, and the shuffled data will produce the same). Prior that at least one rule survives all four steps: 10%; if one does, it is most likely a smooth-climb relative (already live at 1 contract), so I will report how many survivors are just rewordings of it (rise, range and flip features).

**Limits, stated now.** The 5,000 rules share 35 features and 78 days, so they are far from independent and the effective number of tests is smaller than 5,000; I count 5,000 anyway. The perpetual is a proxy for the settlement index; the strike proxy is the perpetual at the open minute. Funding is published every 8 hours, so its "change" is a step, not a signal in the last minutes.

## Result: SEARCH5K (run once on 2026-10-25): FALSIFIED

4,558 Bitcoin and Ethereum L1 entries over 79 days (2,243 and 2,315); discovery 2,819 entries (before 2026-09-22), confirmation 918 (before 2026-10-08), holdout 821 (not opened: no rule reached it). 34 features, 131 conditions, 5,000 rules (4,576 with enough discovery entries). Corrections to the pre-registration text, none involving an outcome: the feature count was 34 (30 numeric and 4 calendar), the single-condition count 131.

**The null.** The best z over all 5,000 rules on shuffled outcomes had a median of **5.00**, a 95th percentile of **7.59** and a maximum of 13.42 over 300 shuffles. The best observed rule had z **6.14**, below even the null median-to-95th range top. **Zero rules** cleared step 1; zero cleared steps 1 to 3. A z of 6 out of 5,000 correlated rules is what chance alone produces.

**Top by discovery (information only):** `rv15 top quartile AND 12 to 18 UTC` +5.15c z 6.14 (confirmation +0.20c z 0.07); `rise3 bottom quartile AND quarter-hour slot 2` +4.65c z 5.32 (confirmation -3.00c); `range15 top quartile AND 12 to 18 UTC` +4.53c z 5.23 (confirmation +2.29c z 0.96); `ret15 top quartile AND 12 to 18 UTC` +4.45c z 5.02 (confirmation +3.44c z 1.43). Seven of the top ten contain the 12 to 18 UTC bucket. That bucket is also where gold, XRP and Dogecoin had no losses in 33 fills (order scan, 2026-10-25), so it is a single, simple, three-market-consistent observation; it is not a SEARCH5K result (the bucket alone did not clear the null). **No claim is registered from it here.** Implied volatility, funding, cross-asset moves and perpetual volume produced no rule that survived.

Count: 5,000 tries added, about 10,260. Code `src/scalper/search5k.py`, tests `tests/test_search5k.py`, result `data/search5k_result.txt`.

## Pre-registration: RT1, take the 99c and come back at 92c (written 2026-10-25 before any result; 2 tries, running count about 10,262)

**Idea (owner's).** Enter the L1 favourite, sell it the moment it touches 99c, and if it later dips back to 92c buy it again and sell at 99c again: scalp the same contract repeatedly instead of holding to settlement.

**Rule A (take 99).** Entries are the L1 entries (favourite ask 0.88 to 0.97 at 6 minutes left) on gold, XRP, Dogecoin (the paying series; Bitcoin and Ethereum shown for information). After the entry, the first later candle in which the bought side's bid high reaches 0.99 triggers a sell at 0.99 (taker fee 7%·0.99·0.01). Otherwise hold to settlement. Compared with holding every entry, on the same entries.

**Rule B (re-entry).** After rule A sold, the first later candle in which the same side's ask low is at 0.92 or lower triggers a buy at 0.92 (fee included); then sell at 0.99 on the first later candle with bid high 0.99, else hold to settlement.

**Fill assumption (flattering, stated).** A candle touch is not a fill: the bid high or ask low prints only if someone traded there. Every number here is an upper bound; a rule that does not win on touches cannot win on fills.

**Prediction.** A earns about 1c per entry LESS than holding: it gives up 1c on every winner (the 99c exit vs the 100c settlement, plus a second fee) and the reversals it saves after a 99c touch are almost nonexistent. B fires on under 3% of entries and loses. **Kill.** A: `FALSIFIED` if its net per contract minus hold's is 0 or below. B: `FALSIFIED` if its net is 0 or below or it has under 100 re-entries (`NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` then). Verdict words only. Run once.

## Pre-registration: RT2, reverse when a 99c favourite drops to 92c (written 2026-10-25 before any result; 1 try pooled, running count about 10,263)

**Idea (owner's).** RT1 found that buying the favourite back at 92c after it touched 99c lost about 11c a contract: the dip is usually a real reversal. The mirror image: buy the OTHER side when that happens.

**Event.** An L1 entry (favourite ask 0.88 to 0.97 at 6 minutes left). After the entry, the favourite's bid high reaches 0.99 in some candle (a touch). Then, in a LATER candle i, the favourite's ask low is 0.92 or less AND its closing bid is 0.92 or less (the dip is still there when the candle ends; this removes the "touch is not a fill" flattery). One event per market (the first).

**Trade.** At the close of candle i, buy the opposite side at its closing ask (1 minus the favourite's closing bid), at most 0.20 (a dearer opposite side is no trade). Hold to settlement. Taker fee 7%·p·(1-p). One order per market.

**Series.** Gold, XRP, Dogecoin, Bitcoin and Ethereum pooled (the candle history for the five); per series shown for information. 1 try pooled.

**Bar.** At least 200 events; mean net per contract above 0 with day-clustered z of 2.1 or more; positive in both halves of the days; positive with fees x1.2. Fewer than 200 events is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. Verdict words only.

**Prediction.** The mirror is only as good as the spread allows: the opposite side's ask is 1c to 2c above the favourite bid, and its loss rate must beat that. Expected gross about +8c, net after spread and fees about +2c to +4c with z about 1.5 on roughly 250 events: `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` or `FALSIFIED`. Prior for a pass: 15%. If it does pass, it is a bet that costs the opposite price (8c to 20c) to win 80c to 92c: a lottery-ticket shape, which is the shape the owner asked for. Run once.

## Pre-registration: BTCBOOK, two complete new Bitcoin strategies (written 2026-10-25 before any result; 4 tries, running count about 10,267)

**Why.** The owner asked for full strategies, not filters on L1. A strategy here means a thesis (who loses money), an entry, an exit, a size and a stop. Both below are structurally different from L1: neither buys "the favourite at 6 minutes". Simulated on the 79 day history with real closing quotes (no candle touches), taker fee on every buy, held to settlement (no exit fee).

**BK1, Sibling catch-up (cross-market relative value).** *Thesis:* Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and Dogecoin 15 minute markets close in the same minute and move together; when the others already price one side at 0.88 or more, a Bitcoin (or Ethereum) market still priced between 0.60 and 0.88 on that side has not caught up, and whoever quotes it is slow to read the siblings. *Entry (6 minutes left):* at least 2 of the other three crypto series have a favourite at 0.88 to 0.97 on the SAME side; the target series' ask on that side is 0.60 to under 0.88; buy it at its ask. *Exit:* hold to settlement. *Size:* 1 contract (a loss is 60c to 88c, so it needs a win rate above the entry price plus fee). *Kill:* FALSIFIED if net per contract is 0 or below or z under 2.1; also if the win rate is under the average price paid. *Tries:* 2 (target Bitcoin, target Ethereum).

**BK2, Streak fade and streak continuation (sequence behaviour).** *Thesis:* retail extrapolates (or fades) the last few windows; four straight same-direction windows should move the next window's opening price off 50 against what the next move does. *Entry (14 minutes left, the first candle):* the four previous consecutive 15 minute windows of the same series all settled the same way; fade = buy the other side at its ask; continue = buy the same side at its ask. *Exit:* hold. *Size:* 1 contract. *Kill:* same bar. *Tries:* 2 (fade, continue), Bitcoin only.

**Judging for all four.** At least 300 entries; day-clustered z of 2.1 or more (4 tries, so also reported against 2.5); positive in both halves; positive with fees x1.2. Verdict words only.

**Predictions (stated now).** BK1: `FALSIFIED`, win rate close to the price paid; the siblings are priced by the same makers at the same instant, so there is no lag to catch (win rate about 1 point below the price paid, net about -2c). BK2: `FALSIFIED` both ways; windows are independent coin flips and the opening price is 50c. Prior of any pass: 8%.

**Not testable with the data held, and what would unlock it.** (3) A market-maker strategy that earns the spread with resting orders: needs queue position and the full book history (the recorder holds only the last 150 seconds). (4) A news and event strategy (CPI, FOMC, large prints): needs a timestamped event calendar and tick-level spot; neither is held. (5) A two-leg hedge (the favourite plus the cheap underdog as insurance) is an insurance premium paid at the market price: expected value is the sum of the two legs' (negative) edges, so it needs no test to know it lowers variance and not expectancy.

## Result: BTCBOOK (run once on 2026-10-25): all four FALSIFIED

| Strategy | Entries | Net per contract | z | Halves | Fee x1.2 | Win rate vs price paid |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Pre-registration: FACT1, a factory of 4,230 complete strategies for Bitcoin and Ethereum with a Reality Check (written 2026-10-25 before any strategy was simulated; 4,230 tries, running count about 14,500)

**Owner's instruction.** Many full strategies for Bitcoin and Ethereum, replace the struggling ones, deploy what has an edge. A strategy is an **entry** (when, which side, which price band), an **exit** (hold, take profit, stop, or a time exit) and an optional **time-of-day gate**. Unlike SEARCH5K (which only filtered L1's favourite-at-6-minutes entries), this varies the entry time, the side and the exit.

**The grid (per asset, Bitcoin and Ethereum separately).**
- *Entry time (left):* 13, 11, 9, 7, 5, 4 and 3 minutes.
- *Side rule (9):* FAV50 (favourite's ask 0.50 to 0.70), FAV70 (0.70 to 0.88), FAV88 (0.88 to 0.97, L1's band); UND5 (underdog ask 0.03 to 0.12), UND20 (0.12 to 0.30); SPOT_UP-lo and SPOT_UP-hi (buy the side the perpetual's last 5 minutes moved toward, at least 3 basis points, ask 0.30 to 0.60 or 0.60 to 0.88); FADE-lo and FADE-hi (the opposite side, same bands).
- *Exit (up to 7):* hold to settlement; take profit when the closing bid reaches the entry ask +0.10, or +0.20; stop when it falls to the entry ask -0.10, or -0.20; sell at the close-of-candle bid at 4 minutes left (only if entered at 5 minutes or earlier) or at 2 minutes left. Exits read later closing quotes only, so a gap through a stop fills at the gapped price. A sell pays the 7%·p·(1-p) fee; settlement pays none.
- *Gate (5):* all hours; 00-06, 06-12, 12-18 or 18-24 UTC.
- *Valid combinations:* 47 entry-and-exit pairs x 9 side rules x 5 gates = 2,115 per asset, **4,230 in all**. One contract per entry, one entry per market.

**Data.** The same 79 days of Bitcoin and Ethereum 15 minute candles (closing bid and ask), Deribit perpetual bars for the spot-direction rules (bars usable only from their close, as in IV1 and SEARCH5K).

**Judging (the Reality Check, White 2000).** Daily profit and loss per strategy (one contract per entry, zero on days without entries). Discovery = first 60% of days. For each strategy, t = mean daily P&L over its standard error. The null is built by resampling discovery days with replacement 1,000 times, jointly for all strategies of one asset, centred on each strategy's own mean; the family-wise critical value is the 95th percentile of the maximum t over all strategies. **A strategy is a survivor only if** (1) its discovery t is above that critical value, (2) it has at least 150 discovery entries, (3) confirmation (next 20% of days) mean net per entry above 0 with t of 1.64 or more, (4) positive with fees x1.2 in both parts, (5) holdout (last 20%) mean above 0 with t of 1.0 or more. One run; a second is refused.

**Prediction.** No survivor on either asset (prior 10% that one asset has one). Reason: the price is the probability on every band, entry time and side, and every exit variant only changes the payoff shape, not the expected value; the fee (about 1.7c at 50c, 0.5c at 90c) is paid on every buy and on every sell. The largest discovery t among 2,115 will look good (about 3.5 to 4.5) and fall inside the null.

**What happens to a survivor.** It is a forward claim, not a deployment: it goes to the build session as a paper-trade log (1 contract, logging only) for 4 weeks, with kill rules registered before the first logged trade; live money only on the owner's direct word in the build session.
