79 days, 7,393 markets each; discovery 47 days, confirmation 16, holdout 16. Strategies with at least 150 discovery entries: Bitcoin 1,447, Ethereum 1,509.

- **Bitcoin:** best discovery t **4.59** against a Reality Check 95th percentile of **3.80** (median of the best-of-1,447: 2.96). One strategy above it: 9 minutes left, favourite 0.88 to 0.97, sell at 2 minutes left, 06:00 to 12:00 UTC, +4.85c on 154 entries. **Confirmation -0.04c (t -0.01): fails.** No survivor.
- **Ethereum:** best discovery t **3.94** against a critical value of **3.84** (median 2.98). Two above it. One passes confirmation: 7 minutes left, favourite 0.88 to 0.97, sell at 2 minutes left, 18:00 to 24:00 UTC: discovery t 3.87 (+2.86c, 328 entries), confirmation **+2.27c (t 1.97, 91 entries)**, holdout **-0.42c (t -0.19, 94 entries): fails.** `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` by the registered wording.
- **What appears:** every top strategy is L1's own band (0.88 to 0.97) entered a little earlier with a time exit or none, in one six-hour gate. No underdog (UND5, UND20), no spot-momentum, no fade, no 50% to 88% favourite strategy is near the top on either asset. Entering earlier than 6 minutes, selling before settlement and take-profit/stop exits add nothing the hold does not already have; the top rows with `hold`, `tp20` and `tp10` are the same trades.
- **Against chance:** three strategies above a 5% family-wise critical value across two correlated families is at the edge of what chance gives (about 10% to see one in either asset), and none held out. 4,230 tries added; running count about 14,500. Code `src/scalper/fact1.py`, tests `tests/test_fact1.py`.

## Pre-registration: PROG1, four portfolio-level strategies across all 18 series (written 2026-10-25 before any result; 4 tries, running count about 14,505)

**Owner's instruction (2026-10-25):** keep researching new ideas for the 15 minute markets until something has a true historical edge. The earlier searches asked "which side, price and time" on one series. These four ask what only a portfolio of all 18 series can ask: which series and which hour to trade, whether losses cluster across series, and whether the number of series with a tradable favourite says anything. Entries are L1's (favourite ask 0.88 to 0.97 at 6 minutes left, `feat1.build`, all 18 series, about 79 days); the strategies decide which of them to take. All nets are per contract with the entry fee, held to settlement; stress is fees x1.2.

**P1, US-hours strategy.** Take only entries whose window closes 12:00 to 17:59 UTC. *Why:* informed US-session liquidity makes quotes sharper and reversals rarer (SEARCH5K and the live orders both point there). *Test:* adjusted net (each entry minus its series' own average) of those entries minus the rest, day-clustered z. *Pass:* difference at least +1.0c, z at least 2.5, positive in both halves of the days, at least 8 series individually positive, positive with fees x1.2. *Prediction:* +1.0c to +1.5c, z about 2, so `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`.

**P2, Cooling-off after a loss.** *Why:* losses cluster in shocks that hit many series at once (a macro move, a data release); the strategy skips every entry if any entry of the previous four windows (across all 18 series, taken or not) lost. *Test:* adjusted net of entries after four clean windows minus entries after at least one loss. *Pass:* same bar; the clean-window group must also have at least 60% of all entries. *Prediction:* no difference (|diff| under 0.5c): losses at 6 minutes are independent across windows.

**P3, Breadth.** *Why:* when many series show a tradable favourite in the same window the market is calm and trending; when only a few do, it is choppy. *Test:* breadth = the number of series with an L1 entry in the window; adjusted net of entries in the top third of windows by breadth minus the bottom third. *Pass:* same bar. *Prediction:* a small positive, z about 1.5.

**P4, Adaptive allocator (walk-forward slot selection).** *Why:* the live bot can only fill a few slots per window; choose the best candidate by what the history says about its series and its hour. *Rule:* for each window, among the L1 entries available, score each by the mean net of its (series, UTC 6 hour bucket) cell over the previous 14 days only (fewer than 30 earlier entries in the cell: score 0); take the single best entry if its score is above 0, otherwise nothing. First scored day: day 15. *Test:* the selected entries' mean net per contract, day-clustered z, and the same figure for the average candidate of the same windows (a no-skill pick). *Pass:* selected mean at least +1.5c and at least +1.0c above the average candidate, z at least 2.5, at least 300 selections, positive in both halves, positive with fees x1.2. *Prediction:* +0.5c to +1.2c, a little above the average candidate, z about 2: `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` or `FALSIFIED`. Honest note: gold's strength will pull the score towards gold, which already trades; the test is whether selection beats picking at random, not whether gold works.

**Judging.** Verdict words only. One run each; no variants. Tries: 4.

## Result: PROG1 (run once on 2026-10-25): P1 NOT_ENOUGH_DATA, P2 and P3 FALSIFIED (wrong sign), P4 NOT_ENOUGH_DATA

28,390 L1 entries, 18 series, 79 days. Adjusted net per contract (each entry minus its own series' average), difference between groups, day-clustered:

| Test | Group vs rest | Difference | z | Halves | Series positive | Verdict |

| P1 US-hours (window closes 12 to 18 UTC) | 7,230 vs 21,160 | +0.65c | +1.41 | +1.42 / -0.27 | 13 of 18 | `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` |
| P2 cooling-off (no loss in the previous 4 windows, any series) | 12,252 vs 16,138 | **-0.94c** | **-2.19** | -0.62 / -1.12 | 7 of 18 | `FALSIFIED` (wrong sign) |
| P3 breadth (top third by number of series with an entry vs bottom third) | 17,126 vs 6,864 | **-1.02c** | **-2.42** | -1.07 / -0.90 | 4 of 18 | `FALSIFIED` (wrong sign) |
| P4 adaptive allocator (one entry per window by its series and 6 hour cell, past 14 days) | 5,009 selections | +0.80c per contract against +0.15c for a random candidate | +2.76 | +1.02 / +0.58 | stress +0.71c | `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` (bar was +1.5c and +1.0c over the pool) |

**Reading.** Predicted: no effect from P2, a small positive from P3. Observed: both are NEGATIVE and about as large as the bar, in both halves: entries after a loss in the previous four windows, and entries in windows where few series have a tradable favourite, earn about 1c MORE. That is the opposite of "losses cluster". It has not been tested in that direction, so it is a lead, not a result. **Registered as forward claims, not scored yet (2 tries, running count about 14,507):** P2R and P3R, read once on markets closing from 2026-10-26 00:00 UTC only, bar: difference at least +1.0c with z at least 2.0 in the stated direction (any loss in the previous four windows, or breadth in the bottom third, better than the rest), positive in both halves, positive with fees x1.2, at least 8 series individually positive. P4's selection adds +0.65c per contract over a random pick (z 2.76, both halves positive) but earns less than gold alone (+1.60c) because it spreads over 18 series.

## Pre-registration: P5, a market-wide volatility state from outside data (written 2026-10-25 before any result; 2 tries, running count about 14,509)

P2 and P3 (both built from the 15 minute markets themselves) point to the same thing: L1 earns more when the market is turbulent. A real regime should show in an independent source. **Test:** for every L1 entry on all 18 series, the Bitcoin perpetual's realised volatility over the last 60 minutes (standard deviation of 1 minute log returns, bars closed before the decision; Deribit, as in SEARCH5K), and the DVOL implied-volatility level at the same minute. Top third against bottom third (cuts from all entries, no outcome used), adjusted net per contract, day-clustered. **Two sided bar:** absolute difference at least +1.0c with |z| at least 2.5, the same sign in both halves, at least 8 of 18 series with that sign, same sign with fees x1.2. **Prediction:** high-volatility entries earn about +0.7c more (z about 1.8), `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`: the P2 and P3 effects are partly chance. If either clears the bar it becomes a forward claim on days after 2026-10-25 (a real regime must survive new days).

## Result: P5, a market-wide volatility state (run once on 2026-10-25): both FALSIFIED

Same 28,390 entries. Bitcoin perpetual realised volatility over the last 60 minutes, top third against bottom third: **+0.56c, z +0.93**, halves -0.03 / +0.94, 10 of 18 series positive. DVOL level: -3.58c, z -3.38, but its first-half difference is exactly 0.00 because DVOL is a 30 day measure, so its thirds are blocks of weeks (a calendar effect, not a regime). So the independent volatility measure does not reproduce P2 and P3: they stay exploratory leads (forward claims P2R, P3R, read on days after 2026-10-26), not a regime. Count: 2 tries, about 14,509.

## Pre-registration: P6, adaptive timing-and-series allocator with shrinkage (written 2026-10-25 before any result; 1 try, running count about 14,510)

P4 chose among series and hours at the fixed 6 minute entry and added +0.65c over a random pick. P6 lets the strategy also choose the ENTRY TIME, with the cells shrunk towards their series' own record so thin cells cannot win by luck. **Candidates per window:** every series' L1-band entry (favourite ask 0.88 to 0.97) at 9, 7.5, 6 and 4.5 minutes left. **Score (past 14 days only):** (n·m_cell + 30·m_series_left) / (n + 30), where m_cell is the mean net of the same (series, entry time, 6 hour UTC bucket) cell, n its count, and m_series_left the mean of the same (series, entry time) over the same days; a series with fewer than 30 earlier entries scores 0. **Rule:** take the single highest-scoring candidate in each window if its score is above +0.5c, else nothing. First scored day: day 15. One position per window. **Test:** the selected entries' mean net per contract, day-clustered z, against the mean of all candidates in the same windows (a no-skill pick). **Pass:** mean at least +1.5c and at least +1.0c above the pool, z at least 2.5, at least 300 selections, positive in both halves, positive with fees x1.2. **Prediction:** about +1.0c, +0.7c over the pool, z about 2.5: `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. Honest framing: the walk-forward result is a genuine out-of-sample estimate of a rule that picks where to trade; if it clears the bar it is the first thing in this log that is a strategy and not a filter.

## Pre-registration: LAD1, option-style fair value on the hourly Bitcoin ladder (written 2026-10-26 before any ladder candle was fetched for this test; 6 tries, running count about 14,534)

**Why here.** A 2026-10-26 census of open Kalshi markets (excluding the combination markets) by 24 hour volume put the hourly Bitcoin ladder `KXBTCD` among the most liquid products: the 2026-10-26 01:00 UTC event had 188 strikes, 376,595 contracts of 24 hour volume, 22 strikes above 1,000, middle strikes 1c wide with 400 to 1,500 contracts at the best price. (Sports spreads and totals lead the list; they were tested before as SP1 and lost 4.2c.) The earlier ladder test (E4, 14 days) only applied L1's rule. This tests the options idea directly, on the product where it can matter: the horizon is 15 to 45 minutes, not the 6 minutes the 15 minute markets leave, and the quotes are deep enough to fill.

**Data.** `data/lad1.sqlite`: every settled `KXBTCD` market closing in the last 30 days, with 1 minute candles (closing bid and ask) from 55 minutes to 1 minute before the close; Deribit perpetual bars and DVOL from `data/search5k.sqlite` (usable only from a bar's close, as in IV1).

**Model (fixed).** At the decision minute, S = the perpetual's close, K = the strike, tau = minutes to the close, sigma per minute from one of two sources (each a separate try): DVOL/100 over the square root of 525,600 (implied), or the standard deviation of the last 60 one minute log returns (realised). p(YES) = Phi(ln(S/K) / (sigma x sqrt(tau))). The hourly ladder settles on a 60 second CF average, so the averaging correction is a variance factor tau + 1/3 instead of tau.

**Trade.** For each strike with a two sided book (bid and ask both present, ask minus bid at most 2c) and a yes ask between 0.10 and 0.90 (the liquid middle): buy YES at its ask if p minus the ask minus the fee exceeds **0.03**; buy NO at 1 minus the bid if (1 - p) minus that price minus the fee exceeds 0.03. One contract per strike, held to settlement, 7%·p·(1-p) taker fee. **Decision times:** 45, 30 and 15 minutes before the close. 3 times x 2 sigma sources = **6 tries**.

**Pass bar.** At least 300 entries on at least 100 distinct hours; day-clustered z at least 2.5 (6 tries); positive in both halves of the days; positive with fees x1.2. Note: the strikes of one hour are one bet on one number; the day-cluster z already treats days, not strikes, as independent, so it is conservative about that.

**Prediction.** `FALSIFIED` on all six. Reasons: the ladder is quoted by the same firms that read DVOL and the perpetual; a flat-volatility model is wrong in the wings (the market prices the smile) so the model's largest disagreements are its errors; and the 1.75c fee at 50c plus a 3c margin leaves nothing to find. Expected net -2c to -4c per contract, win rate below the price paid for the model's picks. Prior of a pass: 5%. Run once.

## Result: ladder arbitrage snapshot and two quick checks of the owner's pasted claims (2026-10-26; information, not a try)

Owner pasted two blocks of unsourced claims (sports "67% to 100% win rates", evening 6 to 11 PM ET "67% win rates", take-profit and trailing stops, fractional Kelly, diversification, scalping 42c to 49c). A win rate without the price paid says nothing (a 95c favourite wins 95%), the "internal platform data Q2 2026" has no source, and I treat all of it as unverified. What can be checked on our own data:
- **Evening window (7 to 11 PM ET = 23:00 to 03:00 UTC), L1 on 18 series, 28,390 entries:** loss rate **7.3% against 6.4%** the rest of the day, adjusted net -0.76c (z -1.74), both halves negative. The claim does not hold for us; the evening is slightly worse.
- **Diversification:** daily net per series, average pairwise correlation **+0.02** (crypto with crypto +0.09, crypto with the rest -0.01). True: our series are nearly independent day to day, so adding series with a positive edge lowers the portfolio's swings.
- **Kelly:** gold at 6 minutes, 1,609 entries, loss rate 5.3% (95% interval 4.2% to 6.4%), average win 6.8c, average loss 91.9c. Full Kelly at the point estimate is **25%** of bankroll; at the worse end of the interval it is **8%**. The live gold order (15 contracts, about $13.80) is **2.7%** of a $513 balance, so sizing is already below a conservative half-Kelly (about 4%). There is no case here for a bigger gold order beyond about 1.5 times.
- **Cross-strike arbitrage, snapshot at 00:35 UTC on 2026-10-26:** 4,064 strike pairs on the single-underlying ladders (Bitcoin and Ethereum hourly, 50 state gas-price ladders, WTI, gold, silver) checked for a locked profit (YES at the lower strike plus NO at the higher). **Zero** locks after fees. (A first pass reported thousands; they were different cities sharing an event ticker, not a ladder, and were discarded.)
- **Post-peak weather:** at 8:35 PM ET the New York, Miami and Los Angeles brackets that contain the day's high were already priced 0.99 / 1.00 and the rest 0.00 / 0.01. No carry: the market knows the station readings before a public hourly model does.

## Pre-registration: SC1, in-play scalping after a price jump on tennis, with basketball, football and hockey for information (written 2026-10-26 before any candle was fetched for this test; 4 tries, running count about 14,538)

**The claim being tested (owner's pasted text):** Kalshi scalping works on sports with real-time catalysts, 3 to 10c per trade, tight spreads, pre-set take-profit exits. **Why tennis:** 2026-10-26 census: the ATP Challenger match-winner market alone trades about 660,000 contracts in a single match, spreads are 1c, and every game and break moves the price: the most in-play volume on Kalshi outside the combination markets. Earlier scalp tests (H1 to H4, the S-series, SC-families) were on the 15 minute crypto and commodity markets and lost to the 4c to 5c round-trip cost at mid prices; this tests the sports setting the claim is about.

**Universe.** Settled markets of the tennis match-winner series (ATP, WTA, Challenger and ITF; the five series listed in the 2026-10-26 census) that closed in the last 45 days; 1 minute candles (closing bid, ask, volume) for the last 6 hours before the close. Information only, not part of the verdict: basketball spreads and totals, football first-half markets, hockey totals (same rule, same bar).

**Event.** A minute t where the mid-price (average of closing bid and ask) moved by 5c or more from the previous minute, both quotes have a spread of 3c or less, the previous mid was between 0.15 and 0.85, and the minute traded at least 100 contracts. Events within 10 minutes of the previous event in the same market are skipped (no overlap).

**Rules (4 tries).** Decision at the close of minute t; the order fills at the closing quote of minute **t+1** (a one minute latency, stricter than a real bot). MOM: buy the side that jumped at its ask. FADE: buy the other side at its ask. Exit by selling at the closing bid k minutes after the entry minute, **k = 2 or k = 5** (so MOM2, MOM5, FADE2, FADE5). Fee 7%·p·(1-p) on the buy and on the sell. If a needed candle is missing the event is skipped and counted. One contract.

**Pass bar.** At least 1,000 events on at least 30 days, mean net per event of at least +1.0c, day-clustered z of at least 3.0 (4 tries), positive in both halves of the days, positive with fees x1.2. **Prediction:** all four negative, about -3c to -4c: spread and two fees cost about 3.5c to 4c at mid prices and a jump of 5c carries no systematic follow-through or reversal after one minute. Prior of a pass: 10% (a break of serve is a real information shock that might overshoot in thin matches). Run once.

## Pre-registration: CRYPTO1, slow Bitcoin and Ethereum strategies on spot and perpetual costs, 2019 to 2026 (written 2026-10-26 before any hourly bar was fetched; 384 tries, running count about 14,930)

**Owner's request (2026-10-26):** trade the actual coins, perhaps with leverage, on a real exchange; "potentially an edge in the market". Earlier crypto work (Alpaca, 2026-08) died on cost: a 0.62% gross edge per trade against a 0.70% round trip. This tests whether anything slow enough to beat realistic costs exists, on 8 years of history instead of 82 days.

**Data.** Deribit `BTC-PERPETUAL` (from 2019-01-01) and `ETH-PERPETUAL` (from its listing, about 2019-03) hourly bars (open, high, low, close) and hourly funding history, public and keyless, into `data/crypto1.sqlite`. Signals use only bars closed before the decision; the fill is the OPEN of the next hour.

**Grid.** Rule families: MOM (long if the last L hours' return is positive, short if negative), REV (the opposite), BRK (long when the close exceeds the highest high of the previous L hours, short when it falls below the lowest low, else flat), VMOM (MOM only when the last 24 hour realised volatility is below its median over the previous 90 days). L = 6, 12, 24, 48, 96, 168 hours; hold H = 4, 12, 24, 48 hours; one position at a time, a new signal is taken only after the previous trade is closed. 4 rules x 6 L x 4 H = 96 strategies; 2 assets; 2 cost modes = **384 tries**. *Perpetual mode:* long and short, round-trip cost **0.14%** (0.05% taker fee each side plus 0.02% slippage each side) plus the actual hourly funding paid or received while held. *Spot mode:* long only (a short signal means flat), round-trip cost **0.60%** (0.30% each side, the top retail tier on most US spot exchanges), no funding.

**What is scored.** Per trade: position x (return over the holding window minus the average return of all windows of the same length in the discovery years) minus costs. The subtraction removes the free ride a long-only rule gets from crypto's upward drift; it tests timing skill, not exposure. Daily P&L = the sum of the trades closed that day.

**Splits.** Discovery 2019-01 to 2023-12, confirmation 2024, holdout 2025-01 to 2026-10.

**Judging (Reality Check, per asset and cost mode, 1,000 resamples of 7-day blocks of discovery days).** Survivor needs: (1) discovery t above the 95th percentile of the best-of-96 maximum; at least 150 discovery trades; (2) confirmation mean net per trade above 0 with t at least 1.64; (3) positive with all costs x1.5 in discovery and confirmation; (4) holdout mean above 0 with t at least 1.0. Verdicts: `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` all four, `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` if the holdout fails, `FALSIFIED` otherwise. One run; refused a second time.

**Prediction.** Spot mode: nothing survives (0.60% eats any slow edge). Perpetual mode: time-series momentum is documented in crypto before 2023 but has decayed; expected best discovery t about 3 to 3.5 near the Reality Check threshold; probability that at least one perpetual strategy passes discovery plus confirmation 25%, and clears the holdout 10%. If one survives it is a candidate for a paper test, not a deployment; leverage and live money are decisions for the owner in the build session after a four week paper log with kill rules registered first.

## Pre-registration: FP1, footprint on tennis jumps: does real buying behind a 5c jump keep it going? (written 2026-10-26 before any tape was fetched for tennis events and before the SC1 read; 4 tries, running count about 14,544)

**Why.** SC1 asks whether any 5c jump in a tennis match market is worth following or fading. A candle cannot say whether the jump came from real aggressive buying (many takers lifting the ask) or from one thin print through an empty book. The public trade tape can (`footprint.py`: taker buys vs sells per minute). A footprint is the only new information here; the price rule is SC1's own.

**Events.** SC1's events, unchanged (5c mid jump in one minute, spread at most 3c, mid 0.15 to 0.85, minute volume at least 100, 10 quiet minutes before). For each, the tape of the jump minute and the two minutes before it (`/markets/trades`, resumable download, only if SC1 has at least 400 events).

**Footprint measures (fixed now).** DELTA_SHARE = taker contracts on the side of the jump divided by all taker contracts in the jump minute. CONFIRMED: DELTA_SHARE at least 0.70 and at least 100 contracts. THIN: DELTA_SHARE under 0.55 or under 50 contracts. Two rules: CONF_MOM (follow a CONFIRMED jump) and THIN_FADE (fade a THIN jump). Fill, hold k (2 and 5 minutes), fees and spread exactly as SC1 (next minute's closing quote). Nothing else is tried.

**Bar.** Per rule and k: net per contract at least +1.0c after fee and spread, day-clustered z at least 2.0, positive in both halves, positive with fees x1.2, at least 150 events on at least 12 days. Also must beat SC1's own unfiltered rule on the same events by at least +1.0c. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` only if all hold; `FALSIFIED` if net is under +0.3c or z under 1.0; fewer than 150 events is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. Run once.

**Prediction.** Neither passes: the quote already moves with the buying, so the footprint repeats what the price says (TAPE20 found the same on 15 minute markets). Prior of a pass 8%. The most likely outcome is that CONFIRMED jumps follow through by less than the cost of crossing the spread twice.

## Pre-registration: FP2, gold footprint as a loss warning: does opposing taker flow before the 6 minute decision mark the losers? (written 2026-10-26 before any gold tape was fetched or split; 2 tries, running count about 14,546)

**Why.** Gold is the only series that earns (profit factor 1.33) and one loss wipes about 12 wins. A filter that removes even a third of the losses without removing many wins is worth far more than a new entry rule. TAPE20 pooled five series and used 21 days; this asks only about gold, over every gold market on file, with one footprint measure.

**Data.** Every gold 15 minute L1 entry (favourite ask 0.88 to 0.97 at 6 minutes left, `feat1.build`) from all gold markets on file (about 80 days). For each, every trade in the 3 minutes before the decision (9 to 6 minutes before close), as taker contracts toward and against the favourite (`data/fp2_tape.json`, resumable, `python -m scalper.fp2 fetch`).

**The one rule.** OPPOSED: contracts taken against the favourite are at least 100 and at least 40% of all taker contracts in those 3 minutes. Entries that are OPPOSED would be skipped. Thresholds fixed now, no second cut tried. A control, FLOW_TOWARD (toward share at least 70%), is reported for information only.

**Judging.** Compare OPPOSED entries with the rest (net per contract, fee included, same entries). Split by day: discovery first 60%, confirmation last 40%. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` needs OPPOSED worse than the rest by at least 3.0c with day-clustered z at least 2.0 on discovery, at least 1.5c with z 1.0 on confirmation, and OPPOSED loss rate at least 1.5x the rest in both. `FALSIFIED` if the all-days gap is under 1.0c or z under 1.0. Fewer than 40 OPPOSED entries in discovery or 20 in confirmation is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. Run once: `python -m scalper.fp2 run`.

**Prediction.** FALSIFIED or NOT_ENOUGH_DATA. The price at 6 minutes already contains the flow (TAPE20), and the Oct 25 gold loss showed normal flow before entry. Prior of a pass 8%. Even a pass is only a candidate skip rule for a forward read, never a live change.

## Pre-registration: FP3, footprint micro-scalps on deep markets, traded as a price move and not as a yes or no (written 2026-10-26 before any footprint trigger was computed on tennis events; 80 tries, running count about 14,626)

**The owner's frame (kept).** Do not wait for settlement. Enter at 20c and sell at 40c because the flow says it will move; earn the spread; trade other people's behaviour. This test treats a contract as a price series and scores every trade from entry quote to exit quote, never to settlement.

**Cost, stated first.** Fee is 7% x p x (1-p) per contract per side: 1.1c at 20c, 1.75c at 50c. Round trip plus a 1c to 3c spread is about 3c to 6c. A 20c target at a 10c stop only needs a hit rate near 40% before cost; a 3c target needs about 65%. So the test is the hit rate that each footprint trigger buys, not the size of the move.

**Universe.** Tennis match winner markets in `data/sc1.sqlite` (in-play, mid 0.15 to 0.85, spread at most 3c at entry, minute volume at least 100), with the trade tape fetched for each trigger minute and the two before it. Basketball totals and the hourly Bitcoin ladder stay information only until tennis reads. One position per market at a time, no overlap with the live L1 series (different markets by construction).

**Triggers (5, fixed now, computed from the tape up to the end of the trigger minute only).**
1. STACK: three or more adjacent YES price levels in the minute, each with taker contracts one side at least 3 to 1 and at least 20 contracts.
2. DELTA_BREAK: minute net delta (taker buys minus sells) in the top 5% of that market's own earlier minutes, same sign as the mid move.
3. ABSORB: minute volume at least 3x the market's trailing median while the mid moved under 1c (heavy flow, no price change).
4. BIG_PRINT: a single taker print of at least 10x the trailing median print.
5. SPREAD_CAPTURE: spread at least 3c and the last two minutes balanced (delta share 0.45 to 0.55); post at the bid, sell at the ask. Fill assumed only when a later candle's ask low reaches the bid and bid high reaches the ask (flattering; queue position is unknown, so this one is an upper bound).

**Directions.** Follow (trade with the flow) and fade (against it), both counted. SPREAD_CAPTURE has one direction.

**Exits.** Target T = 3, 5, 10 or 20c from the entry quote; stop S = T/2 or T; forced exit after 5 minutes at the then bid. Entries and exits at the next minute's closing quote (a taker pays the ask in, hits the bid out), fee both sides, and an unfilled exit at a gap is taken at the next quote, not the stop price. 4 triggers x 2 directions x 4 targets x 2 stops = 64, plus SPREAD_CAPTURE x 4 targets x 2 stops = 8, plus 8 control rules (same exits entered at random minutes in the same markets) = 80.

**Judging.** Family-wise: shuffle trigger minutes among eligible minutes of the same market and day-block bootstrap (300 reps) to get the null distribution of the best of 72 rules. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` needs for a rule: net mean at least +1.0c after fees with day-clustered z above the null 95th percentile, positive in both halves and with fees x1.2, at least 200 trades on at least 12 days, and above its random-entry control by at least +1.0c. `FALSIFIED` if no rule clears +0.3c. Fewer than 200 trades for the best rule is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. SPREAD_CAPTURE can never reach more than `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` without a queue-position recording (RECORD1-style) because its fill is assumed. Run once.

**Prediction.** FALSIFIED. Each trigger mostly repeats what the price already shows (TAPE20 on the 15 minute markets), and 3c to 6c of round-trip cost eats a 3c to 5c target before the hit rate matters. The best chance is the large-target rules (20c / 10c stop) on STACK follow, where cost is small against the move, but a 20c continuation in one to five minutes should be rare. Prior of any pass 8%.

20,278 tennis match-winner markets with candles over 46 days, 62,747 jump events. Net per contract after fee and spread, entry and exit at the next minute's closing quote: MOM2 (follow, hold 2 minutes) **-4.29c** (n 62,165, z -119.5, halves -4.30 / -4.27); MOM5 -4.16c (z -72.0); FADE2 -4.51c (z -116.0); FADE5 -4.52c (z -71.1). **Question (owner's bar: profit factor at least 2.5).** For L1 entries a profit factor of 2.5 needs a loss rate near 2.6% at about 93c entries, i.e. a subset that wins about 4.5 points more often than its price says. 852,975 observations over 79 days, 2,021 cells (series x 9 entry times x 5 price bands x side), 826 with enough discovery entries. **29 cells reached profit factor 2.5 in the first half; the shuffled-outcome null produced a median of 31 (95th percentile 37).** Seven cells held 2.5 in both halves; the null produced a median of **7** (95th percentile 10). Outside the 0.985 to 0.995 band, 1 real cell against a null median of 0 (95th percentile 2). So the whole grid is exactly what chance produces. Verdict `FALSIFIED`.

**Two things the run showed.** (1) Profit factor is easy to game in the 0.985 to 0.995 band: a win pays about 0.5c and a loss costs 99c, so "no losses yet" prints a profit factor of 9.99 on a trade worth 0.5c, and the null produces the same cells. Profit factor alone cannot be the target. (2) The best non-trivial cells, for the record (in-sample, not claims): SOL 7 minutes left, 0.95-0.985, yes side: 446 entries, 3 losses, +2.28c a contract; gold 4 minutes left, 0.95-0.985, no side: 565 entries, 5 losses, +1.93c; Dogecoin 4 minutes left, 0.985-0.995, yes: +0.80c; NEAR 3 minutes, 0.985-0.995, yes: +0.75c. Tries: about 2,000 plus 200 shuffles; running count about 17,500.

## Pre-registration: WX3 (named WX1 in the first draft, which collided with the 2026-10-13 WX1 forecast test; the old file is restored), are the daily-high-temperature ladders internally consistent? (written 2026-10-27 before any weather candle was fetched; 1 test over about 10 cities x 30 days, running count about 17,503)

**Why.** Each daily-high market is one event with mutually exclusive, exhaustive buckets (for example "67 or below", 68-69 ... "76 or above"), so exactly one bucket pays $1. If the buckets' YES asks add to less than $1 after fees, buying one of each locks a profit; if the YES bids add to more than $1 plus fees, selling one of each does. No forecast is needed. Open-Meteo forecast history was refused today (daily API limit), so a forecast-versus-price test is not possible yet; this one needs only Kalshi prices.

**Data.** Settled events of KXHIGHNY, MIA, AUS, DEN, LAX, PHIL, HOU, TDC, TSEA, TATL closing in the last 30 days. For each event with 3 or more buckets, hourly candles (bid and ask close) for every bucket across the 48 hours before the close.

**Rule.** At each hour where all buckets have both quotes: BUY_ALL = sum of asks + sum of taker fees (7% x p x (1-p) per bucket) < 1.00; SELL_ALL = 1.00 + fees < sum of bids... (selling YES at the bid means a $1 payout is owed on one bucket, so the lock is sum of bids - fees > 1.00). A hit needs a gap of at least 1.0c after fees and every bucket to have volume in that hour. Report hit counts, the average locked gap, and how many hours the prices were stale (no trade in the hour). `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` only if there are at least 30 hits on at least 10 events with an average locked gap of at least 1.0c in hours where every bucket traded. Otherwise `FALSIFIED`; fewer than 30 events scanned is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`.

**Prediction.** FALSIFIED: market makers keep the ladder summing to about $1.00 to $1.03 (it is the one thing a bot enforces). Prior of a pass 5%. The scan is cheap and fully riskless if it is real, so it is worth the minutes.

### FP3 implementation notes (added 2026-10-27 before any FP3 trigger was computed or any outcome simulated)

Universe fixed to the 250 most liquid tennis matches in `sc1.sqlite` by candle volume (one market per match, ATP, WTA and the two Challenger series), whole trade tape downloaded (`src/scalper/fp3.py fetch`). Eligible minute: minute volume at least 100, spread at most 3c, mid 0.15 to 0.85 at the trigger minute, next minute quoted. Entry at the next minute's closing quote, exit scan over the following 5 minutes on closing quotes (target, stop, or the 5th minute's quote). Controls: every eligible minute entered in the direction of that minute's net delta (follow) or against it (fade) with the same exits. Family-wise null: 300 draws of random eligible minutes, same count per rule, best day-clustered z over the 64 rules. SPREAD_CAPTURE is not run (its fill needs queue position). 64 rules = 4 triggers x 2 directions x 4 targets x 2 stops. Tests: none beyond a dry import; the module is research-only.

## Result: WX3 (run once on 2026-10-27): FALSIFIED

269 daily-high events scanned (9 cities, 30 days; Houston returned no markets), 2,698 hours in which every bucket of an event traded. **One** hour showed a buy-all lock after fees (1.41c, one event) and none showed a sell-all lock. The ladders sum to about $1.00 as expected; there is no riskless arbitrage in them. Tries: 1, about 17,504.

## Result: FP3 (run once on 2026-10-27): FALSIFIED

228 of the 250 most liquid tennis matches (46 days; the last 22 were still downloading at the read), 64,776 minutes, 37,340 eligible minutes with flow. 64 rules (STACK, DELTA_BREAK, ABSORB, BIG_PRINT x follow or fade x targets 3, 5, 10, 20c x stops T/2 or T), each traded at the next minute's closing quote and scored as a price move with fee both sides. **Every rule lost**: the best is DELTA_BREAK fade, T20c / S20c, **-3.69c per contract** (n 3,236, 45 days, z -20.9, halves -3.63 / -3.74, fees x1.2 -4.28c); most sit between -3.7c and -4.2c. The random-entry control (same exits, entered at any eligible minute in the direction of that minute's net delta) is **-4.14c to -4.22c**. So the footprint triggers are worth about 0.1c to 0.5c over entering at random, and that is nowhere near the 4.2c it costs to cross the spread twice and pay the fee twice. Following and fading lose the same. Verdict `FALSIFIED`; nothing passed. Not run: SPREAD_CAPTURE, because it needs queue position that neither the tape nor the candles give.

**What it means.** Taker scalping on tennis costs about 4.2c a round trip, and no footprint trigger, target or stop moves a 5-minute price by more than that. The only version of this idea left standing is the one that does not cross the spread: resting limit orders on both sides of deep markets, earning the spread instead of paying it. That needs recorded order-book snapshots (queue depth at the best bid and ask), which the owner's bot does not record yet. Tries: 64 + 300-draw null; running count about 17,570. Code `src/scalper/fp3.py`, result `data/fp3_result.txt`.

## Pre-registration: MAKER1, earning the spread on deep tennis markets with resting orders, replayed on the real tape (written 2026-10-27 before any maker fill was computed; 3 queue assumptions x 2 fee assumptions = 6 tries, running count about 17,576)

**The entry mechanic (owner: "find an entry mechanic").** Do not cross the spread. At an eligible minute (volume at least 100, mid 0.15 to 0.85, spread 2c to 4c at the minute's closing quote, bid b, ask a) rest a BUY of YES at b. If it fills within 3 minutes, rest a SELL of the same contracts at a. If that does not fill within 5 minutes of the entry fill, cross: sell at the then closing bid (taker). If the entry does not fill within 3 minutes, cancel it (no trade, counted in the fill rate). One contract, one posting per eligible minute, no overlap within a market.

**Fills from the tape (no model).** A resting buy at b fills when a taker SELL print (taker bought NO) occurs at a YES price at or below b after the post time, once the cumulative taker contracts at or through b since posting reach Q. A resting sell at a fills the same way from taker BUY prints at or above a. Q = 1 (we are first in the queue, an upper bound), Q = 100 and Q = 300 (queue ahead of us; the real displayed size is unknown). This is still optimistic: it ignores that a fill is more likely exactly when the price is about to move against us only if the tape shows it, which it does (adverse selection is in the replay because the exit side only fills if the price comes back).

**Fees.** (a) Maker fee = taker fee 7% x p x (1-p) per side (conservative); (b) maker fee zero (information; Kalshi's maker fee schedule varies by market and I have not verified tennis).

**Judging, per queue assumption, fee (a):** net per filled entry at least +0.5c, day-clustered z at least 2.0, both halves of the days positive, at least 300 filled entries on at least 12 days. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` means only "worth recording the order book to measure the queue", never a trade. `FALSIFIED` if net per filled entry is below +0.1c at Q = 1. Fewer than 300 fills is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. Run once. Data: the 250 tape files `data/fp3*.sqlite` plus `sc1.sqlite` candles.

**Prediction.** Q = 1 shows a small positive (+0.5c to +1.5c) because it is an upper bound; Q = 100 and 300 shrink to about zero or negative as the entry fills become rarer and more toxic (filled only when price falls through the bid). Prior that Q = 100 passes: 10%.

## Result: MAKER1 (run once on 2026-10-27): all six FALSIFIED

228 tennis matches, 45 days, 4,300 to 4,500 postings per queue assumption (resting buy at the bid, resting sell at the ask, cross after 5 minutes). Net per filled entry: **Q = 1 (first in the queue, an upper bound), maker fee equal to the taker fee: -2.80c** (3,159 fills, 70% fill rate, z -28.2); Q = 1 with **zero** maker fee: **+0.22c** (z +2.30, halves +0.24 / +0.20); Q = 100: -4.16c (fee) / -1.15c (zero fee); Q = 300: -4.99c / -1.99c. The more queue we are behind, the worse it gets: fills come when the price is already moving through our order (adverse selection), and the spread we hoped to earn is smaller than what that costs. Even the best case (first in line, no fee) earns 0.22c a fill, which is not a strategy. Spread earning on tennis is closed unless real queue and fee data show otherwise; recording the order book is no longer worth asking for on this evidence. Tries: 6, about 17,576. Code `src/scalper/maker1.py`, result `data/maker1_result.txt`.

## Pre-registration: BOUNCE1, the owner's own trade: buy the cheap side near the strike with about 8 minutes left and sell on the bounce (written 2026-10-27 after the owner described the rule, before any trade of it was simulated; 10 variants + 3 distance variants for information, running count about 17,589)

**The rule (owner, 2026-10-27).** "I usually buy 30c or lower when there is less than 50 points away from bitcoin with like 8 minutes left. I bet on the reversal rather than the winning. I hop in for a pullback and sell when it goes my way, like 30% of my position, and then I'm out."

**Universe.** Every KXBTC15M market on file (about 6,400, 78 days), 1 minute bid and ask candles, Kalshi's strike, and the Deribit BTC perpetual 1 minute bars as the spot proxy (the bar starting one minute before the entry candle ends). **Entry:** the candle ending 480 s before the close; if the spot is within $50 of the strike and one side's ask is between 0.10 and 0.30, buy that side (the cheap side) at the ask, taker fee. One entry per market.

**Exits (10 variants fixed now).** Target price = entry price x M with M in 1.2, 1.3, 1.5 (a 30c entry sells at 36c, 39c, 45c). Mode A1: sell everything at the target, otherwise hold to settlement. A2: same, but if the target was not reached, sell at the bid 120 s before the close. B: sell 30% of the position at the target and hold the other 70% to settlement. Target fill: the first later candle whose bid high reaches the target fills at the target price (optimistic, a resting sell); the information run requires the closing bid instead. Plus the baseline: buy the cheap side and hold to settlement. Fee 7% x p x (1-p) on every sale, none at settlement.

**Information only (not claims):** the same A1 with the distance filter at $25 and $100 (spot to strike), and the same entry at 6 and 10 minutes left.

**Judging.** For each of the 9 exit variants: mean net per contract AND mean return on cost; day-clustered z; both halves of the days; fees x1.2; at least 300 trades; and better than the hold baseline on the same entries. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` only if one variant has net per contract at least +1.0c, z at least 2.5 (9 variants), both halves positive, positive at fees x1.2, and above the baseline by at least +0.5c. `FALSIFIED` if the best variant is under +0.3c. Fewer than 300 trades: `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. Run once.

**Prediction.** FALSIFIED. A 25c to 30c contract wins about as often as its price says (win rate equals price on every band tested here), so buying it has an expected value of minus the fee and spread, and selling part of it early at a +30% target only reshuffles when the same loss is taken. If the bounce is real it must show as the target being reached more often than a random-walk price would reach it; I will report the hit rate against a placebo (the same entries with the target applied to a time-shifted candle series). Prior of a pass 7%.

## Result: BOUNCE1 (run once on 2026-10-27): FALSIFIED, and the cheap side near the strike is the worst place to buy

7,390 Bitcoin 15 minute markets over 78 days; 1,205 entries (about 8 minutes left, spot within $50 of the strike, the cheap side's ask 0.10 to 0.30). **Buy and hold to settlement: -6.21c per contract (return on cost -25.6%, z -5.44, halves -7.48 / -4.45, profit factor 0.68).** Selling on the bounce does not help: A1 (sell all at +20%, +30%, +50%) -6.41c, -6.61c, -6.65c (profit factor 0.18 to 0.41); A2 (sell at 2 minutes left if the target was missed) -5.56c to -5.91c; B (sell 30% at the target, hold 70%) -6.27c to -6.34c. Information: distance $25 -7.17c, $100 -6.25c; 6 minutes left -5.62c, 10 minutes left -6.09c; requiring the closing bid for the target fill (a stricter, realistic fill) -11.27c. **Every variant is far worse than the fee, so the cheap side wins less often than its price says**: the favourite-longshot bias again, on this exact setup. The bounce target is reached often enough to feel like a winner, but the trades that miss it lose the whole price. Placebo (time-shifted target hit rate) not computed; the result does not need it. Tries: 10 + 5 information runs, about 17,605. Code `src/scalper/bounce1.py`, result `data/bounce1_result.txt`.

## Pre-registration: PULL1, buy the pullback on Bitcoin and Ethereum 15 minute contracts, exit on a bounce or by the clock (written 2026-10-27 before any pullback was computed; 288 rules per asset x 2 assets = 576 tries, running count about 20,777)

**The owner's style, made precise.** "Price pulled back from a move" = a side's mid is at least d below its highest mid of the last 6 minutes; buy that same side (the pullback, not the reversal). "Sell a part and be out" and "cut or hold depending on time left" = the exits below. Candles only (1 minute bid and ask closes), Bitcoin and Ethereum 15 minute series, all days on file (about 79).

**Entry grid (24 cells per asset).** Time left at the trigger candle L in 600, 480, 360, 240 s; pullback depth d in 5c, 10c, 15c; the side's ask at entry in 0.25 to 0.50 or 0.50 to 0.75. Entry at the NEXT minute's closing ask (one minute of lag, as in FP3). One entry per market per cell; both sides can trigger.

**Exit grid (12 combos).** Target T = +5c, +10c, +15c on the closing bid (checked every minute until 120 s before the close); optional stop S = -10c on the closing bid (or none); if neither hits, either hold to settlement (A) or sell at the bid 120 s before the close (B). Fee 7% x p x (1-p) on every sale, none at settlement.

**Judging.** Discovery = first half of the days, confirmation = second half. A rule is a candidate if it has at least 150 discovery entries and mean net at least +1.5c; confirmed if at least 60 confirmation entries and mean net at least +0.75c. Null: for each rule, the same number of entries drawn at random from the same time and price band WITHOUT the pullback condition, 100 draws, count of candidates and of confirmed rules. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` only if the number of confirmed rules exceeds the null's 95th percentile AND at least one confirmed rule has day-clustered z at least 2.5 over all days. Otherwise `FALSIFIED`. Run once.

**Prediction.** FALSIFIED. A pullback entry in a mid-priced contract pays about 4.5c of round-trip cost (1.75c fee a side near 50c plus the lag), and the no-pullback control has the same exits; the extra from a pullback should be well under that (the lag-adjusted tape scalps in FP3 were all -3.7c or worse). Prior of a pass 6%.

The one confirmed rule: ETH, 4 minutes left, ask 0.50 to 0.75, pullback at least 15c, target +15c with no stop, hold to settlement otherwise: discovery +2.19c (n 263), confirmation +0.93c (n 285); one of 576, so it is not a finding. ## Pre-registration: SWEEP1, big prints and sweeps on Bitcoin 15 minute markets, followed or faded, with a scale-out exit (built with the owner on 2026-10-27 from their answers: signal = big print or sweep; direction = either, let the data decide; market = Bitcoin 15 minute; exit = scale out; written before any Bitcoin tape was downloaded; 24 rules + controls, running count about 20,801)

**Triggers (tape, computed only from trades up to the end of the trigger minute).** BIG: one taker print of at least 100 contracts AND at least 10 times the median print of that market so far (at least 50 earlier prints). SWEEP: within one second, same-side taker trades covering at least 3 distinct YES price levels and at least 100 contracts in total. Flow sign: +1 if takers bought YES, -1 if they bought NO. Trigger minutes must have 3 to 12 minutes left, a quoted next minute, spread at most 3c and the chosen side's ask between 0.20 and 0.80 at entry.

**Direction.** FOLLOW (buy the side the takers bought) and FADE (buy the other side). Both counted. Entry at the next minute's closing ask (1 minute of lag; a faster entry is not testable on 1 minute candles).

**Scale-out exits (6 combos).** S1: sell 30% of the position at +30% of the entry price (closing bid), hold the remaining 70% to settlement. S2: same, then trail the rest with a stop 5c below the highest closing bid since the entry and sell at the bid 120 s before the close if still held. S3: sell 50% at +20% and hold the rest to settlement. Each with or without an initial stop 8c below the entry (on the closing bid; if hit, everything is sold). Fee 7% x p x (1-p) on every sale, none at settlement; scale-out parts are weighted by their share of the position.

**Data.** The trade tape of every Bitcoin 15 minute market closing in the last 30 days (`data/sweep1_*.sqlite`, sharded download), with `book`, `l1b` and `fresh` candles.

**Judging.** Per rule: net per contract (position-weighted); discovery = first half of days, confirmation = second half; control = every eligible minute in the direction of that minute's net delta (follow) or against it (fade), same exits; family-wise null = 300 draws of random eligible minutes, same count per rule, best day-clustered z over the 24 rules. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` needs: at least 200 trades on at least 12 days, mean net at least +1.0c, z above the null's 95th percentile, both halves positive, positive at fees x1.2, and above the control by at least +1.0c. `FALSIFIED` if the best rule is under +0.3c. Fewer than 200 trades for the best rule: `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. Run once.

**Prediction.** FALSIFIED: FP3 found the same kind of tape trigger worth 0.1c to 0.5c on tennis against about 4.2c of cost, and TAPE20 found no tape rule predicting the 15 minute outcome. Bitcoin's 1c spread makes cost lower (about 3.5c to 4.5c near 50c, the fee dominating), so the chance is a little higher than tennis. Prior of a pass 5%.

### SWEEP1 amendment (2026-10-27, before any trigger was scored)

One Bitcoin 15 minute market carries 25,000 to 33,000 trades in the 13 minutes before the close, so 30 days (2,384 markets) would be about 70 million trades and 13 hours of download. Window cut to the **last 7 days (about 670 markets)**, and the triggers and per-minute net delta are computed while downloading (raw trades are not kept). Nothing else changed. A 7 day sample is small (about 12 to 18 days are needed by the bar), so the likeliest verdict is `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA` unless a rule is clearly bad or clearly good.

## Pre-registration: PM1, does Kalshi's noon Bitcoin ladder follow Polymarket's price for the same strike? (written 2026-10-27 before any Polymarket price was compared with a Kalshi quote; 1 test x 2 thresholds, running count about 20,915)

**Why.** Polymarket lists "Bitcoin above $K on <date>" (noon ET, Binance 1 minute close) and Kalshi lists the 12 PM EDT hourly ladder KXBTCD (the same noon, CF Benchmarks index, strikes at x99.99). Same question, two venues, different settlement sources (a basis of tens of dollars). Polymarket's price needs no account (public API) and is an independent fair value. If the two disagree by more than the fee and spread, does buying the cheaper side on Kalshi earn?

**Data.** Last 20 days (closes at noon ET). For each date: Polymarket's event "bitcoin-above-on-<month>-<day>-2026", each strike's YES token and hourly price history; Kalshi's KXBTCD markets closing at noon ET whose strike equals Polymarket's strike (within $1 of x99.99 + 0.01), with hourly candles. Time points: 8, 9, 10 and 11 AM ET (candle end), Polymarket price = last history point at or before the time (within 90 minutes).

**Rule.** At each time point and strike, if Polymarket's YES price exceeds Kalshi's YES ask by at least 4c, buy YES at the Kalshi ask; if Kalshi's YES bid exceeds Polymarket's price by at least 4c, buy NO at 1 minus the bid. Hold to settlement on Kalshi's result, taker fee. Also reported (not claims): thresholds 2c and 6c.

**Judging.** Mean net per contract, day-clustered z, halves of the days, fees x1.2. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` needs at least 150 trades on at least 8 days, mean at least +1.0c, z at least 2.0, both halves positive, positive at fees x1.2. `FALSIFIED` if the mean is under +0.3c. Fewer than 150 trades: `NOT_ENOUGH_DATA`. Run once.

**Prediction.** FALSIFIED or NOT_ENOUGH_DATA: Kalshi's ladder is deep and tight (1c spreads, 20k+ contracts) and tracks the spot, so any Polymarket "lead" is the same spot information, and the settlement bases differ. Prior of a pass 5%.

## Result: PM1 (run once on 2026-10-27): NOT_ENOUGH_DATA (0 strike-time pairs; the test could not be made)

20 days with both venues listed, 0 usable strike-time pairs. Polymarket's strikes are $2,000 apart and the Kalshi markets with the same strike are 1c to 2c illiquid in the hours before noon (a 6 hour window of the 88,000 and 90,000 strikes shows one hourly candle, at expiry, quoting 0.00 / 0.01). Only the strikes within about $300 of the spot trade, and Polymarket has almost none there. Polymarket's finer 'what price will Bitcoin hit' and 'above on' ladders are the thing to try if this is revisited; the result is "could not test", not "no edge". Tries: 1, about 20,915.

## Pre-registration: PERP3, fast (5 to 60 minute) Bitcoin and Ethereum perpetual strategies with a stop and a target (written 2026-10-27 before any signal was computed on these bars; 336 rules + 100 null draws, running count about 21,350)

**Why.** CRYPTO1 (2026-10-26) tested slow strategies only and failed; the owner asked for fast ones and for the capital they would need. **Data:** Deribit perpetual 1 minute bars (open, high, low, close, volume) for BTC and ETH in `data/search5k.sqlite`, about 78 days; the entry is the open of the bar after the signal. **Cost assumption (stated, not measured here):** 0.14% of notional per round trip (fees and slippage, as in CRYPTO1); 0.08% is reported for information. No funding is charged (holds are at most 60 minutes). One unit of notional, no leverage in the result (leverage scales return and risk equally).

**Signals (14 per asset).** MOMO follow and FADE: the return over N = 15, 30, 60 minutes at least 2 standard deviations (the trailing 24 hour 1 minute return deviation x sqrt(N)) in either direction. BREAKOUT follow and FADE: the close breaks the highest high or lowest low of the previous N = 30, 60, 120 minutes. VOLSPIKE follow and FADE: the last 5 minute volume at least 3 times the median 5 minute volume of the previous 24 hours, direction = the sign of the 5 minute return. A rule may re-enter 30 minutes after its previous entry.

**Exits (12 per signal).** Target T = 0.3%, 0.6%, 1.0% of the entry price; stop S = T/2 or T; maximum hold 30 or 60 minutes (exit at the close of the last bar). If a bar touches both, the stop is assumed first. Target and stop fill at their level.

**Judging.** Discovery = first half of the days, confirmation = second half. Candidate: at least 150 discovery trades and net mean at least +0.10% per trade after cost; confirmed: at least 60 confirmation trades and net mean at least +0.05%. Null: for every rule, the same number of entries drawn at random from all minutes with the direction chosen at random, same exits, 100 draws, count of candidates and confirmed rules. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` only if confirmed rules exceed the null's 95th percentile AND at least one confirmed rule has an all-days net mean at least +0.10% with day-clustered z at least 2.5. Otherwise `FALSIFIED`. Run once.

**Capital reading (planned).** If a rule survives, its capital need is computed from its own numbers (net per trade, trades per day, worst day) at 1x and 3x; nothing is sized for a rule that does not survive.

**Prediction.** FALSIFIED. A 0.14% round trip is large against 5 to 60 minute moves of 0.2% to 0.6% (BTC's median 30 minute range is about 0.3%), and CRYPTO1 found nothing at slower speeds. Prior of a pass 6%. Gold perps are not tested here (no gold perp tick or minute data on file; Yahoo's GC=F 5 minute history is the one public option and is a separate test).

## Literature note (web search, 2026-10-27): what the published evidence says about Kalshi

Bürgi, Deng and Whelan, "Makers and Takers: The Economics of the Kalshi Prediction Market" (2026; read from the author's PDF, https://www.karlwhelan.com/Papers/Kalshi.pdf), over 300,000 contracts: **average post-fee return Takers -31.46%, Makers -9.64%**; contracts at 10c and under lose over 60%; **contracts above 70c earn small, statistically significant positive post-fee returns**; Makers who buy at 50c and over earn +2.6% on average; the pre-fee average Kalshi contract is -20%. Meaning for this project: the only region with a documented positive return is the high-price favourite (what L1 trades); the cheap-contract region (the owner's 20c to 40c bounce style) is the worst region; and **resting orders (Makers) do about 22 points better than crossing the spread (Takers)**, so how the order is placed matters as much as what is bought. Funding-rate carry (delta-neutral perp against spot) was measured at about 2.8% annualised funding in June to July 2026 and a filtered basket at 6.1% over 181 days (1Token / 1ndex via the search result), against vendor claims of 10% to 40%; realistic net low single digits to about 6% a year. Polymarket within-market and combinatorial arbitrage is documented (arXiv 2508.03474, "a realized estimate of 40 million USD of profit extracted", no time window or persistence in the abstract); cross-venue Kalshi to Polymarket gaps are described only by vendors.

## Pre-registration: MAKER2, enter the L1 favourite with a resting bid instead of crossing the spread (written 2026-10-27 before any resting-bid fill was computed; 2 variants, running count about 21,352)

**Why (from the literature above).** Makers beat Takers by about 22 points on Kalshi. The live L1 bot buys at the ask. If a resting bid at the current bid (about 1c cheaper, and a maker order) filled often enough and was not adversely selected, each trade would keep 1c more of a 6c win.

**Rule.** The L1 entries (the favourite's ask 0.88 to 0.97 with 6 minutes left, all 15 minute series on file with full candles in `book`, `l1b` and `fresh`). Variant TAKE: buy at the ask (the baseline). Variant REST: place a buy at the favourite side's bid at the entry minute; it fills if, within the next 3 minutes, the side's ask low falls to the resting price or below (a conservative proxy: candles carry no trades, and this requires the spread to close on the way down); if not filled, no trade. Both hold to settlement; taker fee on TAKE, **the same fee formula on REST** (conservative; Kalshi's maker fee schedule is not verified here).

**Judging.** Net per filled contract and per opportunity (an unfilled REST counts as 0), day-clustered z, halves. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` only if REST's net per FILLED contract exceeds TAKE's on the same entries by at least +0.5c AND REST's net per opportunity is above TAKE's, with z at least 2.0 for the per-filled difference and both halves positive. Otherwise `FALSIFIED`. Run once.

**Prediction.** FALSIFIED: the fills happen when the price is falling (adverse selection), so the cheaper entries lose more often than the missed ones; MAKER1 on tennis found the same shape. Prior of a pass 15%, higher than usual because the literature supports it.

## Result: MAKER2 (run once on 2026-10-27): FALSIFIED (resting bids beat crossing on the fills they get, and lose on the whole)

28,873 L1 opportunities over 83 days. **TAKE (buy at the ask): +0.10c per contract. REST (resting bid at the bid, filled if the ask low reaches it within 3 minutes): filled 67.3% of the time, net -1.19c per filled contract; the same entries bought at the ask would have earned -2.31c, so resting is +1.11c better on the entries it fills (z +33.3, both halves +1.18 / +1.05c). But per opportunity REST is -0.80c against TAKE's +0.10c**: the 33% it does not fill are the winners (the price never dipped to the bid), the 67% it fills are the dips. That is adverse selection, the same shape as MAKER1 on tennis, and it is the reason a Maker's edge in the literature cannot be copied by simply resting under the ask. The fill proxy is conservative (candles carry no trades; a real resting bid also fills when a taker sells into it without the ask touching it), so the true REST per opportunity is somewhat better than -0.80c, but the sign of the selection effect is not in doubt. Tries: 2, about 21,352. Code `src/scalper/maker2.py`, result `data/maker2_result.txt`.

## Pre-registration: MAKER3, hybrid L1 entry: rest a bid, then cross if it has not filled (written 2026-10-27 before any hybrid fill was computed; 2 variants, running count about 21,354)

Same entries, data and fee as MAKER2. Place a buy at the favourite side's bid at the 6 minute entry. If the side's ask low reaches it within W seconds, it is filled at that bid (maker, same fee formula). If not, cancel and buy at the closing ask of the candle W seconds later, provided that ask is still between 0.88 and 0.97 (otherwise no trade, counted as 0 for that opportunity). Variants W = 60 and 120. Hold to settlement. Judging: net per OPPORTUNITY (the count of no-trade opportunities included as 0) against TAKE (buy at the ask at the entry minute) on the same opportunities, day-clustered difference. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` only if the per-opportunity difference is at least +0.3c with z at least 2.0 in one variant and both halves positive. Otherwise `FALSIFIED`. Run once. **Prediction:** FALSIFIED, difference about zero or negative: the chase leg buys the trades whose bid was not reached, which are the ones that went up, at a higher price (the MAKER1 hybrid result in the equities work had the same shape). Prior of a pass 8%.

## Result: MAKER3 (run once on 2026-10-27): FALSIFIED

28,873 L1 opportunities, 83 days. TAKE +0.101c per opportunity. Hybrid (rest a bid, cross at the later ask if not filled): **W = 60 s -0.458c per opportunity (difference -0.559c, z -10.95), W = 120 s -0.675c (difference -0.776c, z -14.43)**, both halves negative. The chase leg buys the entries that went up, at the higher price, which more than cancels the cheaper fills; every maker-style entry variant for L1 tested here (MAKER2, MAKER3) loses to simply buying at the ask. Tries: 2, about 21,354. Code `src/scalper/maker3.py`, result `data/maker3_result.txt`.

## Pre-registration: THROTTLE1, does sizing down when the recent record is bad help? (written 2026-10-27 after the owner showed the account chart (-$26.25, -5.0% over 1 month) and the bot status (win rate of the last 100 orders 89.0% against 92.0% to break even; edge -3.2c a contract; best market over 7 days Dogecoin +$6.60, worst XRP -$13.97); 3 variants + 200 shuffles, running count about 21,557)

**Question.** The dashboard already shows a trailing edge. Would a hard-coded throttle on that number (half size, or pause, when the trailing edge of the last 100 trades of a series is below a line) have improved the L1 record over the 79 days on file? Per series, in time order, shadow net per contract of every L1 entry (the 6 minute favourite at 0.88 to 0.97, hold); the trailing mean of the previous 100 entries of that series decides the size of the next one. Variants: HALF if trailing mean < 0c; HALF if < -2c; PAUSE if < -3c. Outcomes: total net (size x net per contract summed over all series), the maximum drawdown of the running total in the same units, and net divided by drawdown, against always-on. Null: order of the entries shuffled within each series (200 draws), which keeps the same trades and removes serial dependence; the throttle's change in total and in drawdown is compared with the null's. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` only if a variant raises net divided by drawdown by at least 20% and the change in total is above the null's 95th percentile. Otherwise `FALSIFIED`. Run once. **Prediction:** FALSIFIED on the total (a rule on past outcomes cannot predict iid-like next outcomes), with the drawdown falling about in proportion to the size removed; no improvement in net per drawdown beyond the null. Prior of a pass 10%.

## Result: THROTTLE1 (run once on 2026-10-27): FALSIFIED on the registered bar; the drawdown cut is real but mostly mechanical

31,293 L1 entries over 21 series, 79 days. Always-on: total +5,370 cent-contracts, maximum drawdown 4,942 (net per drawdown 1.09). **HALF when the series' trailing 100-trade mean is below 0c: total +6,690 (change +1,320; the shuffled-order null's 95th percentile of the change is +1,640), drawdown 3,479 (-30%), net per drawdown 1.92 (+77%).** HALF below -2c: total +5,384 (change +14), drawdown 4,754. PAUSE below -3c: total +6,436 (change +1,066; null 95th +2,906), drawdown 4,151, net per drawdown 1.55 (+43%). The registered bar needed the change in total above the null's 95th percentile; none is, so `FALSIFIED`. What does hold: the rule never lost total and cut the worst drawdown by about 30% for the 0c line, which is largely the size removed (halving during bad stretches halves the loss in those stretches) rather than foresight. Used as risk control, not as an edge claim. Tries: 3 + 200 shuffles, about 21,557. Code `src/scalper/throttle1.py`.

## Pre-registration: FLOW1, five order-flow ideas on the underlying market, as filters on the Bitcoin and Ethereum L1 entry (written 2026-10-27 before any Binance flow was joined to an outcome; 32 variants, running count about 21,589)

**New information.** Everything before used Kalshi prices or Kalshi's tape. This uses the signed order flow of the underlying: Binance spot and USD-M perpetual 1 minute klines (public daily and monthly files at data.binance.vision) carry the taker-buy volume next to the total, so the net aggressor flow of each minute is known (net flow = 2 x taker buy - total). Binance's REST API is blocked from here; the static files are not. Bars are stamped by their start; a bar is usable only after it ends.

**Universe.** L1 entries on Bitcoin and Ethereum 15 minute markets (the favourite at 6 minutes left, ask 0.88 to 0.97, hold to settlement, as `feat1.build`), about 9,000 entries over 79 days. Each idea defines a group of entries; the group's net per contract is compared with the REST of the same entries (day-clustered difference), as TAPE20.

**Ideas and variants (32).** (1) Flow toward the favourite: net flow over the last k = 1, 3, 5 minutes divided by the volume, signed toward the favourite (positive = flow supports it); groups top quartile (ALIGNED) and bottom quartile (AGAINST), on spot and perpetual = 12. (2) Delta divergence: the price moved toward the favourite's direction over the last N = 10 or 20 minutes by at least 0.05% while the cumulative net flow over the same minutes was against it (DIV_AGAINST), and the mirror (price against, flow toward, DIV_TOWARD), on spot and perpetual = 8. (3) Point of control: the price with the most volume over the last 60 or 120 minutes (volume by close price in 0.05% buckets, spot); REVERT_AGAINST = the spot is at least 0.2% from the POC and the POC lies on the side opposite to the favourite's direction (a pull away from the favourite), and REVERT_TOWARD the mirror = 4. (4) Opening drive: net flow share in the first 3 minutes of the window (15 to 12 minutes before the close), signed toward the favourite, top and bottom quartile, spot and perpetual = 4. (5) Cross-asset flow: Bitcoin's 3 and 5 minute signed flow share for Ethereum entries and Ethereum's for Bitcoin, ALIGNED and AGAINST (top and bottom quartile), using spot = 4. Total 32. Quartile cuts are computed per asset from the entries' features, with no outcome used.

**Judging (as TAPE20 with a stricter bar for 32 variants).** Discovery = first two thirds of the days, confirmation = last third. `NOT_YET_FALSIFIED` needs for the group, versus the rest: discovery difference at least +2.0c with day-clustered z at least 3.0, confirmation at least +1.0c with z at least 1.0, positive at fees x1.2 in both, at least 150 discovery and 60 confirmation entries. For an AGAINST or DIV_AGAINST or REVERT_AGAINST group the sign flips: the useful finding is that the group loses more (a skip rule), so the difference is taken as rest minus group. `FALSIFIED` if the all-days difference is under +0.5c or z under 1.0. One run, no rerun.

**Prediction.** FALSIFIED for all 32 (at most one passes by chance in a family of 32 at z 3.0, about 4%). The underlying's flow is public and arbitrageurs read it faster than a 6 minute entry; TAPE20 found the Kalshi tape flow worth nothing. Prior that any variant passes both halves 6%.

## Result: FLOW1 (run once on 2026-10-27): FALSIFIED for all 32 variants

4,786 Bitcoin and Ethereum L1 entries over 83 days (not the 9,000 estimated in the pre-registration; the L1 band at 6 minutes leaves about 58 a day across both assets), Binance spot and USD-M perpetual taker-flow klines. **No variant passed.** The few positive discovery numbers do not hold: POC pull-away from the favourite (REVERT_AGAINST, 60 minutes) +3.61c discovery (z +2.62) and **-8.62c** in confirmation; Delta divergence against the favourite on the perpetual (10 minutes) +2.41c then -0.03c; opening-drive flow against the favourite (skip rule) +1.72c then +1.01c (z 0.63, below the bar). Idea 1 (flow toward the favourite in the last 1, 3, 5 minutes, spot and perpetual): the top-quartile ALIGNED groups are negative in 5 of 6 variants (-0.70c to -2.58c all-days; the worst, 3 minute spot, z about -1.8 and -1.9 in the two thirds) and the bottom-quartile AGAINST groups are mixed: when the underlying's flow has already pushed hard toward the favourite, the favourite does a little worse, not better, which points at the favourite being overpriced after a run, but nothing is significant. Idea 5 (the other asset's flow): all four negative. Delta-toward and point-of-control-toward groups had too few entries (0 to 144). Tries: 32 variants, about 21,589. Code `src/scalper/flow1.py` (klines in `data/binance`, not committed).
