## Pre-registration: GEN2, 7,500 more distinct full strategies from new building blocks (owner's order via the main session, 2026-10-29; written before any GEN2 row is built or scored)

**Brainstorm, then the building blocks that are NEW relative to GEN1 and GEN1S** (every GEN2 strategy must use at least one, so none can coincide with a GEN1 or GEN1S strategy in canonical form; the overlap count is reported and is zero by construction):
1. **Series:** all 18 fifteen-minute series on file (Bitcoin, Ethereum, gold plus Dogecoin, XRP, BNB, NEAR, HYPE, Zcash, WTI, silver, natural gas, copper, palladium, platinum, EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY), alone or by family (crypto, metals, energy, FX).
2. **Entry features:** day of week; the window's position in the hour (0 to 3); candle volume against the series' median; the market-wide move (mean YES mid change over 2 minutes of every other series closing at the same time, signed toward the side); a family partner's mid and 2 minute change (crypto: Bitcoin, metals: gold, energy: WTI, FX: EUR/USD); the previous window's result on this side and its last YES price (reference price). GEN1's features stay available.
3. **Exits, all before settlement:** trailing stops (sell when the bid falls 5, 10 or 15c below its best since entry, else at 60, 120 or 240 s left); scale-out (half at +5 or +10c, the rest at 120 or 240 s left); plus GEN1's 216.
4. **Scale-in:** add a second equal entry one minute later if the side's bid has fallen at least 5c (same side only); P&L of both legs.
5. **Pairs (structure, no single-outcome bet):** in one close window, buy one series' side and the partner's opposite side when their 2 minute moves diverge by a quantile threshold, both legs exited by the same exit rule; profit comes from the spread between two correlated contracts closing, not from either outcome.
**Counterparty classes named per family:** slow quoters on thin alt-coin and commodity books (series), late takers after market-wide moves (market move), traders anchoring on the previous window (reference), momentum chasers stopped out by trailing exits (trailing), and dislocations between correlated contracts (pairs).
**Data and split.** Candle files `book`, `l1b`, `fresh`, `alts2`, `alts3`, `alts4`, `e3b` and `search5k` (input hashes in `studies/gen2_input_hashes_2026-10-29.txt`). DISCOVERY = days 1 to 55 of the 83 on file, VALIDATION = days 56 to 83 (to 2026-10-27 23:45 UTC), **HOLDOUT = windows closing from 2026-10-28 00:00 UTC, not on disk now** (fetched with `fresh_update` and read once on or after 2026-11-08 with at least 10 days, frozen survivors only).
**Fills, fees, dedupe, gates:** exactly GEN1's (ask in, closing bid out, zero-volume fill-optimism rule, per-order rounded fee at 10 contracts with 1 contract reported, stress x1.2, Jaccard above 0.5 with exits within one step = same, at least 30 discovery trades; discovery PF 1.5 with 150 trades on 25 days; validation PF 1.5 with 60 trades on 15 days, stress PF 1.2, day-clustered bootstrap 5th percentile above 1, deflated z at the Bonferroni bar for all N tried, about 411,000 + GEN2's generated). Target 7,500 distinct. **Prediction:** at most a few dozen pass discovery, none after deflation; NO_WINNER is the most likely result.

## Pre-registration: GEN3, a strategy generator on the HOURLY Bitcoin ladder (KXBTCD), single-strike scalps and adjacent-strike bracket spreads, all exited before the close (written 2026-10-29 before any GEN3 row is built; target 5,000 distinct)

**Why it is outside the covered families.** A different product (the hourly "above K" ladder, 6 strikes near the money per hourly close, a 60 minute life seen at 1 minute), different shapes (bracket spreads between adjacent strikes, which pay from the spread between two strikes rather than one outcome), and a longer entry horizon (55 to 3 minutes before the close). LAD1 tested an option fair-value rule HELD TO SETTLEMENT on the same file; nothing here holds to settlement. **Counterparty classes:** hourly-ladder takers crossing 1c spreads during spot moves (singles); quoters who move one strike and lag its neighbour (brackets).
**Data and split, fixed now.** `data/lad1.sqlite` (hash in `studies/gen3_input_hash_2026-10-29.txt`): 704 hourly closes, 2026-09-26 to 10-26. Calendar days 1 to 15 = DISCOVERY, days 16 to 23 = VALIDATION, days 24 onward = HOLDOUT; holdout rows are not built until the survivor list is frozen and committed, and are read once.
**Grammar.** Kind: single (one strike, YES or NO) or bracket (YES at strike K and NO at the next strike up, both bought at the ask; both sold at the bid). Entry window [L_hi, L_lo] of seconds left inside 3,300 to 180 (60 s grid, width 60 to 1,800 s); 1 to 4 conditions on: ask (bracket: cost of the pair), bid, spread, side bid change over 1, 2 and 5 minutes, 5 minute range, candle volume, open-interest change, strike distance to spot in sigma units (spot from `search5k`, sigma from the trailing hour), 3 minute spot return and perpetual taker imbalance over 1 and 5 minutes (signed toward the side), ladder slope (YES mid of the strike below minus the strike above), hour of day, day of week; first matching minute enters, one entry per strike per close (bracket: per pair). Exits: take profit {+3, +5, +8, +12, +20c, none} x stop {none, -5, -10, -20c} x time {60, 120, 300, 600 s left} x book {none, spread at least 3c} plus trailing {5, 10, 15c} x time: 204 exits, all before the close.
**Fees, fills, dedupe, gates.** Ask in, closing bid out; per-order rounded fee at 10 contracts on every leg (1 contract reported), stress x1.2; zero-volume rule as GEN1; distinct = Jaccard of (close, strike) entry sets at most 0.5 or exits more than one step apart, at least 30 discovery trades. DISCOVERY: PF 1.5, at least 150 trades on 10 days. VALIDATION: PF 1.5, 60 trades on 6 days, stress PF 1.2, day-clustered bootstrap 5th percentile above 1, deflated z at the Bonferroni bar for all N tried (425,360 + GEN3's generated). HOLDOUT: PF 1.5, 40 trades on 5 days, stress 1.2. Days are fewer than GEN1's, so n is in hourly closes as well as days, and both are reported. **Prediction:** NO_WINNER; at most a few pass discovery.

### Result: GEN3 (2026-10-29): ONE STRATEGY PASSED EVERY REGISTERED GATE, including the frozen holdout. NOT_YET_FALSIFIED; earns a forward paper read only.

Funnel: 13,237 generated, 5,000 distinct (3,298 singles, 1,702 brackets), 21 passed discovery, 2 passed every validation gate including deflation (N tried 438,597, Bonferroni z bar 5.17), survivor list frozen and committed (`studies/gen3_survivors_FROZEN_2026-10-29.json`, sha256 e73c1af9...) BEFORE the holdout was built; holdout (8 days, 165 hourly closes) read once: **1 of 2 passed.**

**GEN3-H1 (the pass).** Market KXBTCD, the 6 strikes nearest the money of each hourly close. Entry: from 3,060 to 2,760 s before the close (51 to 46 minutes), buy the side (YES or NO) whose ask is at most 10c when that side's bid has risen over the last 2 minutes; first match per strike. Exit: sell at the bid when it is at least 3c above the entry price (or when the spread reaches 3c), otherwise at the bid at 60 s before the close; never held to settlement. Profit factor at 10 contracts (1 contract, fees x1.2), trades, closes, days: **discovery 3.48 (n 348, 211 closes, 15 days); validation 2.77 (2.18, 2.62; n 229, 8 days; z +5.66 against the 5.17 bar; bootstrap 5th percentile above 1); HOLDOUT 2.57 (2.04, 2.42; n 178, 109 closes, 8 days; mean +2.54c a trade; z +5.33).**
**GEN3-H2 (failed the holdout):** cheap side at 45 to 33 minutes left with spot and path conditions, target +8c, stop -20c: holdout PF 1.45 (gate 1.5). FAILED_GATE_HOLDOUT_PF.

**Audit (discovery and validation only, before the holdout):** entries median 7c (3c to 10c), YES and NO about equally; 73% to 80% of trades reach the target; hits average +5c to +6c (the bid often jumps past 3c within the minute), misses fall to a 0 bid and lose about 5.5c. Several strikes trade in one close, so the honest n is closes (109 to 211) and days (7 to 15), not trades. **Who pays:** sellers of cheap far strikes early in the hour who do not reprice for the hour's remaining volatility (a 7c contract with 50 minutes left touches 10c more often than its price implies). **Risks stated plainly:** (1) candles carry no sizes, so the depth at 7c to 13c bids is unknown; (2) 16% of holdout trades touch a zero-volume candle (the limit is 20%); (3) one month of one regime (Sep 26 to Oct 26), and LAD1 had read these days with a different, held-to-settlement rule; (4) the hourly ladder is not in the second slot's allowed series and its 51 minute entry is outside the slot's 840 s limit, so the slot cannot run it as built. The forward read below is the test that matters.

## Pre-registration: GEN3-F1, forward paper read of G3H1 on recorded order books (written 2026-10-29 before any recorded book row is read)

**Rule:** G3H1 exactly as frozen (cheap side, ask at most 10c, side bid up over the last 2 minutes, 51 to 46 minutes before the hourly close; sell at entry + 3c or when the spread reaches 3c, else at 60 s left; never held to settlement). **Data:** the QUOTE2B recorder's KXBTCD books (7 strikes nearest the money, depth 5 every 3 s, from 55 minutes before each close), sampled at each minute boundary to match the minute-candle rule; nothing recorded is read before the read date. **Fills, now with depth:** entry only if the displayed size at the ask is at least 10 contracts, at the ask; exit at the best bid only if its displayed size is at least 10, otherwise at the next level down that has 10 (walking the book). Fee: per-order rounded at 10 contracts; stress x1.2. **Read date:** 2026-11-12, or later once at least 150 independent hourly closes with an entry exist. **Kill:** profit factor under 1.5, under 1.0 in either half by date, under 1.2 at fees x1.2, or more than 20% of intended entries without 10 contracts at the ask = FALSIFIED; fewer than 150 closes with an entry = NOT_ENOUGH_DATA. A pass means the owner decides whether to build a slot for it (KXBTCD and a 51 minute entry are outside the current slot registry); nothing else.

### AUDIT FAILURE in GEN3 (found 2026-10-29, after the holdout read): universe look-ahead. G3H1's pass is VOID pending a corrected read.

`data/lad1.sqlite` was built by LAD1, which kept, for each hourly close, only the strikes whose YES mid was between 3c and 97c in the window 35 to 25 minutes BEFORE THE CLOSE (`PROBE_S = (2100, 1500)`). G3H1 enters at 51 to 46 minutes before the close. The universe therefore used information from after the entry: a cheap side bought at 7c whose contract had collapsed below 3c (or whose other side passed 97c) by the 30 minute mark was removed from the file. Those are exactly G3H1's losing trades, so every GEN3 figure on this file, discovery, validation and holdout alike, is biased in the strategy's favour, by an unknown amount. This is the same class of error as the backtest lookaheads recorded at the top of this repository's CLAUDE.md, and it was not caught by the gates because all three windows share it.
**What happens now (no tuning, no new search):** re-fetch the hourly Bitcoin ladder for the same 30 days with the strikes chosen from quotes 55 to 52 minutes before the close (before any G3H1 entry can occur), keeping every strike with a YES mid between 1c and 99c then, and re-read G3H1 and G3H2 exactly as frozen on all three windows (CORR1 below). The original GEN3 verdict line stands in the record as written, with this note; `forward_candidates.json` is relabelled AUDIT_VOID until CORR1 reads.

## Pre-registration: CORR1, G3H1 and G3H2 re-read on a look-ahead-free hourly ladder file (written 2026-10-29 before the new file is fetched)

Fetch KXBTCD settled hourly events of the same 30 days into `data/lad2.sqlite`; for each close keep every strike whose YES mid is between 1c and 99c in the candles 55 to 52 minutes before the close (before any entry time of either rule), and store its candles from 55 minutes to 1 minute before the close. Apply G3H1 and G3H2 exactly as frozen (same features, same exits, same fees, same zero-volume rule), with the same calendar windows (days 1 to 15, 16 to 23, 24 onward). Read once. **Kill (unchanged gates):** in each of the three windows profit factor at least 1.5 with the window's minimum trades and days, stress at least 1.2, and validation z at least 5.17; anything less = FALSIFIED. **Prediction:** profit factor falls in every window; most likely below 1.5, so FALSIFIED.

## Pre-registration: LADL1, L1's own rule on longer clocks (owner's question via the main session, 2026-10-29: "can L1 influence a ladder or hourly strategy"; research only; written before any LADL1 data is fetched; 4 market groups x 2 entry times = 8 tries)

**Rule, exactly as live L1:** buy the side whose ask is 0.88 to 0.97 at 10 minutes and at 6 minutes before the close (two separate entry looks, each its own try), 1 contract, held to settlement, fee 7% x 1 x p x (1-p) rounded up to the cent per order (1 contract, as L1's smallest order; 10 contracts reported too). **Markets:** gold daily ladder KXGOLDD and weekly KXGOLDW (close 21:00 UTC), Bitcoin and Ethereum hourly ladders KXBTCD and KXETHD. **Universe without look-ahead:** for each close, the strikes whose YES mid is 1c to 99c in the candles 30 to 27 minutes before the close (at least 15 minutes before the first entry look); nothing later is used to choose strikes. Note: E4 already tested L1 unchanged on the hourly Bitcoin and Ethereum ladders (FALSIFIED); LADL1 repeats them with the look-ahead-free universe and adds gold's daily and weekly ladders, which are new. **Counterparty:** sellers of the favourite near the close (hedgers, holders of the longshot taking a small loss to free capital); honest alternative: favourites are fairly priced and the fee is the loss. **Data:** public settled history; the recorder's ladder.csv for information only. **Windows:** thirds by close date (discovery, validation, holdout, read once). **Unit:** closes (independent per market group; strikes of one close clustered). **Gates (unchanged bar):** PF at least 1.5 in each window after fees, at least 30 closes per window, positive at fees x1.2, deflated z at the bar for all N tried (about 438,600 + 8); fewer than 30 closes in a window = NOT_ENOUGH_DATA (gold daily has about 22 closes a month, so it is likely NOT_ENOUGH_DATA). **Prediction:** PF 0.9 to 1.2 on every group (favourites priced about fairly; the fee is the cost), FALSIFIED or NOT_ENOUGH_DATA. **Overlap with live L1:** for gold, whether a LADL1 entry at 21:00 UTC closes falls in the same 15 minute window as an L1 gold entry (KXGOLD15M closing 21:00 UTC) and on the same side (same direction of gold), counted and reported.

## Pre-registration: CONF1, confluence across clocks and instruments as a filter on L1's entries (owner via the main session, 2026-10-29: "more confluence"; research only; written before any conjunction is scored; 3 conjunctions = 3 tries)

**Parent:** L1's rule on its history (15 minute series, side priced 88c to 97c at the 6 minute look, held to settlement, 1 contract, per-order rounded fee), the same entries GROW1 and DAYCUT1 used. **Conjunctions, fixed now (no thresholds searched):** (a) LADDER: keep a Bitcoin or Ethereum entry only when the window closes at the top of an hour and the hourly ladder strike nearest the 15 minute strike is also priced 88c or more on the same side at the same minute (data: `lad2.sqlite`, Bitcoin only, 30 days; gold daily only at 21:00 UTC closes from `ladl1.sqlite`); (b) TWIN: keep an entry only when its twin series (Bitcoin with Ethereum, Ethereum with Bitcoin, gold with silver, silver with gold) closing in the same window is also in 88c to 97c on the same side at the same look; (c) TAPE: keep an entry only when the market-wide move (mean YES-mid change over the previous 15 minutes of every other 15 minute series closing in the same window, signed toward the side) is positive. **Report per conjunction, against the unfiltered parent on the same windows:** PF, entries kept, entries removed and the PF and net of the removed ones. **Windows:** thirds by close date of the L1 history; the last third is the holdout, read once after the discovery and validation verdicts are written. Disclosure: the L1 history has been read as a whole many times; only these conjunctions are new. **Gates (unchanged bar):** PF at least 1.5 in each window, positive at fees x1.2, at least 30 independent closes per window, deflated z at the bar for all N tried; a conjunction that only removes trades without lifting PF above 1.5 is FALSIFIED. **Counterparty:** the same as L1's (sellers of the favourite near the close); confluence only claims to pick the windows where they are more wrong. **Prediction:** each filter keeps 20% to 60% of entries and moves PF by less than 0.15; FALSIFIED (or NOT_ENOUGH_DATA for the ladder form).

### Result: CORR1 (run once, 2026-10-29): G3H1 and G3H2 FALSIFIED on the look-ahead-free file; the whole GEN3 family was the look-ahead

`lad2.sqlite`: 704 hourly closes, 9,969 strikes (every strike with a YES mid of 1c to 99c 55 to 52 minutes before the close; LAD1's file had 4,296). **G3H1: PF 0.43 / 0.60 / 0.60** (discovery / validation / holdout; 1 contract 0.32 / 0.45 / 0.45; n 1,212 / 660 / 543; mean -2.14c / -1.34c / -1.34c; 53% to 61% of trades touch a zero-volume candle). **G3H2: 0.77 / 0.83 / 0.59.** The independent re-implementation (AUD1 on `lad2`) agrees: 0.43 / 0.60 / 0.60 with the registered fill, 0.45 / 0.61 / 0.66 with next-candle fills, 0.43 / 0.62 / 0.61 with zero-volume candles dropped or unfillable. **All 21 GEN3 discovery survivors** (regenerated deterministically from the same seed) scored 1.50 to 3.48 on the biased file and **0.27 to 0.83 on the corrected file in every window** (`studies/gen3_family_table_2026-10-29.txt`). GEN3's verdict is therefore NO_WINNER; G3H1 is withdrawn, its forward read GEN3-F1 is cancelled (nothing to test). ## Pre-registration: GOLDFV1, gold's 15 minute market against the COMEX gold future it never had (Strategy Research V2, 2026-10-29; written before any gold future bar is compared with any Kalshi quote or outcome; 4 tries, running count about 438,670)

**Why it is new.** Every gold fair-value idea in this ledger stopped at "there is no free gold spot series here" (L-series, H7, S16 to S26, IV1 Bitcoin only). Gold settles on the 1 minute Pyth GOLD candle close at the close against the one at the open; Pyth's history now answers 401 without a key, so it stays unavailable. Yahoo's public, keyless 1 minute COMEX gold future bars (`GC=F`, last 30 days, `data/gc1m.json`, 28,802 bars, 2026-09-30 15:30 to 10-29 15:18 UTC, fetched 2026-10-29) are the closest outside price. Gold is also the one series where L1 history is positive (6 minute PF 1.20), so an outside price is the cheapest way to ask whether that is pricing lag or luck.

**Model, fixed now.** For a KXGOLD15M market with open time O and close time C, decision time D in {C - 10 min, C - 6 min}. Only future bars whose START is at or before D - 60 s are read (Yahoo stamps a bar with its start). d = close of the last such bar minus close of the bar starting at O - 60 s (the minute ending at the open, which is the minute Pyth's strike candle covers); the basis between the future and spot cancels in the difference. sigma = standard deviation of the 1 minute close-to-close changes of the 60 bars before D (at least 45 present). p_model(YES) = Phi(d / (sigma x sqrt(tau))), tau = minutes from D to C. **Skipped, before any outcome is read:** a missing bar within 2 minutes of O or of D, fewer than 45 sigma bars, any 1 minute future change above 0.5% inside the 60 bars or the window (contract roll or bad print), a missing Kalshi candle ending at D.

**Universe, chosen on close time only:** every settled KXGOLD15M market with a close time from 2026-10-01 00:00 UTC to the last close with future bars (nothing chosen from quotes). Kalshi candles from the restored databases and `data/five.sqlite`.

**Tries (4).** S10 and S6: standalone, at D = 10 and 6 minutes, buy the side whose p_model minus its ask (the closing ask of the Kalshi candle ending at D) is at least 0.05, ask between 0.10 and 0.95, 1 contract, held to settlement. F10 and F6: filter on L1's own gold entries (side with ask 0.88 to 0.97 at D) kept only when p_model of that side is at least its ask; report kept and removed sets.

**Fills and costs.** Primary fill: the closing ask of the candle ending at D (the signal candle; the future bars used end one minute earlier). Conservative check: the closing ask of the next candle. Zero-volume Kalshi candles reported both ways (kept, and treated as unfillable). Fee 7% x C x p x (1-p) rounded up to the cent per order at C = 1 and 10; fees x1.2 check.

**Counterparty.** Kalshi gold quoters who reprice after a COMEX move with a lag (gold has fewer quoters than Bitcoin); the honest alternative is that they quote from the same or a better feed and every gap is noise in this model (basis moves, Pyth versus COMEX, a sigma from 60 minutes).

**Windows and unit.** Thirds by close date (discovery, validation, holdout read once after the first two verdicts are written). Unit: markets (one trade per market per try), with day-clustered z.

**Bar (unchanged).** PF at least 1.5 in each window after fees, at least 30 trades per window, positive at fees x1.2, deflated z at the bar for N about 438,670 (z about 5.17), named counterparty above, independent re-implementation before anything is reported as surviving. A filter only counts if the kept set clears the same bar.

**Prediction.** Kalshi gold tracks the future: S10 and S6 trade rarely and lose (PF under 1.0, the gaps are model error); F10 and F6 move gold's PF by under 0.1. **FALSIFIED** expected. Kill: any try under PF 1.0 in discovery is FALSIFIED without reading the holdout. Thin by construction: about 28 days, so NOT_ENOUGH_DATA if any window has under 30 trades.
Recorder look 2026-10-29 (information only): 132 of 300 trades over 8 of 10 dates, 0% 429, clock_ok still False. Read not yet due.

## Pre-registration: LOCK2H, LOCK2's coincident-close locks looked for in history (Strategy Research V2, 2026-10-29; written before any 15 minute quote is paired with any ladder quote; 1 try, running count about 438,671)

**Why.** LOCK2 (registered above) waits for 25 recorded closes per asset. The corrected hourly Bitcoin ladder `lad2.sqlite` (704 top-of-hour closes, 2026-09-26 to 10-26, strikes chosen 55 to 52 minutes before the close, so no universe look-ahead) and the 15 minute Bitcoin candles (`book.sqlite`, `fresh.sqlite`) already overlap; minute-close quotes can say whether locks exist at all before weeks of recording.

**Rule.** For each top-of-hour close C with both files: the KXBTC15M market closing at C (strike K0, fixed after its first minute), and every ladder strike in `lad2` for C. At every candle end t from C - 14 min to C - 1 min present in both: (a) 15 minute YES at its closing ask plus ladder NO (1 - closing YES bid) at any strike K >= K0; (b) 15 minute NO (1 - closing YES bid) plus ladder YES at its closing ask at any strike K < K0. Either pair pays at least $1 whatever the settlement average. Lock value = 1 - both prices - both fees (7% x C x p x (1-p) rounded up per order), at C = 1 and C = 10 contracts. Quotes of 0.99 or more as an ask, or 0 as a bid, are no quote.

**Counterparty.** The slower of two quoting bots on two books that settle on the same number (as in LOCK2). Honest alternative: the same makers quote both and keep them consistent.

**Caveats fixed now.** Candle closing quotes are the last quote of the minute on each book, not one instant, and carry no size, so a lock here is an upper bound: zero locks FALSIFIES the history version; any lock is NOT_ENOUGH_DATA (only the recorder's simultaneous quotes with sizes, LOCK2, can confirm it). Reported also with both candles having volume above zero.

**Unit and gates.** Independent closes. FALSIFIED if no close has a lock of at least 1.0c per contract at 10 contracts; otherwise NOT_ENOUGH_DATA with the count of closes with a lock, the largest lock, and how many consecutive minutes it lasted. **Prediction:** zero locks at 1.0c (ARB1, ARB2, the ladder snapshot found none); FALSIFIED.

### Result: LOCK2H (run once, 2026-10-29, V2): NOT_ENOUGH_DATA (by the registered rule: some minute-close locks, none confirmable)

704 top-of-hour Bitcoin closes (2026-09-26 to 10-26), every one with pairable minutes. **Closes with a lock of at least 1.0c per contract at 10 contracts: 4 of 704 (0.6%), 5 lock minutes in all; largest 16.8c, median best pair -4.4c (at 1 contract: 3 closes, -5.7c).** Requiring volume on both candles changes nothing. Longest lock: 2 consecutive minutes. Every lock is at a ladder strike within $10 of the 15 minute strike (K0 82,894.82 against 82,899.99, 81,600.38 against 81,599.99, and so on), and 4 of the 5 minutes are 1 to 2 minutes before the close in a fast move (2026-10-20 00:58: the 15 minute YES bid went 0.29 to 0.977 in one minute), where each book's last quote of the minute comes from a different second. One sits 14 minutes before the close (2026-10-24 13:46, 2.8c). Candle quotes carry no size and are not simultaneous, so none can be confirmed. **What it changes:** LOCK2's forward read is worth doing and should look at the strike pair within $10 of K0 in the last 2 minutes, with sizes and timestamps from the recorder; expect very few. Tries +1 (about 438,671). `src/scalper/lock2h.py`, `studies/lock2h_result_2026-10-29.txt`.

Filter: keep the entry when the hourly Bitcoin ladder (KXBTCD) strike nearest the 15 minute market's OWN strike (its stored floor strike; CONF1 used a spot proxy, this is the correction) is priced at least 0.88 on the same side at the same candle (YES ask for a YES entry, 1 - YES bid for a NO entry). An entry with no ladder candle at that minute is undefined (counted and reported, neither kept nor removed).

**Universe without look-ahead.** Ladder strikes are chosen as in CORR1: every strike whose YES mid is 0.01 to 0.99 in the candles 55 to 52 minutes before the close; nothing later chooses a strike. 15 minute markets: every settled KXBTC15M market closing at a top of the hour (chosen by close time only).

C, frozen forward holdout: closes from 2026-10-27 00:00 UTC, read ONCE when C holds at least 30 kept closes (expected within about a week); nothing is tuned between now and then.

**Counterparty.** Two books settling on the same 60 second average: when the ladder near the strike is also confident, the 15 minute favourite is less likely to be a stale quote that a late move breaks; the losers are buyers of the 15 minute longshot who pay for a reversal both books say is unlikely. Honest alternative: the two books are the same information and the filter only trims the sample.

**Bar (unchanged).** Kept set PF at least 1.5 in A and in C, at least 30 kept closes in each, positive at fees x1.2, deflated z at the bar (about 5.17 for N about 438,672; not reachable on these counts, stated in advance: a pass on PF alone earns only a forward paper read and the owner's look). ## Pre-registration: TIMEX1 and DCAP1, the owner's two "time stop" questions for live L1 (owner order via the main session, 2026-10-29; Strategy Research V2; research only, no bot change; written before any of these rules is scored; 20 + 36 = 56 tries, running count about 438,728)

**Common.** L1's history entries as EXIT1 used them (`l1studies.load()`: the 6 minute look, side priced 88c to 97c, 18 series, about 32,499 entries, held to settlement unless a rule sells), windows by close-date thirds. Disclosure: these thirds have been read by EXIT1, EXIT2, REGIME1, DAYCUT1 and others, so no history window is a fresh holdout. A rule that meets its bar earns a forward read once on closes after 2026-10-29 23:59 UTC (fresh candles), nothing more. Fees 7% x C x p x (1-p) rounded up per order, on the entry and on any exit sell.

### TIMEX1: conditional time exits (new shapes only; TIME1, DROP10, DROP20, HALF25 and fixed lines are not re-run)

Sell at the closing bid of the trigger candle (the bought side's bid: YES bid, or 1 - YES ask for NO), else hold to settlement. Rules, fixed now:
- **TX1 late weak 2:** at the candle ending 120 s before the close, sell if the side's bid is at or below 0.70.
- **TX2 late weak 1:** the same at the candle ending 60 s before the close.
- **TX3 late adverse:** at the first candle ending at most 180 s before the close whose side bid is at least 0.15 below the entry price, sell.
- **TX4 own volatility:** line = entry price minus max(0.05, 2 x the mean absolute 1 minute change of the side's mid over the 5 candles ending at the entry candle); sell at the first later candle whose side bid is at or below the line (entries without 5 prior candles hold).
- **TX5 spread keyed:** only entries whose spread at entry (YES ask minus YES bid) is 2c or more: sell at the first later candle whose side bid is at least 0.10 below the entry price; other entries hold.
Groups: gold, Dogecoin, Bitcoin, and the pool of the five live series (gold, Bitcoin, Ethereum, Dogecoin, XRP): 5 rules x 4 groups = 20 tries. **Bars:** (a) the strategy bar, PF at least 1.5 in each third (not expected); (b) "better than hold": PF above hold's on the same entries by at least 0.03 in all three thirds and a day-clustered z of the per-entry difference of at least 2.0 pooled. **Prediction:** no rule meets (b) in any group; holding wins, as in EXIT1 and EXIT2. FALSIFIED.

### DCAP1: daily profit cap and daily loss cap on realised P&L

Day = US Central calendar date of the entry time (close - 360 s). An entry is skipped when that day's REALISED P&L (orders whose close time is at or before the entry time; an order counts only when it settles, at its close) has reached the cap; orders already open still settle and count. Size: one contract per $43 of account, so 11 contracts on a $500 account and 23 on $1,000; caps in dollars as a share of the account. **Rules (9):** profit caps +1%, +2%, +3%; loss caps -2%, -4%, -6%; combined +2% / -4%; SPREAD1 alone (skip entries with spread at entry of 2c or more, as a reference); SPREAD1 plus the combined +2% / -4% cap. **Universes (2):** all 18 series (the owner's 32,499), and the five live series only. **Accounts (2).** 9 x 2 x 2 = 36 tries. **Report per rule:** net, PF, worst day, sum of the worst 5 days, maximum drawdown of the daily equity curve, days the cap triggered, wins given up and losses avoided (count and dollars), per third. **Success definition (fixed now):** worth the owner's consideration only if, in ALL three thirds, it cuts the worst day or the maximum drawdown by at least 20% AND gives up no more than 25% of the third's net (if the third's baseline net is zero or negative: net must not fall). It can never pass the 1.5 bar: it removes trades and adds no edge. **Prediction:** profit caps fail (L1's wins are small and the day's later losses are random, so a profit cap gives up more net than it saves); loss caps cut the worst day mechanically but fail the net condition in at least one third; SPREAD1 plus a cap is the most likely to meet the definition because SPREAD1 alone raised PF in every third (REGIME1).

### Results: TIMEX1 FALSIFIED; DCAP1 caps FALSIFIED, SPREAD1 alone meets the risk definition on all 18 series only (run once each, 2026-10-29, V2)

**TIMEX1** (32,499 entries; PF at 1 contract, thirds). Hold: gold 1.439 / 1.026 / 1.170, Dogecoin 1.294 / 1.263 / 1.147, Bitcoin 1.000 / 1.188 / 0.780, live five 1.194 / 1.112 / 0.975. No rule beats hold by 0.03 in all three thirds in any group and none reaches 1.5. Best looking: Bitcoin TX3 (sell when 15c down with 3 minutes or less left) 1.077 / 1.037 / 0.947, lower than hold in the second third, difference z +1.12. Dogecoin is hurt by every exit (difference z -3.0 to -4.5), the live-five pool by four of five (z -1.6 to -3.6): selling a dip in the last minutes sells positions that mostly recover. Holding stays best, as in EXIT1 and EXIT2.

**DCAP1** (realised P&L at each order's close, midnight Central days, 11 and 23 contracts on $500 and $1,000). **No daily profit cap, loss cap or combination meets the definition in either universe or account.** Live five, $500, thirds: baseline net +$663 / +$453 / +$126 (PF 1.30 / 1.21 / 1.06, worst day -$48 / -$42 / -$60). Profit cap +2%: net +$185 / +$230 / +$114 (gives up 72% and 49% in the first two thirds; worst day unchanged in two). Loss cap -4%: worst day -$34 / -$41 / -$37 (cut 28%, 4%, 38%) but net +$456 / +$261 / +$1 (gives up 31%, 42%, 99%), and the maximum drawdown RISES (49 to 55, 42 to 99, 90 to 167) because stopping after a bad morning also skips the recovery. Combined +2% / -4% gives up 61% to 96% of net. Caveat: history enters every series in every window (about 140 entries a day on the live five), far more than the live bot, so a cap trips earlier in the day here than it would live; the direction of every result (caps give up more net than the risk they save) is the same in all 12 universe, account and third cells. **SPREAD1 alone** (skip entries with a 2c or wider spread): on all 18 series it meets the definition in every third (PF 1.046 / 1.009 / 0.976 to 1.151 / 1.102 / 1.074 at $500, net +$290 / +$63 / -$194 to +$609 / +$519 / +$410, worst day cut 21% to 58%). **On the five live series it does not:** PF 1.296 / 1.206 / 1.056 to 1.280 / 1.203 / 1.055, net lower in every third (-18%, -11%, -4%), worst day cut only in the first third. So REGIME1's spread lift comes from the 13 series the bot does not trade. SPREAD1 plus the combined cap fails (the cap's cost dominates). Tries +56 (running count about 438,728). Files: `src/scalper/tstop1.py`, `studies/timex1_result_2026-10-29.txt`, `studies/dcap1_result_2026-10-29.txt`.

## Pre-registration: MKTTIME1, per-market time-of-day and weekday stand-down rules for L1 (owner request via the main session, 2026-10-29; Strategy Research V2; research only; written before any block is scored per market; 70 tries, running count about 438,904)

**Disclosure.** HOURS2 (12 to 18 UTC, pooled), CAL1 (weekday x 16 series), GOLD1 Part I (best UTC block per series) and REGIME1 (a) 22 to 02 UTC and (b) weekends have read parts of this on the same history. ## Pre-registration: HOUSE1, trade only with the day's profit after a target (owner idea via the main session, 2026-10-29; Strategy Research V2; history only, nothing live; written before any HOUSE1 rule is scored; 12 tries, running count about 439,024)

**Entries and days.** As DCAP1: L1's history entries (`tstop1.load()`), the five live series (gold, Bitcoin, Ethereum, Dogecoin, XRP), close-date thirds, US Central day by entry time, realised P&L counted at each order's close only, orders already open always settle. Normal size: one contract per $43 (11 on $500, 23 on $1,000), fee rounded up per order. **Variants:** (a) stop at T is DCAP1's profit cap (cited, not re-run: profit caps gave up 49% to 72% of net). (b) after the day's realised P&L reaches T, each later entry is sized so that the cost of all open orders entered after T plus the new order is at most the realised P&L above T (contracts = floor(room / price), capped at normal size; under 1 contract skips the entry). (c) after reaching T, keep normal size until the day's realised P&L falls back to T or below, then stop for the day. T in {$10, $15, $25}, accounts $500 and $1,000: 2 x 3 x 2 = 12 tries. **Report per rule and third:** net, PF, worst day, share of negative days, mean day, maximum drawdown of the daily equity curve, days reaching T, and of those the share finishing below T and below 0. **Pass (fixed now, risk-shaping, no counterparty needed):** keep at least 70% of the third's net (if the baseline net is zero or negative: net not lower) AND cut the worst-day loss by at least a third, in all three thirds; else FALSIFIED. It can never pass the 1.5 strategy bar. **Prediction:** (b) and (c) give up more than 30% of net in at least one third (they shrink or stop after good mornings) and barely touch the worst day (worst days rarely reach T first): FALSIFIED. A 20 contract loss is about $18, larger than a $15 cushion, so "never negative after T" will not hold literally; measured.

### Result: HOUSE1 (run once, 2026-10-29, V2): FALSIFIED (12 tries)

Five live series, realised P&L at each close, Central days. Baseline at $500 (11 contracts), thirds: net +$661 / +$545 / +$30, worst day -$48 / -$42 / -$66, negative days 27% / 28% / 52%. **No variant keeps 70% of net AND cuts the worst day by a third in all three thirds; the worst day is unchanged in 10 of 12 rules in the first two thirds,** because the worst days rarely reach T before they go wrong. **(b) "only bet the profit above T"** cuts the share of negative days sharply (27% to 7% to 20%) but keeps only 28% to 80% of net in the two good thirds ($500, T $10 / $15 / $25: 28% and 52%, 49% and 55%, 66% and 80%). In the weak third it does better than the baseline (the baseline nearly lost the whole third), which is the regime, not the rule. **(c) "normal size until back to T"** keeps 65% to 102% in good thirds but loses money in the weak third at T $10 and, at $1,000, at all three T. **How often a day that reached T finished badly (baseline):** at $500 and T $10, 26 / 27 / 24 days reached $10 and 5 / 6 / 11 of them finished below zero; in the weak third, 14 of 24 finished below $10. At $1,000, (b) with T $10 or $15 made the weak third's every day positive (worst +$10, +$15), one cell of 36, and the same rule kept only 14% to 34% of net in the good thirds. Plain answer: it trades a smaller, smoother day for most of the profit; it never protects the worst days. Tries +12 (running count about 439,024). `src/scalper/house1.py`, `studies/house1_result_2026-10-29.txt`.

## Pre-registration: HOUSE2, step the size up after wins and stop for the day after a loss (owner idea via the main session, 2026-10-29; Strategy Research V2; history only, nothing live; written before any HOUSE2 rule is scored; 18 tries, running count about 439,042)

**Entries and days** as HOUSE1 (L1's history entries on the five live series, close-date thirds, Central day by entry time, realised P&L at each order's close; open orders settle). Base size as the owner stated: 13 contracts on $500, 23 on $1,000; add-on cap: extra contracts at most a quarter of base (max 16 and 28). Fee rounded up per order at the order's own size; fees x1.2 reported as stress. **Step-up (3):** S1 +1 contract per settled win of the day; S2 base x 1.25 to the power of the day's settled wins, rounded down; S3 extra contracts = floor(the day's realised profit / entry price), only when that profit is positive. All capped. **Stop (3):** K1 after the day's first settled loss, no new entries; K2 after the second; K3 after a settled loss that leaves the day's realised P&L at or below zero (V2's fixed reading of "a loss that takes the day below its banked profit"). 3 x 3 x 2 accounts = 18 tries. **Report per rule and third:** net and share kept, PF, mean day, worst day, share of negative days, maximum drawdown, share of losses taken at the top rung (at the cap), plus for the baseline the share of days with zero losses and the median number of trades before a day's first loss. **Pass (fixed now):** keep at least 70% of the third's net and cut the worst-day loss by at least a third, in all three thirds; else FALSIFIED. Never a 1.5 strategy pass. **Prediction:** K1 and K3 give up more than 30% of net in at least one third (DCAP1's loss caps gave up 31% to 99%); the step-up puts a large share of the day's single loss at the top rung, so the worst day is not cut; FALSIFIED.

### Result: HOUSE2 (run once, 2026-10-29, V2; registration commit 6afd429, README sha256 5a39a28d12375894...): FALSIFIED (18 tries)

Baseline (five live series, $500 at 13 contracts), thirds: net +$785 / +$648 / +$39, worst day -$56 / -$50 / -$78, negative days 27% / 28% / 48%; days with no loss at all 7% / 3% / 0%; median trades before a day's first loss 10.5 / 11 / 20. **Every rule fails.** Share of net kept ($500; $1,000 is the same within a few points), thirds 1 / 2: stop after the first loss (K1) 2% / 0% with every step-up; stop after the second (K2) -11% to -8% / 48% to 51%; stop when a loss takes the day to zero or below (K3) 24% to 25% / 15%. **Negative days rise, not fall:** K1 60% / 62% / 48%, K3 73% / 83% / 83%, against 27% / 28% / 48%. The single loss lands at the top rung most of the time (K1 at $500: 32 of 41, 27 of 38, 41 of 42 losses at the cap), and stopping right after it locks the day in the red with no trades left to earn it back. The weak third looks better under K1 (net +$79 against +$39, worst day -$17) only because that third was a loss-heavy period. Fees x1.2 change no verdict. Plain answer: L1 makes about 10 wins before its first loss on a typical day; stopping at that loss throws away the rest of the day's wins and keeps the loss. Tries +18 (running count about 439,042). `src/scalper/house2.py`, `studies/house2_result_2026-10-29.txt`.

## Pre-registration: HOUSE3, a cooldown after a loss, then resume (owner's clarification of HOUSE2 via the main session, 2026-10-29; Strategy Research V2; history only; written before any loss timing or cooldown is computed; 40 tries, running count about 439,082)

**Part 1, loss timing (the gate, information, no try).** On L1's history entries for the five live series (as HOUSE1 and HOUSE2): for every settled loss at close time c, the orders ENTERED after c (so a rule could have known of the loss) whose close is within N minutes of c, N in {15, 30, 60, 120, 240}: their loss rate against the unconditional loss rate over all entries; per market and pooled; split (i) any market and (ii) same market. Separately, the same-window co-loss rate: given a loss, the share of other entries in the SAME 15 minute window (entered before the loss was known) that also lost, against their unconditional rate (information: a cooldown cannot touch them). **Rule from the owner, fixed now:** if no conditional loss rate is above the unconditional one by a two-proportion z of at least 2 (pooled live five), a cooldown cannot help, and every Part 2 variant is FALSIFIED by that alone; Part 2 is still run and reported.

**Part 2, cooldown variants.** After a settled loss, pause new entries for N minutes from the loss's close, N in {15, 30, 60, 120, 240}; scope (a) a loss on any market pauses all markets, (b) a loss on a market pauses that market only (V2's fixed reading of the brief's variant (b)); size either base only, or HOUSE2's S1 step-up (+1 contract per settled win since the last cooldown ended, capped at base plus a quarter) reset to base after each cooldown; accounts $500 (13 contracts) and $1,000 (23). 5 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 40 tries. Days, thirds, realised P&L and fees as HOUSE2; fees x1.2 as stress. **Report:** net and share kept, PF, mean day, worst day, negative days, maximum drawdown, entries skipped and their own net. **Pass (fixed now):** at least 70% of net kept and the worst-day loss cut by at least a third in all three thirds, else FALSIFIED. **Prediction:** losses are not clustered across windows (S06 found no next-window dependence), so the conditional loss rate is close to the unconditional one, the cooldown skips entries about as good as the rest, and every variant fails on the worst day: FALSIFIED.

**Part 1, loss timing (live five, 11,802 entries, unconditional loss rate 5.79%).** Entries made after a loss had settled lost LESS often, not more: any market within 15 / 30 / 60 / 120 / 240 minutes 6.21% (z +0.55, n 1,015) / 4.54% (z -2.29) / 4.86% (-2.23) / 4.98% (-2.47) / 5.23% (-2.02); same market 5.56% / 4.51% / 4.51% / 4.34% / 5.23%. ## Pre-registration: BAND2, calibration of L1 by price paid (owner's live table via the main session, 2026-10-29; Strategy Research V2; history only; written before any band is split; 24 cells counted, running count about 439,106)

**How it differs from BAND1.** BAND1 chose a sub-band per market on discovery as a FILTER and was FALSIFIED. BAND2 asks a calibration question: within 88c to 97c, does the realised win rate minus the average price paid depend on the price? Bands fixed now (the owner's): 88-90c, 91-92c, 93-94c, 95-97c (by ask in cents, rounded); groups: gold, Dogecoin, Ethereum, Bitcoin, XRP and the live five pooled: 4 x 6 = 24 cells, counted. Any rule built on it ("skip 91-92c") would be a band filter, BAND1's family, so BAND2 gives no strategy verdict; it reports whether the live pattern (91-92c: 85.2% won against 91.5c paid, 19 losses in 128; 95-97c: 99.5% against 95.9c) exists in L1's history. **Data:** L1's history entries at the 6 minute look (`tstop1.load()`, 32,499 entries; the live five about 11,800), close-date thirds. **Report per cell and third:** n, losses, win rate, average price, win rate minus price (points) with a binomial z, and PF after fees. **Plus**, on the owner's live orders from the report endpoint (aggregates only): the 91-92c band split by market and by entry lead (10m vs 6m). **Reading, fixed now:** the live 91-92c hole is "in history" only if the pooled 91-92c cell is below its price in all three thirds with z at most -2 pooled; otherwise the live hole is read as chance on few orders (as LIVELOSS concluded for 91-94c).

## Pre-registration: SIZE3, size L1 by price paid and expected win rate (owner idea via the main session, 2026-10-29, sent as "SIZE1"; renamed because SIZE1 already names the 2026-10-28 size audit; Strategy Research V2; history only; written before any variant is scored; 17 tries, running count about 439,141)

**Entries:** L1's history at the 6 minute look (`tstop1.load()`), the five live series, held to settlement, close-date thirds t1 / t2 / t3. Base size 13 contracts ($500 account); an order's size = round(13 x multiplier), 0 skips it; fee rounded up per order at its own size; fees x1.2 as stress. Bands fixed: 88-90, 91-92, 93-94, 95-97c. **Anything learned is learned on t1 only** (the train window) and applied unchanged to t2 and t3; t1 is reported but in-sample.
- **(a) band by train edge** (6 tries: each of the five markets and the pooled five): rank the four bands by t1's win rate minus price; multipliers 2x, 1.5x, 1x, 0.5x from best to worst.
- **(b) the owner's live hint, fixed** (6 tries, same groups): 95-97c 2x, 93-94c 1.5x, 91-92c 1x, 88-90c 0.5x. Expected to fail: history has 95-97c as the weakest band (BAND2: +0.8 pts, PF 0.93).
- **(c) shrunk Kelly by market x band** (2 tries, k = 50 and 200): on t1, p_s = c + (p_hat - c) x n / (n + k) per cell (c = the cell's mean price paid); f = (p_s - c) / (1 - c); multiplier = clip(f / f_pool, 0, 2), where f_pool is the same formula on all of t1 pooled; f at or below 0 skips the cell.
- **(d) rolling record** (2 tries, last 20 and last 50 settled orders of the same market, settled before the entry): 1.5x if their win rate is at or above that market's t1 win rate, else 0.5x. Expected no effect (S06, HOUSE3: losses are not followed by losses).
- **(e) spread at entry** (1 try): 1.5x when the spread (YES ask minus YES bid) is 1c or less, 0.5x when 2c or more, else 1x. Time in band and depth are not used: depth is not in the history candles, and time in band was SCAN1's feature.
**Report per variant and third:** net, PF on dollar P&L, worst day, maximum drawdown, the share of net from its largest band and largest market, and the day-clustered z of the daily difference against flat 13 contracts. **Pass (the owner's, fixed now):** net at least 10% above flat AND worst day not worse than flat, in all three thirds, AND the difference's z at the deflated bar (about 5.17 for N about 439,141); else FALSIFIED. A survivor is a forward spec only. **Prediction:** (b) fails in every group; (a) and (c) look good on t1 by construction and fall back on t2 and t3 (BAND1's pattern); (d) changes nothing; (e) repeats SPREAD1: helps off the live five, not on it. All FALSIFIED.
